title: ‘Bruach’ ensemble and Balfolk dance Workshop
description:
Join us at East Clare Community Co-op for a vibrant, joyful evening of music and dance to celebrate Culture Night 2025! This special event honours the rich folk traditions of Europe and invites everyone to come together in a spirit of connection, creativity, and celebration.

The evening features a live performance by ‘Bruach’, an ensemble of talented traditional musicians: Sara Corey (fiddle), Sue Hammond (guitar/vocals), Martin Tully (accordion), and Jonathan Spazzi (flute/guitar), along with dancers and facilitators Ilari Bertuola and Marion Carey. Their lively repertoire includes beloved European dance tunes such as the Circassien, Chapeloise, Scottish, An Dro, and Mazurka — melodies and rhythms that capture the heart and soul of European folk culture.

A highlight of the night will be an engaging Balfolk dance workshop led by the East Clare Balfolk Collective. Ilari and Marion will guide participants through joyful, accessible circle and couple dances, all set to live music from Crack of Dawn. This participatory workshop invites people of all ages and backgrounds to move, connect, and enjoy the shared energy of traditional dance.

Free and open to all, this event embodies the values of Culture Night: inclusion, community spirit, and creative exploration. Come and experience an unforgettable evening celebrating European folk music and dance in the warm, welcoming atmosphere of East Clare Community Co-op.

title: ‘Drawn Together’ Portraits of a Place and its People
description:
To mark Culture Night and a milestone 75th year for St. Joseph’s Secondary School Tulla, students past and present, unveil a curated collection of work exploring the idea of portraiture — not only of people, but of place, memory, and community. Inspired in part by the “Today’s World” strand of the Leaving Certificate Art curriculum, the work reflects how students interpret their surroundings and social realities. Through drawing, painting, and mixed-media responses, the exhibition captures layered identities and lived experiences.

Facilitated and curated by Ce/ART, visitors are invited to drop in between 5 p.m. and 10 p.m. to explore the work and meet the artists. Ce/ART will facilitate this, by liaising with current and past students, taking art for their leaving Cert / with an interest in art and work with them to create portraits of ‘their place’ Tulla – representationally or metaphorically, in a range of 2D drawing media. Selected / nominated students will conduct a live drawing demonstration, (drawing community representatives of varying ages) on the evening which may be recorded in timelapse for sharing post Culture Night and / or posting live snippets on social during the event.

Ce/ART (Co. Clare based Artists/Researchers/Teachers) is a collaborative group of four: Lorraine Callanan, Bairbre Geraghty, Edel Hogan, and Mary Moran. Each member actively balances artistic practice with educational roles, contributing to critical thinking, creativity, and teaching methodologies. Together, exploring interdisciplinary approaches to art, education, and research.

This event will involve;
4 x Ce/ART members.
20 x 2nd level students
3 x 3rd level students
4 x selected sitters from the local community (to have their portrait drawn live on the evening) ranging in age from youth (under 12yrs) to teens to older adults.

title: ‘Giving it a Go’ a fun interactive theatre style workshop
description:
This fun & interactive workshop will be led by Facilitator/ Arts Worker Louise Holian where a theatre style approach meets personal development through games, group, pair and individual tasks.

Louise, hailing from Ballygar has many years of experience in the sectors of Theatre, Youth Work, Community Work, Arts based Facilitation, Health Promotion & general Arts sectors.  Currently studying a Masters in Counselling & Psychotherapy, Louise is interested in how the Arts & Health / Mental Health sectors interlink and she recognizes more of a need for connection and positive fun activities and spaces in our communities as well as wanting to make the arts more accessible for everyone.

 Spaces on this workshop are limited, so get in early and book your place!

Giving it a Go – Have you ever wished you had more confidence? Often our inhibitions, what others think of us and that negative voice in our heads can block our potential or want to be ourselves.  In this workshop you are invited to come along, step out of your comfort zone and into an encouraging, supportive and safe space where trying new things, connecting with others in an easy going, open and fun environment is what it’s all about. There is no getting it wrong, if you give it a try, you’re already winning. Whether you’re a regular visitor to the Arts Centre or you have never done anything on Culture Night or find the whole ‘Arts’ thing a bit intimidating you will be welcome to participate in an equal space and have a laugh while you’re doing it.

title: ‘Soundings’ by Capella Productions
description:
In 1967 Professor Augustine Martin was commissioned by the Department of Education to produce an interm collection of poetry for use in all secondary schools. The book produced was entitled “Soundings” and it was used in Irish schools from 1969 up until 2000. The collection passed through the hands of hundreds of thousands of students over the 30 years. This Culture Night event offers people, who studied the poetry collection in secondary school, the opportunity to read their favourite poems from the collection interspersed by live music from the era.

‘Soundings’ was published by Gill and Macmillan and Longmans Browne and Nolan.  The book, with it’s iconic green and blue cover, featured poems by, among others, Wordsworth, Shakespeare, T.S. Eliot John Milton, Wordsworth, Keats, Emily Dickenson, Yeats, Kavanagh, Dylan Thomas and Austin Clarke. So popular was the book that Gill and MacMillan re-issued it in 2010 and it spent several weeks in the top sellers list. This event celebrates this wonderful and memorable book bringing back memories of school days in chalky classrooms of the 70’s 80’s and 90’s. We will bring together a group of people to read from the collection the poems which inspired them and ones they have carried with them all their lives, interlinked with music from the era. The participants will range in age from their 70’s to their late 30’s. It promises to be a truly memorable event. 

Participants will be asked to select one poem from the collection and one other poem, either from the collection or by another poet to read. Participants will introduce the poem, give some background on the poet and say why they have selected the particular poem. Appropriate music from the 1960’s to the late 1990’s will be performed in between each poetic performance.

title: ‘The Whistling Balladeer’ Breda Cooney – Skibbereen Library
description:
An Afternoon with ‘The Whistling Balladeer’ Breda Cooney


Location: Skibbereen Library

Time: 5:00 – 6:30 PM

 The latest project from Breda Cooney, this is  a unique one hour show blending traditional Irish ballads, storytelling, and the rare art of mouth whistling. From ancient plough tunes to original compositions, The Whistling Balladeer breathes new life into a nearly forgotten tradition that once echoed across Irish fields and festivals. 

More than music, whistling is a language — a form of healing, communication, and connection. With voice, whistle, and guitar, she weaves together Ireland’s musical soul and her own story, inviting audiences on a powerful cultural journey. 

Expect: • Irish tunes from the 1700s & 1800s • Original whistling compositions • Traditional ballads and folklore • Stories of whistling from Ireland and beyond 

Host of the long-running Fishers Cross music session, she’s been singing and whistling all her life — keeping tradition alive, one haunting note at a time. 

Free event | All welcome

title: ‘Beyond Beauty: Taiwan From Above’ | Taiwanese Film Extravaganza
description:
As part of this year’s Culture Night programme, audiences are invited to a screening of ‘Beyond Beauty: Taiwan from Above’, a breathtaking aerial documentary by visionary filmmaker Chi Po-Lin. This extraordinary film soars over Taiwan’s mountains, coastlines, forests, and cities, capturing not only the island’s astonishing natural beauty but also the stark environmental damage caused by human activity.

Chi dedicated years of his life to this monumental project, determined to spark awareness and inspire change. The film became a cultural phenomenon in Taiwan, igniting national conversations about environmental protection and conservation. Tragically, Chi’s life was cut short in 2017 when he died in a helicopter crash while filming its sequel.

Today, his legacy lives on through the Chi Po-Lin Foundation, which continues his mission to use powerful visuals to advocate for the planet. Screening as part of Culture Night, this moving film is both a celebration of the Earth’s beauty and a poignant call to action.

title: ‘Guardians over the city’, by Samir Mahmood
description:
As part of Culture Night 2025, Temple Bar Gallery + Studios presents ‘Guardians over the city’, a public artwork consisting of a series of flags by Samir Mahmood, hoisted along Wellington Quay. They suggest a spiritual, peaceful space within the fusion of cultures and communities of the city. The artist sees the flags as portals for imagination and as guardians of the city. Along the Liffey quays Mahmood’s flags open up a space for mindfulness in an urban landscape. Like the art in the galleries and museums, the flags give a moment to be contemplative and still in the city. 

Samir Mahmood is an artist based in Dublin, born in Pakistan. His art practice explores migration, spirituality and queer identity drawing from Indo-Persian miniature painting.

title: ‘The Boy: A Two-Play Theatrical Event’
description:
Written by Marina Carr and directed by Caitríona McLaughlin, ‘The Boy: A Two-Play Theatrical Event’ brings a contemporary Irish lens to the pain and beauty of Sophocles’ Theban trilogy of Oedipus Rex, Oedipus at Colonus and Antigone.

This is a major world premiere of two new plays which will run back-to-back for the full epic story on Ireland’s national stage this Culture Night.

Play one is called The Boy and is inspired by Oedipus Rex. We meet Oedipus and his family at the height of their powers before things begin to unravel.

Play two is called The God and His Daughter and is inspired by Oedipus at Colonus and Antigone, exploring the consequences that continue into the next generation.

Please note that this event is a two-play theatrical event which will begin at 14:00 and run for approximately 5 hours with multiple intervals.

There are 50 tickets available, which will be allocated through a lottery system. Registration is required (this is not a drop-in event).

This play is suitable for ages 16+. See The Abbey Theatre website for more details. Please see here for more information on planning your journey to the Abbey Theatre and parking options.

title: 30 Plays in 60 Minutes
description:
30 Plays in 60 Minutes is an experimental form of theatre, and the goal, as the name implies, is to perform 30 different plays in 60 minutes. All plays take place in the room, and everything performed is the truth–no characters. Each audience member receives a menu as they walk in. Look on that menu, you will see a list of plays. There are 30 plays. There are 30 numbers hanging above the performers heads. Each number corresponds to a play on the menu. The audience choose the order of the show. Some plays are funny, others serious, others just bizarre. Audience and performers are in this together, and our common enemy is time. We’ll have 60 minutes on the clock. Ready? …

title: 6th Annual ÍOVA Culture Night Exhibition: “I Live Here”
description:
The ÍOVA Photography Collective is proud to present its 6th annual Culture Night exhibition, entitled “I Live Here”: a visual exploration of identity, belonging, and the many ways we shape, and are shaped by, the communities around us.

Launched in 2018, ÍOVA started with casual conversations at John Gunn’s Camera Shop, and has now grown into a dynamic collective of photographers, united by a passion for film, image-making, and storytelling. What began as informal meetups has since become a thriving community of artists with a shared commitment to documenting life in Ireland through fresh and diverse lenses.

“I Live Here” invites over 50 contributing artists to explore how individuals create community and how diversity is vital to a healthy society. From the struggles or comforts within one’s own mind to regarding home life and broader social happenings, it will offer the viewers a ‘reflection of self’ in modern day Ireland. With a blend of raw honesty and emotional intimacy it celebrates the unique perspectives and idiosyncrasies which shape and enrich Ireland today.

title: A DEEP TIME WALK with Artist and Ecologist Rachel Sweeney
description:
Come and join artist and ecologist Rachel Sweeney for a DEEP TIME WALK through Maynooth’s waterways, woodlands and walking routes. The Deep Time Walk is a participatory and fun citizen science approach to exploring earth science. Our planet is over 4.6 billion years old and humans, or homo sapiens, have only been around for less than 200,000 years. Together travel back in time through Maynooth’s geological, astrological and biological timelines, reflecting on how our own carbon footprint is reshaping our bioregion and beyond.


Meet at Maynooth train station main entrance. This is a circular walk that follows the Royal Canal Greenway trail.

Suitable for all ages and abilities. Pathway has wheelchair access.

FACILITATOR

Rachel Sweeney is a DEEP TIME WALK facilitator who has worked in the area of creative arts and climate change for over thirty years. She is currently Creative Collaborator for the Co-Creative Lab project which is a collaboration between Kildare County Council Climate Team and Maynooth University. Rachel enjoys co-creation and collaboration as ways of navigating these complex times that we find ourselves in.

The Co-Creative Lab is a recipient of the Creative Climate Action fund, an initiative from the Creative Ireland Programme. It is funded by the Department of Tourism, Culture, Arts, Gaeltacht, Sport and Media in collaboration with the Department of the Environment, Climate and Communications. The fund supports creative, cultural and artistic projects that build awareness around climate change and empower citizens to make meaningful behavioural transformations.

This is part of Kildare County Council Arts Service, KCC Climate Team and Maynooth University’s Co-Creative Lab project which is supported by Creative Ireland’s Creative Climate Action Ignite Fund.

This house is generally accepted as a design of Edward Lovett Pearce and is perhaps the most palatial residence on Henrietta Street. Come along on Culture Night and experience a glimpse of life in Georgian Dublin.

title: A Huge Ever Growing Pulsating Brain That Rules from the Centre of the Ultraworld
description:
Beyond Skin presents

‘A Huge Ever Growing Pulsating Brain That Rules from the Centre of the Ultraworld’

Culture Night Belfast 19th September. 7.15pm. Black Box.

Electronic music composer Alex Thompson, musician and founder of Beyond Skin, Darren Ferguson will bring together an eclectic group of musicians, poets, whirling dancers, meditation practitioners, a choir and bell ringers to perform an interpretation of The Orb’s 1989 soundscape ‘A Huge Ever Growing Pulsating Brain That Rules from the Centre of the Ultraworld’

The 18-minute performance will feature some vocals and sounds that were sampled on the original track played live. This includes Northern Irish singer and songwriter Claire-Louise McBride singing “Loving You” by Minnie Riperton and the VOYPIC Culture Night Choir singing the sample taken from “Slave to the Rhythm” by Grace Jones. The choir has been specially curated for the performance by the organisation VOYPIC that supports young people in care.

Providing the rhythm to the electronic melodies played on synthesisers by Alex and Darren are percussion maestros Henrique Franco (Brazil) and Slawomir Cichy (Poland). On bass guitar Jan Uhrin (Slovakia).

The participatory element of the performance will also invite members of the audience to participate on hand bells.

Special guests flying in for the event, complimenting the music with poetry, movement and whirling dance are Meala Amin, Mursal Kharoti, Anna Rüya Ayyildiz.

Maela Amin is a visionary artist and art psychotherapist whose work lives at the intersection of creativity, healing, and cultural reclamation. Rooted in embodied and decolonising practice, she reimagines art therapy beyond rigid structures, opening it as a living ceremony, an invitation into the language of the soul. Now liiving in England Meala was born in Northern Ireland to a Pakistani Muslim family. She draws on lineage, mysticism, and her own journeys of belonging to return art to its essence as ceremony.

Mursal Kharoti is an Afghan/British peacebuilder and published poet, with experience in humanitarian diplomacy. Drawing on her background in political communications, psychology and NGO consultancy, she brings a compassionate and strategic approach to community empowerment.  She facilitates art and creative writing workshops as a medium for regional dialogue and individual healing.

Anna Rüya, a captivating whirling dancer, who was born in London to an Irish mother and an Anatolian Alevi father. Her diverse cultural background seamlessly weaves into the rich tapestry of her artistry. With a lifelong inquiry into dance, she found herself drawn to the mesmerising and spiritual practice of spinning. She delved into the intricacies of whirling through the exploration of her ancestry roots.

Her lifework is not just showcases of skill and technique but profound explorations of the whirling dance’s spiritual essence. Prepare to be transported into a realm where dance becomes a language that speaks to the spirit, a meditation that resonates with the soul, and a healing force that transcends the boundaries of time and culture.

“When you read through the elements of this production you can’t help but smile. There is some creative playful humour in the spirit of culture night, but when you delve in you find something beautiful and deeper. A healing, connectivity, a breath of release for our human spirit. Bringing all these amazing people together in one space will also plant seeds for future collaborations, and that is truly exciting.” Darren Ferguson

Combining painting, photography, storytelling, and object-based installation, it gathers fragments of lived experience to reveal an Éire that is intimate, layered, and constantly evolving. title: A Presentation On The Vernacular Wrought Iron Farm Gate Heritage Of The Irish Landscape
description:
With a particular reference to surveyed gates in the Castlecomer, Thomastown and Inistioge areas the presentation will focus on local gate design and explore their cultural and social significance.

Shem Caulfield works as an artist and heritage consultant and since 2002 has surveyed and recorded vernacular farm gates throughout many parts of Ireland since 2003. His focus over the past twenty years has been on the Irish landscape and he will present photographs, drawings, writings in an attempt to bring to light the social, economic, cultural and political narratives that the Irish landscape holds.

The vernacular wrought iron farm gate offers a cultural totem through which this rich and complex story can emerge. Shem will showcase the vast archive of material he has accumulated on his extensive travels throughout the island of Ireland.

title: Abbey Church (Findlater’s): Celebrating 160 Years at Parnell Square
description:
Step inside one of Dublin’s architectural gems this Culture Night as Abbey Presbyterian Church marks 160 years in Parnell Square and celebrates the full restoration of its iconic spire.

From 17:00, visitors are invited to explore the building at their own pace with self-guided tours, browse a second-hand book sale, and take part in a fun treasure hunt for children — all within the beautiful surroundings of this historic church.

At 19:00, join historian Peter J. Clarke for a special talk: “Alexander Strain, Builder: His Life and Times.” Learn about the legacy of Alexander Strain, who arrived in Dublin in the early 1890s and went on to build some of the city’s finest homes. Known as a modest and charitable man, Strain played a vital role in the life of the city, serving as Chairman of Drumcondra Hospital, Governor of the Adelaide Hospital, and Trustee of Abbey Presbyterian Church. He passed away in 1943 at his home in Glasnevin, remembered as “an inspiration to us all.”

All are welcome for an evening of history, heritage, and community in one of Dublin’s most storied buildings.

title: After Light: These Dark Citizens
description:
Another night. 

So many, so few. But another. 

This ache to be something, 

the lumen of my soul visible in the evenings’ risen gloom. 

I am light, I am a light. 

Unseen in the daytime.

After Light: These Dark Citizens by Peter Power (Sparsile Collective) is a city wide interactive story that unfolds as the night falls on the Liberties and surrounds of Dublin 8.

Using state of the art audio design technology the audience is allowed to wander freely around the city centre experiencing the stories and events of unseen citizenry and the shadowy stories hidden in the streets, the river, the architecture and the night. 

 

This interactive work is a meditation on the tensions of urban living, of decay and development, of community and story,  of unseen things and unfelt emotions, of architecture and archetype, the rise of the night and the presence of story in not only words but felt experiences.

Using a free smart phone software called Echoes.xyz (available on iPhone and Android) and requiring audience members to bring their own headphones, this work allows the audience to choose the parts of the city they wish to explore and encounter hidden art work on their own unique walk. 

Download the app on Apple Store or Google Play. Once downloaded, open and search for “After Light: These Dark Citizens Dublin” after September 16th. 

Meeting point: The Digital Hub, Roe Lane, Dublin

Area of event: Liberties + surrounds of Dublin 8

Staff will be on hand to assist the public from The Digital Hub from 7 p.m. and the event from 9 p.m. through 12 p.m. The duration of the walk is at participants’ own pace. It is not a linear walk as such, rather a spread of interchangeable walks all across the Liberties and Dublin 8. The guided walk of particular areas will have a duration of around 50-60 minutes. 

Group walks will take place at:

9.30 p.m.
10.30 p.m.
11.30 p.m.

After Light: These Dark Citizens will remain available to the public for a month after Culture Night, and is possible to do at any time of the day if the Culture Night event is missed. 

Proudly funded by the Arts Council’s Culture Night Late Fund and Dublin City Council. Also supported by The Digital Hub and Beta Festival Ireland. Technology powered by Echoes.xyz

title: All Belfast’s a Stage
description:
Join Alternative Ulstours’ Andrew Johnston on a walking tour of historic Belfast theatre sites, in a dramatic programme spanning nearly three centuries.
First Tour: 6pm- 7pm
Second Tour: 7.30pm-8.30pm

Let us set the scene and recite the script, and applaud the larger-than-life characters, both on stage and ‘behind the curtain’.

• Music hall memories of Belfast’s original Empire

• The modest, formative theatre on Ann Street

• Shakespeare and ‘strollers’ in a lost tavern cellar

• Three incarnations of Belfast’s ‘Royal’ auditorium

• Belfast’s first public hall, where drama unfolded

• Noble patronage of Millfield’s prestigious playhouse

• Smithfield theatres on the wrong side of the law

• On ‘Rosemary Lean’, the pride of Belfast’s impresario

• Triumph and disaster at Belfast’s rowdiest venue!

Please note:

• The walking tour starts at the Jaffe Memorial Fountain on Victoria Square in Belfast city centre, where your guide will be waiting for you

• The route is fully accessible, but please inform us in advance of any mobility issues

• The tour ends at the Deer’s Head on Lower Garfield Street in Belfast city centre

• The tour will go ahead in all weathers, so please dress accordingly and stay hydrated

• There are public toilets near the start and end points

• Well-behaved dogs are welcome on the tour

• Your guide is a Level 4 ‘blue badge’ tour guide and Visit Belfast industry partner

• The tour is fully insured through Tour Guides NI

title: Alliance Française de Cork: French Film Screening

Directed by Marie-Castille Mention-Schaar, 2022
In French with English subtitles

Join a free screening of the powerful French film Divertimento, based on the inspiring true story of Zahia Ziouani, one of the few renowned female orchestra conductors.

Synopsis:
At just 17, Zahia dreams of becoming a conductor—a role rarely held by women—while growing up in an underprivileged suburb of Paris. Alongside her twin sister Fettouma, a talented cellist, the two face significant social and cultural barriers when they enter an elite Paris music school. Determined to make classical music accessible to all, Zahia takes matters into her own hands and forms her own orchestra: Divertimento.

A moving, triumphant story of perseverance, passion, and breaking boundaries in the world of classical music.

In this 45-minute session, participants will create small, abstract artworks using chemigram and lumen processes, combining light-sensitive paper, natural developers (like coffee and plant infusions), and resists such as cream, honey, and oil.

This workshop introduces the magic of image-making without a camera blending art, science, and experimentation. Each participant will leave with their own one-of-a-kind artwork and a deeper understanding of how nature and process can shape creative expression.

Suitable for teens (ages 13–17). All materials provided. No experience needed, just curiosity! This event is free. Booking is required

title: An Ciúnas / The Silence Gallery Tour & Late Opening
description:
For Culture Night, Wexford Arts Centre are pleased to present a late opening and gallery tour of An Ciúnas / The Silence, a solo exhibition by artist Marianne Keating curated by Miguel Amado.
Gallery talk: Friday 19 th September, 6.30pm – 7pm
Late opening hours: 5pm-9pm

Marianne Keating is a London-based Irish artist and researcher whose practice examines intersecting and overlooked narratives of Irish emigration to the Caribbean, particularly Jamaica, where the Irish
were recruited as a new labour force after the abolition of enslavement. Keating’s multidisciplinary film installations that combine a range of archival materials, found footage, newly shot footage, text, and
sound.

An Ciúnas / The Silence traces multiple trajectories of migration from Ireland to both Jamaica and Britain from the period preceding the Great Famine of 1845–52 to the present day. It identifies catalytic
moments in the history of the British Empire through the lenses of Ireland and Jamaica to illuminate how events from the past inform current politics and society. The work establishes a radical account of
Ireland’s and Jamaica’s fights for self-determination, the social conditions of Ireland in the nineteenth century and today, the evolution of the Jamaican political system, and the power structures at play in
both countries before and after independence.
The gallery tour is free but booking is essential. To book a place please contact Wexford Arts Centre
on 053 9123764 or log on to www.wexfordartscentre.ie.

title: An Evening with Eleanor McEvoy
description:
An evening of music and stories with Eleanor McEvoy.

After captivating audiences across the UK, Australia, Germany, and beyond in 2024, Eleanor McEvoy returns to Ireland for a much-anticipated tour that promises a spellbinding evening of music, storytelling, and raw emotion in 2025. With an intimate, almost theatrical presence, McEvoy takes audiences on a journey through her acclaimed catalogue—songs of love, loss, resilience, and hope.

The creator of “A Woman’s Heart”, Ireland’s most beloved folk anthem, McEvoy continues to mesmerize fans with her powerful lyrics and soaring melodies. From heartfelt ballads like “Sophie”, a song that has touched thousands struggling with anorexia, to the evocative storytelling of “South Anne Street”, she brings a deep emotional honesty to every performance.

This tour showcases new material from her upcoming release alongside McEvoy’s signature blend of sharp lyricism, warm humour, and deeply moving songs. Whether reinterpreting classics or unveiling new material, she effortlessly bridges the personal and universal, making every performance feel like an intimate conversation. This is an opportunity to witness one of Ireland’s finest songwriters in an intimate live setting.

Join award-winning sean-nós singer and highly regarded teacher Sorcha de Róiste for a unique workshop celebrating traditional Irish song. Hailing from Glanmire, Cork, Sorcha is deeply rooted in the Munster style of sean-nós singing — an expressive and highly ornamented form of unaccompanied Irish singing.

With a wealth of experience as both performer and educator, she has collaborated with notable figures such as composer Linda Buckley and Eoin ‘Stan’ O’Sullivan, a renowned fiddle player from the Sliabh Luachra tradition.

Amhráin na Mara

title: ART IN THE OPEN: EXPLORE ROSCOMMON THROUGH PUBLIC ART
description:
Culture Night Trail of Roscommon’s creative footprint, a park and town tour celebrating Artists, Place and Nature.

Join a curated route featuring a collection of innovative temporary and permanent public artworks. Begin at Áras an Chontae, with the exhibition launch of Honor FitzGerald’s “See, Saw – A Journey Through Nature” a painting collection that invites viewers into the quiet world of the garden.

Continue reflecting on our relationship with the natural word in the grassy surroundings of Loughnaneane Park. A special limited-edition event by up-and-coming local artists, discover four new interactive installations which animate, respond and illuminate the park space. They bring a fresh perspective to the landscape and showcase the evolving artistic voice of the next generation. The guided trail includes an opportunity to Meet the Artists; Christina Carty, Helen Duncan, Maria Mollohan and Nickie Harrington, and hear directly about their concepts. These temporary artworks will be in situ in the park for the WEEKEND ONLY.

Continue into the town centre and roam through Roscommon Town’s permanent installations in the Living Laneways series. Continuing the connection with nature, appreciate our buzzing pollinators through the colourful corridor of The Bee Lane by Graham Reid. From there, make your way to the town’s centre to encounter a landmark bronze sculpture, the vivid blue twine Held Together by Simon Carmen and Dr. Helen Sharp. An eye-catching, photo opportunity that celebrates Roscommon’s rural and creative identity. Following the footsteps of generations before, connect with place at the Mosaic Laneway by Chris Judge and Triskell Designs which celebrates local history, characters and Roscommon’s mosaic tradition and industry. We end our journey at the Poetry Laneway, curated by poet Dani Gill, where site-specific poetry lights the laneway walls and echoes the immense history of the lane. Carry on in your Culture Night tour with our vast evening programme of events.

Whether you’re a visitor or a local rediscovering the town, this unique trial offers a FREE opportunity to find out more about Roscommon’s Public Art. Perfect for families, art and nature lovers, and explorers of all ages.

title: Artist Talk & Film Screening – Bryan Gerard Duffy with Mohamed Sleiman Labat
description: Interface Inagh presents an artist talk and documentary film screenings by Bryan Gerard Duffy and Mohamed Sleiman Labat. DESERT PHOSfate (58mins) is an experimental documentary film by Labat. It weaves through the story of phosphate, exploring the multi-layered narrations about connections to land, sand particles, plants, human and mineral displacement. The film explores ways of telling about realities, metaphors and poetics in the desert. It highlights connections between ecological justice, colonial practices, environmental violence, traces of anthropocentric mineral extractions, and the loss of indigenous ways of knowing and telling about the world. Delivery (16.41 minutes) is a short documentary by Duffy about Morocco’s brutal occupation of Western Sahara, the exploitation of its natural resources, and the struggle for Sahrawi freedom. Mohamed Sleiman Labat is a visual artist, filmmaker, and writer, born and raised in the Sahrawi refugee camps in southwest Algeria. Mohamed’s work explores the multifaceted political, environmental, and social issues that affect his local community in the Hamada desert and the world at large. He is the founder of Motif Art Studio: a small, community art space constructed entirely from discarded materials, a response to the destructive floods that struck the camps in 2015. Mohamed has received numerous awards and his work has been exhibited internationally. Bryan Gerard Duffy is a multi-disciplinary artist working in paint, sculpture, lens-based work, moving image and installation. Exhibitions include shows in the Courtyard Gallery at the National Museum of Ireland, Country Life, Ballina Arts Centre, GOMA, Waterford, and the Custom House Studios and Gallery, Westport.

title: Aye Walled Garden: Finding Beautiful
description:
Finding Beautiful — A Poetry & Art Experience by Addicted Beautiful (Michael Droney)

‘Finding Beautiful’ is a powerful multimedia experience that explores addiction, trauma, recovery, and hope through raw poetry, striking visuals, and original music. The exhibition features a blend of older poems with hand-crafted, emotionally intense designs alongside newer works with fresh beats and contemporary visuals. Each piece is displayed inside vintage analog TV sets housing tablets that play curated Instagram poetry reels, merging nostalgia with modern digital storytelling.

The online aspect of this exhibition allows visitors scan QR codes on every artwork to listen to Addicted Beautiful’s voice layered with music via headphones, creating a deeply personal and immersive experience. The evening culminates in a live reading where the artist brings the poems off the page, delivering an unfiltered and intimate performance.

This event is more than art—it’s a lifeline, breaking silence and sharing stories of struggle and resilience. It invites audiences to connect, reflect, and find hope amid hardship.

title: Baroque around the Clock
description:
Visit St Finian’s Church this Culture Night for a special, peaceful evening of live music from a variety of choirs, talented soloists and spectacular music groups.

The music tradition in the Lutheran Church is rich and deeply rooted in the Reformation era. Martin Luther emphasized the importance of music in worship, stating that “next to the Word of God, music deserves the highest praise”. In particular, Johann Sebastian Bach contributed significantly to the Lutheran musical tradition, composing numerous chorales and cantatas that continue to be celebrated today.

Music in the Lutheran tradition reflects a strong commitment to engaging everyone in a communal and participatory experience. There are numerous wonderful choirs, music groups and highly talented individuals active in the St Finian’s space who will present a memorable relaxing non-stop musical experience for all visitors.

title: BEEHIVE THEATRE presents “The Vagina Monologues” by Eve Ensler
description:
Beehive’s slighted adapted version of “THE VAGINA MONOLOGUES” by Eve Ensler was one of the best pieces of theatre I’ve ever seen. A tour de force! I laughed, I cried. The stark stage, the intimate setting, authentic costumes, atmospheric music and makeup transported you into the world of the characters. The acting by these 10 women was brilliant. You could see every emotion portrayed in their facial expressions, their body movements and especially the voice; ranging from the bass growl of anger to the soprano pitch of ecstasy. I was brought to a place I have rarely been in theatre where a hidden world was opened up to us (literally). The director Wendela Rosenberg Polak is a wonder at spotting such local talent and directing it so skillfully. She was very brave in choosing this script and judged our need for it perfectly. Both men and women tumbled out of the show in a state of emotional excitement and transformation. Bravo! Obviously took great courage and hard work to put this on. I hope it will be on again as I would definitely love to see it again! – Orna Dunleavy

Booking is essential by text only to 087 7946279

Throughout the evening, you’ll be immersed in a global feast for the senses. Sample delicious food from around the world, showcasing the unique flavours and culinary traditions of our residents. The air will be filled with the sounds of music that will transport you to different corners of the globe.

Our residents will also be proudly displaying their heritage through vibrant traditional dress, sharing the stories and significance behind their beautiful garments. Additionally, you’ll have a chance to admire unique art and crafts, from intricate hand-woven textiles to beautiful paintings that reflect the artists’ journeys and cultures. Positioning tactile encounters with the material world at the centre of this inquiry, the exhibition explores a sense of networked and interconnected resonances across time and space, situated beyond, beneath and beside the riverbank.

title: Bloomsday Belles
description:
Join us for Bloomsday Belles, a performance featuring original music and song inspired by the female characters in James Joyce’s Ulysses. Composed by critically acclaimed musician Emer Kenny and commissioned for Bloomsday 2025, the performance features original musical compositions alongside excerpts from Ulysses by James Joyce, a seminal modern novel that chronicles a single day in the lives of Dubliners Molly and Leopold Bloom. The Bloomsday Belles performance features readings by spoken word poet Mikey Cullen, live Spanish music from the period representing Molly’s youth and heritage, performed by award-winning concert harpist Rosie Murphy, and interpretation of the text by the brilliant Ukrainian contemporary dancer, Polina Skarha.
Together, they breathe life into Joyce’s text in a bold, multi-disciplinary work that blends themes of love, loss, and identity.  Clock chimes and bells feature throughout the work as Molly and Leopold Bloom’s lives are punctuated by the church bells chiming ‘Heigh Ho’, symbolising the relentless passing of time and the briefness of youth and beauty. The performance also showcases excerpts from Donizetti’s opera ‘Lucia Di Lammermoor and De Falla’s Spanish Dance.
*There will also be a later performance at 8pm taking place at an Tain Arts Centre, https://www.antain.ie/event/culture-night-2025-bloomsday-belles/

title: Blue Skies by Purple Door
description:

In ‘Blue Skies’, sound, silence, and movement come together to explore our evolving relationship with the planet – and with one another. Co-written and performed by Sinéad, a performer from Purple Door led by Kasia Eliasz, this piece invites audiences into a space of calm awareness, where climate grief and compassion gently meet.

‘Blue Skies’ offers a pause – a moment to sit with change, to feel with tenderness, and to imagine how small acts of care might ripple outward. It is not a call to urgency, but to presence. To stillness. To the radical possibility of gentleness.

Developed through inclusive, collaborative practice, this performance centres lived experience – celebrating Sinéad’s unique voice as both performer and co-creator.

title: Border Memories – Film
description:
Border Memories, is a visual elegy of a life lived on the border at a certain time in history. With a dreamlike aesthetic, it paints a picture of life on the border in the 50’s and 60’s before the crushing conflict of the troubles changed the landscape and the attitudes of the people forever.

Sinéad Murphy grew up during one of the most turbulent periods in the Northern Irish Border. She wanted to understand life before then and decided to make a film about some of the stories she’d heard as a child. Border Memories is a gentle snapshot of a way of life. A time that could be forgotten, a hard working farm life and ordinary life but also a magical one. From milking the cows to digging potatoes, and chasing faeries, it is a world seen through the eyes of the Murphy family living on the border at that time.

Sinéad Murphy was one of An Táin Arts Centre’s Artists in Residence 2025.

title: Boy to Man – A Black History Month Event
description:
Disrupting Dublin Artists, a collective of BIPOC creators, is breaking new ground in Ireland’s cultural scene. This October, they will host Ireland’s first official Black History Month in partnership with the Civic Theatre. As a prelude, their Culture Night offering will be an evocative spoken word and storytelling event titled “Boy to Man,” staged inside a working barbershop.

Barbershops have long held deep cultural significance in the Black community, not only as places for haircuts and braiding but as hubs for conversation, connection, and shared experience. Throughout the evening, BIPOC men from across Ireland will perform original works inspired by the theme, while the rhythms of the barbershop continue around them.

This unique event seeks to centre the voices and stories of Black men in Ireland, foster greater BIPOC engagement with Irish theatre, and spark dialogue ahead of October’s historic Black History Month celebrations. Culture Night’s spirit of inclusivity makes it the perfect stage for this bold beginning.

description:
Brian Cleary, RCSI Honorary Professor and Pharmacy Executive Manager at the Rotunda Hospital, will present Gibbet Hill, the story of his extraordinary discovery of a long-lost short story by Bram Stoker, author of Dracula and brother of William Thornley Stoker, former RCSI Professor of Anatomy and President.

Brian’s journey began in 2021, when sudden hearing loss led to cochlear implant surgery. While retraining his hearing, he visited the National Library of Ireland to explore his passion for historical literature and uncovered this hidden gem.

Before his death, Stoker had planned three short story collections. Only one appeared, published posthumously by his wife; Brian believes Gibbet Hill was intended for one of the others.

The find led to a unique book launched in October 2024, with proceeds supporting the Charlotte Stoker Fund for research into preventable deafness in newborns.

Joining Brian for the evening’s panel are Paul Murray, Stoker’s pre-eminent biographer, and acclaimed visual artist Paul McKinley, who will share insights into their contributions to the book.

The talk begins at 18:00. RCSI look forward to welcoming visitors to their home on York Street this Culture Night.

title: Bus Tours of Dublin Port with Port Heritage Director Lar Joye
description:
Step aboard for a special Culture Night edition of our behind-the-scenes bus tour through Dublin Port, led by Port Heritage Director Lar Joye. This unique evening tour offers rare insight into Ireland’s busiest working port, which handles over €165 billion worth of freight and 1.6 million passengers each year.

Departing from EPIC The Irish Emigration Museum in the historic Stack A warehouse, the journey begins through Dublin’s Docklands before entering the Port’s North Estate. Visitors will gain exclusive access to Ocean Pier, with highlights including the Oil Zone, Ro-Ro and Lo-Lo terminals, the MP2 development, and the ferry lanes—revealing the scale of modern logistics.

The tour pauses at the Tolka Estuary Greenway, Dublin Port’s newest public amenity, where landscaped paths meet working infrastructure.

The final stop is The Substation, restored and reopened in 2023 as Dublin Port’s cultural hub. Here, visitors will see where part of the city’s original 1728 sea wall was uncovered beneath the building, once enclosing the reclaimed land of the North Lotts and giving the East Wall its name.

IMPORTANT NOTE:

Tickets are free but must be won through a raffle. To take part, please enter via the link provided. Winners will be notified in advance.

title: Carbon and Oak Gall Inks – Writing Inks of Medieval Manuscript Traditions from Egypt, Ireland and the Middle East.
description:
Taking our inspiration from writing inks used throughout medieval manuscript production, we will make our own carbon based black inks – the first writing ink used, alongside a demonstration of a variety of historical writing inks – soot, lamp black, bone black and ivory black along with modern day iterations on these sometimes antiquated approaches.

When we have bottled our ink, Annie will demonstrate the process and alchemy of Oak Gall ink – the successor to carbon inks. This is a fascinating foray into the life cycle of the wasps who are responsible for the formation of these tannin rich growths, the science behind its development and movement of this ink technology around the world.

Each participant will go home with a bottle of ink they make on Culture Night, PDF handout with all required information and a new admiration of oak gall wasps, and oak gall ink!

title: Casino Marino Guided Tours
description:
The Casino is a remarkable building known for its unique architecture and interesting history. Sir William Chambers designed it in the late 18th century as a garden temple for James Caulfeild, the 1st Earl of Charlemont, next to his residence, Marino House, in a then rural area. It is a leading example of neo-classical architecture and is regarded as one of the finest buildings of that style in Europe.

Join the Casino’s knowledgeable guides for a tour this Culture Night, where you can learn about the unique design and history of this hidden treasure.

During Culture Night, guided tours will take place at 16:00, 17:00,. 18:00 and 19:00. 

Tickets for the tours must be booked in advance through Eventbrite.

Children must be supervised at all times.

title: Celebrate the Launch of SparkNet Art Hub & Gallery
description:
As part of Culture Night 2025, SparkNet will officially launch its brand-new Art Hub & Gallery on Anne Street South, Dublin 2. Visitors are invited to celebrate this exciting new space with an evening of art, live music, refreshments, and the chance to meet the artists in person.

The gallery is designed as a welcoming home for creativity, collaboration, and community—combining art education with a showcase space for both established and emerging artists. It aims to be a place where people can create, view, and buy art, while engaging directly with Dublin’s vibrant cultural scene.

After months of renovation and preparation, SparkNet is ready to open its doors. On Friday, 19th of September, the public is warmly invited to explore the gallery, join the celebration, and be part of the very beginning of SparkNet’s artistic journey.

title: Celebrating 120 Years of Rotary International
description:
Formed 120 years ago, Rotary International is a non-religious and non-political organisation formed to provide service to others, promote integrity, advance world understanding, goodwill, and peace through the fellowship of business, professional, and community leaders. Current membership is approximately 1.4 million worldwide and some former Rotarians included Neil Armstrong, Pope Francis, Thomas Edison, Franklin D Roosevelt and Walt Disney. 

Rotary Club, Dublin invites you to join them this Culture Night in the Grand Canal Hotel to meet a “Rotarian”, in person, and learn about the wonderful work that Rotary Club members undertake nowadays both in Dublin and internationally. The Rotary Club, Dublin is based at the Grand Canal Hotel in Dublin 4 where members meet weekly. On this their inaugural Culture Night Rotary Club, Dublin have invited a local historian to join them through the evening to provide historical highlights about the Grand Canal Hotel and surrounding environs.

title: Celebrating culture every day, every step of the way | We Act together at NCI
description:
On Culture Night, the National College of Ireland (NCI) invites visitors to its Mayor Square campus to explore a vibrant evening of STEM, wellness, and learning through play. Activities will be hosted by NCI’s Early Learning Initiative (ELI), alongside the Schools of Computing, Business and Social Sciences, as well as local community groups.

A highlight of the evening is ELI’s PlayLab and Sanctuary Space: a dedicated indoor play and therapeutic area for children aged 0-6. This space supports ELI’s ongoing work to help make Dublin’s Inner City a safer, more vibrant place for families to live and thrive.

Home to a diverse community of learners, NCI is proud to showcase the talents and passions of its students, staff, and community partners this Culture Night.

description: We provide Latin-American background music or disco before and after the main live band. The band is a five-piece with two singers. It focuses on hugely popular South American songs and tunes and some lesser-known ones, in Spanish and/or English. The band has a surprisingly large Latin community following in Ennis and the focus is on people dancing. We bring with us many really good dancers. title: Celebrating Limerick through Sport, Song and Fireworks!
description:
Origami Jerseys, Sports Songs, Tunes on the Tin Whistle, Poetry and some Organ Fireworks will reverberate the walls and sacred space of St. John’s Cathedral Choir, as Croom NS Choir, together with their teacher, Pádraig Wallace, Assistant Organist at St. John’s Cathedral perform a suite of songs, hymns and variations celebrating music, both sacred and secular through various media. Members of the audience will get their fine motor skills ignited through creating jerseys of their favourite sports teams and players with paper using Origami. Opportunities to listen and respond to organ music through art, LEGO building, dance and movement will also be available to audience members as they experience responding to music using various methodologies as would happen in the primary school classroom.
We are really looking forward to sharing our love of the arts with the audience for this amazing opportunity participating in Culture Night 2025 at St. John’s Cathedral.

title: Celebration of Daniel O’Connell and Parish Heritage
description:
This Culture Night, St Andrew’s Church on Westland Row will mark the 250th anniversary of Daniel O’Connell’s birth with a special celebration honouring both the Liberator and the rich heritage of the parish he inspired. 

Visitors are invited to attend an exhibition exploring O’Connell’s life and his pivotal role in the creation of this historic church. The evening’s programme will blend history, music, and community spirit, featuring a recital on the church’s historic organ and a performance by the resident choir. Reflecting the parish’s diverse present-day community, the event will also include contributions from local Chinese and Lithuanian groups, offering a vibrant mix of traditions. 

This unique celebration pays tribute not only to one of Ireland’s most influential figures but also to the evolving story of a parish at the heart of Dublin’s inner city.

title: Ceol, Craic, Caint agus Culture @ Culture Night Shannon
description:
Following the success of Culture Night 2024, Shannon Community Partnership is proud to once again bring Culture Night to life in Shannon on Friday, 19th September at Drumgeely Plaza. This year’s exciting programme celebrates the creativity, diversity, and community spirit of our town with a packed evening of music, dance, art, and more.

We’re thrilled to welcome back world-renowned uilleann piper Blackie O’Connell, fiddle virtuoso Eoin Neff, and Shannon’s own Ray Fean, followed by performances from Youth in Music and local legends One September. Hosting the evening’s festivities is none other than Damian O’Rourke from Cuppa Tea TV.

Enjoy traditional set dancing and music from The Kirbys, a stunning video presentation by Christina Bennett, and a vibrant wool installation from Michelle Hickey Legge. Experience the energy of Brian Fleming’s drumming circle, created in collaboration with the North Clare All Stars Refugee Project and Mná le Chéile Women’s Shed.

You’ll also find skittles fun with the Shannon Men’s Shed, and a range of delicious options from our on-site food trucks.

Ceol, Caint, Craic agus Culture — all in the heart of Shannon. Come for the music, stay for the magic. Everyone welcome

title: Challenge Game: Inside Picasso’s World | 19:15
description:
Step into the vibrant heart of the Spanish-speaking world at the Instituto Cervantes Library, home to over 11,000 volumes spanning literature, language-learning resources, graphic novels, and a cosy children’s section.

As part of Culture Night, the library invites visitors to take part in an immersive and interactive experience where art meets mystery. This creative escape room offers participants the chance to explore the life, work, and secrets of Pablo Picasso, one of the most influential artists of the 20th century.

Come with friends or join a team on the night for an unforgettable cultural adventure. Solve puzzles, uncover hidden clues, and discover the magic of Spanish art and culture—through the eyes of Picasso himself. Fun, thought-provoking, and suitable for curious minds of all ages.

For young people aged 12 and over, and adults. The game can be played in English or Spanish.

 

This event is part of the European Culture Trail – a EUNIC Ireland (European Union National Institutes for Culture) in cooperation with the European Commission Representation in Ireland.

For those visiting European Culture Trail events in person, download the passport here and collect stamps at each stop. You can win some wonderful prizes!

title: Chicken by Eva O’Connor & Hildegard Ryan
description:
Don Murphy is a proud Irish man, a hopeless ketamine addict and one of his generation’s greatest actors. He also happens to be a chicken. A Kerry cock to be precise. Across one fateful night, the feathered Oscar winner shares his star-studded story with an intimate audience – from getting his big break, to his first bird on bird sexual experience, to navigating life in the (human-dominated) celebrity spotlight. But along the way Don will be confronted with some harsh truths about himself, chicken kind and humankind.

“This show where a woman who plays a chicken who thinks he’s an Irishman is unlike anything you’ve ever seen.” — Playbill

★★★★★ “Sharp as a wishbone, with just the same potential to catch in the throat” – The Skinny

★★★★ “Clucking clever stuff” – The Stage

★★★★ “O’Connor’s performance is mesmerising, with plenty of laughs punctuating this otherwise unsettling tale of exploitation, self-loathing and sacrifice.” – British Theatre Guide

Winner of Filipa Bragança Award for Best solo female/ non binary identifying performer Edinburgh Fringe 2023, Best Performer Dublin Fringe 2024, Pick of the Fringe Adelaide Fringe 2025.

description:
Multi-award-winning and world renowned vocalist/composer Christine Tobin presents a programme of songs which explores themes of journey, growth, and resilience including originals alongside new arrangements of Tom Waits, Dylan, L. Cohen, Percy French, plus Tobin’s musical settings of WB Yeats, Paul Muldoon and more.

Christine Tobin – vocals https://www.christinetobin.org

Phil Robson – guitar https://www.philrobsonmusic.com

Damian Evans – double bass https://www.damianevans.net

Christine Tobin grew up in Dublin, later moving to London to attend the Guildhall School of Music & Drama. She was an integral part of the London contemporary scene for many years before moving to New York in 2015 where she made a considerable impact on the city’s creative music world. She returned to Ireland in 2020. ‘Returning Weather’, released in March 2023, was Christine’s twelfth album under her own name. In 2012 she won a BASCA British Composer Award for her settings of poems by WB Yeats, ‘Sailing To Byzantium’. The following year, her arrangements of Leonard Cohen songs won a Herald Angel Award at the Edinburgh Festival. In 2014 she was awarded ‘Jazz Vocalist of the Year’ at the Parliamentary Jazz Awards. Earlier in 2008, she won a BBC Jazz Award for ‘Best Vocalist’. Aside from her own projects, she has worked and recorded with an array of artists including musicians Django Bates, Billy Hart, Julian Joseph, Kenny Wheeler, Mark Turner, Louis Stewart, Nigel Kennedy, Jean Toussaint, Francesco Turrisi, Ingrid Jensen, poets Paul Muldoon, Eva Salzman, Don Paterson, actor Gabriel Byrne and film director Mike Figgis. She has played at major festivals and venues around the world.

title: Church of the Annunciation Blackpool – CANCELLED – : A Guided Visit
description:
<<THIS EVENT HAS BEEN CANCELLED>>
The Church of the Annunciation was opened in October 1945 was designed by noted Cork sculptor, Seamus Murphy, along with architect E.P. O’Flynn.
The church is of concrete block construction and very characteristic of its period. It was built on the site of a former church, St Nicholas’. Funds for the build were donated by Industrialist William Dwyer, Managing Director of the nearby Sunbeam Ireland and his staff. The stonework, tabernacle, lamp, candlesticks and other brasses designed by Seamus Murphy contribute to its artistic significance.
Mr Aidan O’Shea, a local historian, who has operated a pharmacy business in the shadow of “Blackpool Church” for many years, will give a short talk on the design, building and history of the church and the contribution of Seamus Murphy to this project.

description:

This open rehearsal, led by Strive Theatre and director Ciarain MacArtain, is part of a new project exploring the layered history of the house and the people who may have passed through it over the past three centuries. You’ll encounter fragments of work in progress of short monologues drawn from historical research and imaginative storytelling performed by actors in a relaxed, informal setting. Some pieces are polished, others still taking shape. You might see lines being rewritten, scenes discussed, or characters brought to life for the very first time. Drop in, listen, and stay as long or as briefly as you like.

This is a unique opportunity to witness not just the stories themselves, but the collaborative craft of interpreting and refining them. As this is a working rehearsal, we kindly ask all visitors to respect the focus of the performers. While you are free to come and go, please do so quietly to help maintain a supportive atmosphere. Whether you’re drawn by theatre, history, or curiosity, you’re warmly welcome to share in this moment of creative discovery.

title: Clay & Culture: An Introduction to Irish Ceramics: Discover the Craft, Shape the Story
description:
Join us for a relaxed and inspiring evening in our fully equipped ceramics studio in Ballinamore, where you’ll get hands-on with clay and explore the timeless art of Irish ceramics. Whether you’re a complete beginner or looking to build on existing skills, this workshop is the perfect introduction.

The evening begins with a short presentation tracing the rich history of Irish pottery—from ancient Neolithic vessels and Celtic craftsmanship to the work of modern-day ceramicists. You’ll gain a deeper appreciation for how clay has shaped Ireland’s creative heritage over millennia.

Then it’s time to roll up your sleeves! Under the expert guidance of Denise Corbett and her experienced team, you’ll work with authentic Irish clay to create your own ceramic piece. You’ll be introduced to a variety of traditional and modern techniques including pinching, coiling, slabbing, hand-building, modelling, throwing on the wheel, and glazing.

No experience? No problem. Our supportive, small-group environment ensures that everyone gets plenty of hands-on help. Denise Corbett, a seasoned ceramic artist, brings over 30 years of teaching experience and a warm, encouraging style that helps students of all levels unlock their creativity.

All pieces created on the night will be professionally fired and available for collection at a later date, leaving you with a unique, handcrafted reminder of your journey into clay.

Places are limited so early booking is essential.

title: Clonakilty Guitar Fest – Mohammad Syfkhan
description:
Mohammad Syfkhan is an Irish based Kurdish/Syrian singer and Bouzouki player. Mohammad’s own brand of ecstatic music takes elements from Middle Eastern and North African music to create an atmosphere of joy, love and happiness. Since arriving in Ireland, Mohammad has used the language of music to integrate into the local community by playing at private parties and concerts. He has been playing music since the 1980’s, while living in the city of Raqqa, Syria  where he began working as a professional singer and started his own band, The Al-Rabie Band which played concerts, parties, weddings and festivals all over Syria. His debut album ‘I Am Kurdish’ came out on Nyahh Records in February.

“Syfkhan takes his domestic influences and fuses them with music from beyond those regions, from North African folk rhythms to Turkish psychedelia. It’s a glorious alembic not bound by borders, where Mohammad himself brings a cultivated exuberance to his playing that belies his vintage.”
The Quietus

“His bouzouki playing, all coiling melodies, gliding shreds and emotional drive, is obviously a crucial component. So it fits that the first sounds to speak out from the grooves are the poised trills from Syfkhan’s buzuq, tempting you into the swirling uplift” – Backseat Mafia

”No one would be left sitting to this.” – Klof Mag

description:
The Art Trail is a vibrant celebration of local creativity, featuring a series of artworks displayed in the windows of businesses throughout the town. Created by talented local artists, each piece adds a splash of colour and imagination to the streetscape, turning everyday shopfronts into mini galleries.

This initiative not only showcases the incredible talent within the community, but also encourages locals and visitors alike to explore the town in a new and engaging way. title: Come Over to the Far Side: Poetry & Story at Athlone Bookshop
description:
Come over to the Far Side:

Poetry & Story at Athlone Bookshop

Join Jackie Gorman, Keith Payne and Catherine Prasifka from 6pm-8pm this Culture Night for poems and tales in Athlone Bookshop. There will be music on the night from Dylan Ó Muineóg. 

This public reading is the culmination of a day of readings in domestic settings across Connaught St and Environs.

Wine and refreshments will be served.

Jackie Gorman is the recipient of the John Broderick Emerging Writers Bursary. She has a Masters in Poetry Studies from DCU and her debut collection “The Wounded Stork” was published by the Onslaught Press, UK in 2019. It was described by Martin Dyar as an “engrossing and ecologically attuned debut.”

Keith Payne is the author of eleven collections of poetry in translation and original poetry, most recently Savage Acres (Dedalus Press, 2025), and Whales and Whales, from the Galician of Luisa Castro (Skein Press 2024).  Building the Boat (Cork City Libraries, 2023), was featured on BBC Radio 3’s The Essay He is curator of the Aodh Ruadh Ó Domhnaill Poetry Exchange Ireland/Galicia.

Catherine Prasifka is the 2025 John Broderick Writer-in-Residence. Her debut novel, None of This Is Serious, was an Irish Times bestseller and was picked as ‘one to watch’ by the Irish Times, Stylist and The Irish Independent. She holds a BA in English Lit. from Trinity College, an MLitt in Fantasy Lit. from the University of Glasgow and an MA in Irish Folklore and Ethnology from UCD. She was 2024 Writer Fellow at Trinity College Dublin.

Dylan Ó Muineóg is a multi-instrumentalist songwriter, performer & event organiser. He’s been playing music for over 15 years with various bands and under many names. In 2020 he moved to Brisbane and used this time to delve more into musical theory and composition, and worked with a number of jazz musicians and electronic music producers to make his favourite release to date – Kilramish Philharmonic. He returned home in 2023 and has spent the last year writing and recording his own new material as well as collaborating intensively with guitarist Kelvin Barr and fiddle player Ailish O’Grady for a new project, Bream.

title: Conor Schmtz
description:

Schmutz brought a fresh hybrid of fun and musical discovery to small venues across the city, hosting DJs like Midland, Krystal Klear, Hunee, and John Talabot.

He currently holds a monthly residency at Ulster Sports Club, where his marathon 5-hour performances span a wide range of styles.

title: Consent Chronicles: Stories of Hope, Healing, and Humour | We Act
description:
This Culture Night, join Dublin Rape Crisis Centre’s We-Consent campaign for an evening of thought-provoking storytelling at the Chapters Bookstore. “Consent Chronicles: Stories of Hope, Healing and Humour” will be a safe and inclusive space where voices can be heard, and experiences can be shared.

Throughout the night, we will spotlight different personal stories that explore themes of consent, sex, sex education and more. From tales of survival and resilience to humorous anecdotes about the first time someone had “the talk,” the night will balance the gravity of important conversations with moments of levity and light-heartedness.

Whether you have a poignant story about overcoming adversity or a funny story about learning the facts of life, we want to hear from you. Selected stories will be featured during the event, offering a diverse tapestry of experiences that reflect the multifaceted nature of these topics.

This evening promises to be a heartfelt and engaging celebration of human experiences. Together, we’ll laugh, reflect and grow as we listen to stories that remind us of the power of sharing and the importance of understanding consent and healthy relationships.

Consent Chronicles is a proud part of the WeAct Culture Night Campaign.

Submissions from interested storytellers are now closed. Selected storytellers will be notified by: 5th September via email.

title: Cork Centre for Architectural Education: Marseille – Exhibition
description:
Join us for this year’s Master of Architecture Exhibition.
Visitors can expect an array of drawings, models and films that describe new architectural proposals for the city of Marseille.
Surrounded by the Mediterranean and a transit point into Europe from North Africa, Marseille is both a space of crisis and of communication. It is, in a sense, full of contradiction and paradox. The city has its own epistemic kind of latitude; a strange type of milieu or middle-space between Eastern and Western Europe that hinges and ensnares the populations and spaces of Northern and Southern Africa around it. The focus this year evolves distinct architectural positions that produced new poetic types of architecture – something we might say is tethered between speculative realism and new types of material cultures.

title: Cork City Hall – Concert Hall: As If I Always Knew presents Cian Sweeney – A Piano Meditation
description:
As If I Always Knew presents: A Piano Meditation

Join Irish musician Cian Sweeney for a unique semi-improvised piano experience that blends mindful presence with live music. ‘As If I Always Knew’ invites audiences to step away from the digital noise of the modern world, creating a space for collective mindfulness through an immersive musical experience.

Each performance is crafted live, drawing on neoclassical, ambient, and impressionistic traditions while responding to the energy of the room. Audiences are welcomed to lie on yoga mats in an intimate circle around the piano, creating a meditative atmosphere where the performance becomes a shared experience.

The evening includes:

Semi-improvised solo piano performance
Guided group breathwork
Collective vocal toning/humming
Reflective, immersive listening experience

Drawing comparisons to Nils Frahm and Ólafur Arnalds, Cian’s approach returns to his natural musical voice after years as a producer and session musician. Previous performances include Cork Midsummer Festival (St. Fin Barre’s Cathedral) and Dublin Fringe Festival.

Performance Times

8:00pm – 8:50pm – Book here.

description:

This show brings the audience on a journey to normalise big emotions and other neurodivergent features. description:
An array of events this Culture Night at the Adult Lending Library:

 

The Ancient Mariner – A Theatrical Journey by Ocean of Notions

Ocean of Notions is delighted to bring Samuel Taylor Coleridge’s classic poem, ‘The Rime of the Ancient Mariner’, to life in a spine-tingling theatrical production at Cork City Library.

Directed and produced by the brilliant Judie Chalmers, this atmospheric performance features the incredible Kieran O’Leary in the role of The Mariner, with Nicole McDonagh’s hauntingly beautiful vocals adding a powerful emotional depth to the piece.

This is a must-see Culture Night performance, created by the same talented company behind the much-loved ‘Christmas Carol’ at Nano Nagle Place—a production that began its journey right here, at Cork City Library, back in 2010.

Step into this unforgettable tale of mystery, redemption, and the sea—an experience not to be missed.

Time: 18:45 – 20:00

 

‘Word In Edgeways’ Eamon O’Leary – Stories with Heart and Humour

Eamon Duggan is a familiar voice to many, as a regular contributor to RTÉ Radio 1, where he shares his witty and poignant vignettes on the popular Word in Edgeways slot.

After retiring, Eamon quickly discovered that hacking up Kinsale Golf Course wasn’t quite enough to keep him satisfied. Thankfully, his skill with a pen proved far superior to his putter, and his writing soon began to attract attention from editors on both sides of the Atlantic.

His story No Answer earned international recognition, winning the Southport International Competition in 2019. In November, he launched his debut collection of humorous childhood recollections, I’m a Big Boy Now, right here in Cork City Library—a book that has since enjoyed resounding success.

Join us for a chance to hear from a natural storyteller whose work blends humour, nostalgia, and heart with effortless charm.

Time: 19:30 – 21:00

 

Live music session with Áine O’Gorman

Join us for an intimate live music session with Áine O’Gorman, a rising Irish singer-songwriter known for her emotive lyrics and soulful sound. Áine began releasing her music in 2019 with her debut single “Lydia”. Since then, she has continued to captivate audiences with a growing body of work, including her self-titled EP released in 2021 and her powerful 2022 single “These Empty Rooms”, which was shortlisted for submission to last year’s Grammy Awards.

With a style that blends honesty, warmth, and vulnerability, Áine’s performance promises to be a moving and memorable experience for music lovers of all ages.

title: Cork International Film Festival: Online Shorts
description:
Cork International Film Festival celebrates Culture Night 2025 with 2 programmes of Animated Slovak Short Films.

Curated by the Slovak Film Institute, the Slovak Animated Shorts programme features twelve remarkable Slovak animated films. Programme 1 is intended for young viewers, while Programme 2 is aimed at adults. Together, they showcase a rich variety of storytelling and animation styles – from hand-drawn and puppet animation to stop-motion and digital techniques. These films explore a wide range of themes, including instructional, educational, advertising, and environmental subjects.

The legacy of Slovak animation pioneer Viktor Kubal, often regarded as the father of Slovak animation, resonates throughout the collection. His films are presented alongside that of other prolific animators such as Vladimír Pikalík and Jaroslava Havettová.

Spanning from 1955 to 1990, the selection offers a window into the rich history of Slovak animation. Sometimes surreal, at other times thought-provoking or purely entertaining – but always captivating – these shorts will surely engage and delight audiences of all ages.

title: Cork Opera House – Front of House: ‘Hear Here!’ Sound Installation
description:
‘Hear, Here!’ is an immersive sound installation that harnesses the unique technological infrastructure and acoustic character of Cork Opera House to redefine how we listen to, and experience, space. This is the culmination of extensive research into spatial audio, site-specific acousmatic composition, and auditory world-building. Audiences can actively engage with the familiar venue in an unconventional and exploratory way.

Celebrating the 170th anniversary of Cork Opera House as a historical and cultural beacon in the heart of the city, Dyson reflects on the legacy and evolving presence from its origins as the Athenaeum. The work explores the sounds of the city fed back into the arts and what contemporary listening practices reveal.

Beyond the architectural and technological offerings of Cork Opera House, Dyson will present a site-specific arrangement of interdependent speakers in a multichannel format throughout the building. Listeners are invited to let curiosity and attentive hearing guide their movement, experiencing not just the sounds emitted by individual speakers, but also how the concrete walls, carpets, and layout informs the sonic environment.

This installation is the result of UCC’s Masters by Research Studentship and the UCC | Cork Opera House Creating Together Partnership. Audience members can come and go as they please within the timeframe.

title: Cork Opera House: Behind the Scenes
description:
This year, Cork Opera House celebrates its 170th anniversary and is looking back on its long and important legacy while also planning and growing into the future. To celebrate Culture Night, we are inviting you to see parts of Cork Opera House that you may have never seen before!

Starting its life as The Atheneum and designed by John Benson, it was officially opened on Emmett Place in 1855 with the aim of promoting science, literature, and the fine arts. In 1875 the building was renamed The Munster Hall before finally receiving its current title of Cork Opera House in 1877 following extensive reconstruction and development.

Step behind the curtain and learn all about the historic highlights at Cork Opera House. From the icons who have performed on our stage to the tragic fire in 1955, you will not want to miss this Culture Night experience.

Guests with accessibility requirements are encouraged to get in touch ahead of time, so we can provide the necessary support.

For a tribute band, this means you have to look right, you must do justice to some of the finest rock music ever written and you have to capture and transmit that indefinable energy that fuels U2. With songs performed from U2’s Debut album “Boy”, right up to their last album “Songs of Experience” Rattle and Hum have it all covered. title: Culture Night at 18 Ormond Quay Upper Merchant Shop House
description:
Visit 18 Ormond Quay Upper, a traditional Dublin 1840s merchant shop-house saved and restored over a three-year period by Dublin Civic Trust.

Explore the historic upper floor rooms and learn about the restoration in the ground floor shop exhibition.

The project involved many traditional conservation techniques and materials, including Irish brick ‘wigged’ pointing, architectural joinery repair, lime plastering and decorative finishes.

The second phase is now underway, involving an older c.1760 building to the rear at 68 Arran Street East. This has involved conservation of the Georgian brickwork, previously coated in cement pebbledash, and complex restoration of the 1840s Roman cement shopfront and associated door and windows.

The upper floor interiors offer sweeping views of the River Liffey and are decorated in handmade Irish wallpapers typical of the mid-19th century, complemented with traditional mahogany furniture.

The quality of the project, and its demonstrative value, secured the Europa Nostra Award/European Heritage Award 2021, where the judges noted: “Meticulous research was carried out with significant efforts made to ensure a conservation-restoration that was consistent with the original values of the building and to conserve as much of the remaining details as possible.”

Visits on Culture Night are self-guided, but regular guided tours will take place during the evening as visitor numbers permit.

title: Culture Night Campus Tour of Griffith College
description:
Griffith College extends a warm welcome to Culture Night visitors. Discover the remarkable legacy of the college and more on a guided campus tour.

Originally the site of Grimswood’s Nurseries, construction began in 1813 on a remand prison later known as the Richmond Bridewell. Over the years, it housed notable figures such as Daniel O’Connell and James Stephens, and was the site of Joseph Poole’s execution in 1883. The prison held hundreds of inmates, including some involved in the 1916 Easter Rising. In 1892, the site was converted into Wellington Barracks and later became one of the first barracks handed over following Ireland’s independence. Renamed Griffith Barracks in honour of Arthur Griffith around 1922–1923, the premises were eventually purchased in 1991 to establish a third-level educational institution.

Come along to the campus to discover its storied history this Culture Night. 

Booking for this event will go live with the full Dublin City programme launch at 10am on 19 August.

As well as being a regular in the top Irish comedy clubs, he has performed in a number of festivals including the Vodafone Comedy Festival, Body and Soul, Electric Picnic, Forbidden Fruit and at the Edinburgh Fringe.

He is currently the host of RTE Comedy panel show CLEAR HISTORY alongside Jason Byrne and Joanne McNally
