title: Culture Night Crawl
description:
This year Portarlington will come alive with its Culture Night Art Crawl series of events. There is something for everyone and will include history, art, music, crafts, literature and comedy with free entry for all.

The events are spread across locations in the town from the Library down to the Parochial hall and back to the Anvil. Events over the evening will include a local art and photography exhibition in the Parochial Hall, a talk at the newly renovated Portarlington train station and music from the concert band, street buskers and members of Comhaltas.

Additionally, there will be a Guinness & Mussels event in O’Deas pub earlier in the day courtesy of Al’s Fish Shop to get you ready for Culture Night!

 Comedy Night

Anvil Upstairs: 9pm

The evening will culminate with performances by two incredible Irish comedians who bring their Edinburgh shows to Portarlington.

Colman Hayes – ‘Is This Anything?’
A loose, funny work-in-progress show from Colman Hayes about growing up Catholic, figuring out sex and wondering how he ended up like this. Jokes, stories, confusion and possibly closure.

Aideen McQueen – ‘Waiting for Texto’
Waiting for Texto is an electrifying interactive comedy play that captures the raw, universal experience of waiting for a response to your carefully crafted WhatsApp message. Through humour and technology, it explores the frustration of not getting a reply after an unforgettable night. Described as Bridget Jones meets Baby Reindeer, the play offers a fresh, hilarious take on the trials of modern dating, perfect for anyone who’s struggled with love and texting in the digital age. If men are such visual creatures, why can’t they see my texts?!

title: Culture Night Exhibitions at the Irish Architectural Archive
description:
Step inside the largest terraced house on Merrion Square and discover the fascinating work of the Irish Architectural Archive, housed in an elegant Georgian building.

In the Architecture Gallery, don’t miss ‘STUDIO’, a striking photographic exhibition by Harry Moore. This ongoing project delves into the liminal spaces of artistic creation, featuring evocative pinhole photographs of artists at work in their studios on the Beara Peninsula, Co. Cork.

Upstairs on the first floor, see A Form of Justice: The Story of Marshalsea, Empire, Lives and Capital. Created by Hassett Ducatez Architects, this installation unpacks the layered history of the now-lost Four Courts Marshalsea, offering a compelling reflection on architecture, incarceration, the legacies of empire in Dublin’s urban fabric. Incorporating archival documents and photographs, sound, video and a new, specially-commissioned model of the complex, A Form of Justice is an open-ended piece of work, intended to articulate a cultural position for the Marshalsea in the public imagination.

description:

5PM – 5.30PM: FAMILY RELAXED SESSION – PRE-BOOKING ENCOURAGED
LP understands how hectic Culture Night can be so we are delighted to offer one
half hour RELAXED SESSION for parents &/or children who may benefit
from a more peaceful, less populated space for any reason. We will have no music, less artificial lighting, more seating, additional volunteers to help out,
& more space aimed at contributing to an enjoyable experience for everyone.
Our RELAXED SESSION will be limited to 12 children.
5.30PM – 7PM: PRINTMAKING FOR KIDS & FAMILIES! NO BOOKING REQUIRED 
We will be welcoming all parents & kids for fun printmaking activities!
Last year’s event was jam-packed so please arrive well before our last intake at 6.45pm.
7.30pm-9.00pm: Mono Print Sprint – Adults!

Join us in Limerick Printmakers and explore monoprint printmaking and be part of our fast paced Monoprint Sprint! Limerick Printmakers are welcoming adults (16+ only) to the studio from 7.30pm – 9pm to share in the magic of printmaking Monoprint is a versatile printmaking technique where inked surfaces , a range of textures & unique mark making combine to create a one of a kind print every time. Each print is unique and cannot be repeated, offering a perfect introduction to the expressive possibilities of printmaking! Guided by the LP team we will take you through all of the steps of monoprint, from inking up, to picking out textures, to composing & printing your very own monoprint! We’ll be snapping pictures of all of your prints on the night to share in our online culture night gallery Last year’s event was jam-packed so please arrive well before our last intake at 8.45pm. We encourage you to arrive as early as possible as there may be queues This activity will take approximately 20 minutes, giving you ample time to enjoy the creative process.

title: Culture Night Late at SIRIUS, Cobh
description:
Culture Night Late at SIRIUS

SIRIUS presents a festival-style evening of visual art, film, poetry, music, performance and healing. It features new and existing/reconfigured performances, displays and screenings by artists Shirani Bolle, Fionnuala O’Connell, Florin Nolan, Maïa Nunes and SPACES.

The presentation explores themes and experiences of belonging, sharing, personal and intergenerational trauma, and heritage celebration. It is informed by the architecture, nature and history of the SIRIUS location in Cobh, County Cork, and uses water as an element that resonates materially and symbolically with people and land.

This multi-art-form, multi-room, multi-schedule programme allows meaningful encounters between culture and the public. Audience members self-direct their visit, choosing what to see among the multiple types and styles of art on offer.

EXHIBITIONS,   Florin Nolan,  SPACES , 9pm-midnight

PERFORMANCES, Fionnuala O’Connell, 9–9.30pm   Tobi Balogun, 9.45-10.30pm   Shirani Bolle, 10.45-11.30pm

Maïa Nunes (limited availability, booking via Eventbrite is required: https://www.eventbrite.ie/e/1668669448239), 11.45pm-1am

Sirius Arts Centre
Friday, 19 September
9pm-1am

Free; no booking required, unless otherwise stated
Culture Night Late at SIRIUS is produced by SIRIUS and curated by Miguel Amado, Director.

Culture Night Late at SIRIUS is funded by the Arts Council through the Culture Night Late scheme. Florin Nolan’s production is additionally supported by Cork County Council through a Bursary. title: Culture Night Tour of Freemasons Hall
description: The Freemasons’  invite members of the public to learn about one of the oldest historical buildings in the city and share its past and present history. A guided tour of the building will highlight the significance of the building in it various guises, including its notable residents from the past and current owners from 1946. title: Culture Night Tour of Stillgarden Distillery & Laboratory
description:
Discover Dublin City’s last independently owned distillery this Culture Night with a guided tour of Stillgarden Distillery in Inchicore, Dublin 8. Founded in 2019 by Viki Baird and Pat O’Brien, Stillgarden is a multi-award-winning distillery and visitor centre known for reimagining what Irish distilling can be.

Guests will explore the distillery’s innovative lab, where modern distillation techniques meet bold botanical creativity to produce a unique range of lower-alcohol white spirits and aperitifs. Experience Stillgarden’s “Modern Spirit” ethos, founded on ‘pro-social distribution’ built on science, nature, and community and learn about how they utilise science, nature and community to create better drinks, communities and planet.

The tour includes a complimentary cocktail (non-alcoholic options available), and a peek into their Gin School and Distilling Academy, where visitors can create their own custom spirits.

Join Stillgarden for an evening of flavour, experimentation, and forward-thinking craft.

Booking for this event will go live with the full Dublin City programme launch at 10am on 19 August.

title: Culture Night Tour of the Revenue Museum
description:
The Revenue Museum invites visitors to come and explore their unique collection of Ireland’s history this Culture Night in the historical surrounds of the crypt of the Chapel Royal in Dublin Castle.

Uncover the history of Revenue and its pivotal role in shaping the Irish state.

This tour showcases remarkable treasures, including iconic Saorstát Éireann stamps from the early days of Irish independence; the very first Statement of Accounts for the state, a foundational document of modern fiscal governance; and a book rescued from the burning of the Custom House. Explore fascinating customs displays featuring seized contraband and a preserved poitín still — a vivid reminder of Ireland’s history of illicit distilling.

Short tours as Gaeilge will be also available at 16:00, 17:00 and 18:00.

description:

Culture Night / Oíche Chultúir is a national moment, celebrating all that makes up the richness and diversity of Culture in Ireland today, connecting people to cultural activities locally and nationally and aims to open up pathways to ongoing engagement.

Our Culture Night walk will be led by the DMP Volunteer Rangers who will be discussing the history of the Hell Fire Club and its environs, along with the flora & fauna along the way.

**While this walk will start during daylight hours, it may finish in darkness so please bring a torch.

– Date: Friday, 19th of September.
– Meeting point: Hell Fire Club carpark at 18:00.
– Duration: 1.5-2 hours, approximately.
– Distance: 6km approx.
– Degree of difficulty: Moderate.
– Bring: Torch, walking boots, rain gear, warm layers, water, and snacks.
– Public Transport: Plan your journey here Plan A Journey | Transport for Ireland.
– Parking: If driving, please carpool as there is limited parking.

Note – no dogs allowed on this walk.

Please inform us privately of any health issues on the day and ensure you bring any necessary medication with you.

In the event of an orange or red weather warning, this event will be cancelled. Other weather warnings will be assessed on a case-by-case basis.

title: Dance Cork Firkin Crane: Crane Visual: “Satori in Cork” Exhibition & Tours
description:
Exhibition: Satori in Cork: Stage 2 – A Sangha of Makers

‘Satori’ (悟り)—a Japanese Buddhist term meaning sudden enlightenment or deep spiritual insight—serves as the contemplative starting point for this reflective exhibition curated by Dermot Browne.

Satori in Cork: Stage 2 – A Sangha of Makers draws inspiration from ‘Satori and Unfolding’, two contemporary dance works by Australian choreographer Lewis Major, who returned to Cork as part of the 2025 Midsummer Festival. This meditative exhibition brings together a sangha—a creative community—of thirteen artists whose works explore presence, materiality, and the felt experience of stillness. Spanning painting, sculpture, video, poetry, and installation, the exhibition embraces emptiness, quiet form, and the subtle tension between appearance and insight.

Far from spectacle, ‘Satori in Cork’ invites visitors to slow down, breathe, and notice. Like the Zen moment it references, it is an exhibition of attentiveness, offering a space for perception and small awakenings.

Presented by Crane Visual in collaboration with Dance Cork Firkin Crane.

Hourly screenings of ‘Satori’ by Lewis Major Projects on Culture Night at 4pm, 5pm, 6pm & 7pm (upstairs)

Exhibition runs: 24 June – 20 September 2025

title: Demelza Nowell & Mícheál O Muirthile – Recent Workst Work, Macroom
description:
Mícheál O’Muirthile is an Irish prize-winning artist who looks to celebrate his local surroundings, flora and fauna. Although having started out primarily with a realist style, O’Muirthile’s oil paintings in particular have in recent decades become more impressionistic, with an increasing use of sgraffito and impasto giving dynamic textural depth. O’Muirthile is particularly interested in local rural areas and their habitats and looks to evoke their timeless quality within his work. Unchanged for centuries and devoid of people, transport and technology in much of his Art, the artist sees the rural landscape as a special continuum which can never be dated to one specific time. He currently resides in Macroom town in Co. Cork. His work is in private collections throughout Ireland, the U.K., continental Europe, America, Canada, Australia and the Middle East. For more specific information on his artwork, visit www.michealomuirthile.com.

Demelza Nowell is a Cornish artist who grew up in Ireland, where the surrounding landscape, myths, and folklore of her adopted home became her biggest influence. She primarily paints in a realistic style using watercolours on paper and canvas. Recently she returned to higher education and earned both a degree and Masters in Celtic Studies and Early Irish Medieval History. This endeavour enabled her to further study the original medieval Irish manuscripts, particularly the stories and myths that they contain, and so provide endless inspiration from the rich culture and heritage of Ancient Ireland. She currently lives near Macroom. Instagram : @demelzanowell

title: Demilitarising Finance: a walking, talking and singing tour of the IFSC
description:
This Culture Night, Dublin’s Docklands will be revealed as never before. Financial Justice Ireland, in collaboration with Afri, invites the public to join a walking tour that weaves together protest and performance, spoken word and live music.

 

The tour peels back the polished glass and steel of the International Financial Services Centre to expose how global finance fuels militarism, fossil fuels, tax injustice, and even genocide. At the same time, it asks how our economies might be reshaped around care, solidarity, and community rather than violence and profit.

 

With acclaimed speakers, poetry, and music, this is not simply a tour to watch but one to join—walking, questioning, and singing together. Facilitated by Financial Justice Ireland and Afri, it charts a path toward justice, peace, and sustainability.

title: Discovering Greece/Hellas with the Hellenic Community in Ireland
description:
The Hellenic Community of Ireland invites visitors on a fascinating guided tour that uncovers the rich cultural and artistic connections between Greece (Hellas) and Ireland. Beginning with the classical references on the National Gallery’s Merrion Square façade, the tour continues inside to explore masterpieces that reflect the enduring influence of Greek history, mythology, and aesthetics.

Highlights include El Greco’s evocative St Francis of Assisi, the Cretan artist’s spiritual vision with echoes of his homeland; Jacques-Louis David’s dramatic The Funeral of Patroclus, inspired by Homer’s Iliad; Joshua Reynolds’s witty parody of Raphael’s The School of Athens; and Eugène Delacroix’s Demosthenes on the Seashore, a striking portrait of the famed Athenian orator.

This Culture Night tour offers a journey through art, history, and the cultural threads shared by both Greece and Ireland.

 

This event is organised by the Hellenic Community of Ireland under the auspices of the Greek Embassy in Dublin.

title: Don’t Mention the ‘C’ Word
description:
The National Leprechaun Museum, Ireland’s only museum dedicated to the art of oral storytelling, presents a special Culture Night edition of ‘Don’t Mention the ‘C’ Word.’ Join this immersive storytelling experience and learn about the dark side of Ireland’s history. 

London. The year is 1661, the night is dark. An Irish innkeeper, preparing for bed, gets a knock on the door. What the innkeeper sees next is quite a shock: several men lusciously dressed, a high court judge in full garb, and an open coffin. They claim the rotting remains are those of Oliver Cromwell! They have been ordered by the King himself to put Cromwell’s body on trial.

 The trial must take place here, tonight, and in secret. The very mention of the Lord Protector’s name brings a chill down the innkeeper’s spine. The fearful innkeeper agrees to host the trial, but will Cromwell finally see punishment?

Visit the National Leprechaun Museum on Culture Night to hear the true tale of what happened that night. 

This is a 16+ event not suitable for young listeners.

title: Dún Laoghaire Rocks: Tracing the History of Rock Music in DLR
description:
Join IADT for an inspiring evening at the historic Carnegie Library, Dún Laoghaire, as we dive into the vibrant legacy of music in Dún Laoghaire and its cultural impact across generations.

Michael Mary Murphy will explore the venues, bands and people that made Dún Laoghaire’s night life vibrant and exciting over the years.

From David Bowie’s first appearance in Ireland (in a Dún Laoghaire TV studio), to shows by punk bands including the Clash, the Jam and the Damned, and ear-splitting performances by Nirvana, Metallica and the Jesus and Mary Chain, this event highlights Dún Laoghaire’s surprising place in rock history. Jeff Buckley’s first international performance was in Deansgrange!

Discover the journeys of local artists like The Boomtown Rats and Sinéad O’Connor, who rose from DLR neighbourhood’s to achieve global fame.

Whether you’re a music lover, student, historian, or curious local, this is your chance to hear from those who’ve lived it, studied it, and helped define it. This talk celebrates the talent, culture, enthusiasm and enterprise of DLR’s music community.

Presented by IADT as part of our commitment to celebrating creative culture, heritage, and community engagement.

title: Dún Mhuire Legion of Mary Visitor Centre: The Legion of Mary Invites You
description: The Legion of Mary invites you to visit our Centre in Cork City and meet our members. We will share with you the history of the Legion, information about our work in Ireland and all over the world, and the stories of our most prominent members, such as Servant of God Frank Duff, Servant of God Alfie Lambe and the Venerable Edel Quinn, a Cork woman born in Kanturk. The Legion was founded in 1921 by Dubliner Frank Duff, a Catholic layman, and since then has grown to be the largest international organisation ever founded in Ireland, spanning the globe, all continents, and almost all countries.  It is everywhere comprised of ordinary Catholic people who express their faith by serving the Church and their community. The Legion considers itself is an essential part of  Catholic Culture. Whether you are interested in becoming a new member, just want to know more, or are interested in the great trove of local and international history we hold in the Legion, we welcome you. And we will also give you a cup of tea.

title: Earthquakes & Other Geohazards
description:

Robert Mallet produced the first artificial seismic waves at Killiney in 1849 and coined the term ‘epicentre’ for the point on the ground above the earthquake!

title: Echoes of 1916
description:
Roscommon visual artist and traditional Irish musician Ellen Susan Igoe will exhibit her hand-drawn portraits of the seven signatories of the Irish Proclamation—Seán Mac Diarmada, Thomas J. Clarke, Patrick H. Pearse, James Connolly, Thomas MacDonagh, Éamonn Ceannt, and Joseph Plunkett. The artwork will be accompanied by music composed and recorded by the artist, creating an immersive tribute to the men who shaped Ireland’s revolutionary history.

On the night, Susan will also give a live performance at approx. 8pm blending her art and music to honour the spirit of the 1916 Rising in an unforgettable setting in the vaulted stables at Strokestown Park House.

Ellen Susan Igoe is a visual artist, musician and teacher based in Roscommon, having taught both nationally and internationally. Her work explores the transience of human existence and the delicate nature of shared moments. Themes such as life, death, loss, memory, Irish culture and heritage recur throughout her practice, much of which ultimately alludes to the fleeting nature of life.

Through her work, she invites viewers to contemplate the impermanence and brevity of life and to discover the profound beauty found in shared human experiences. She views the concept of memory as an intangible element that can be transformed into objects—whether found or made—shaped by lived experience. Her creative process spans a wide range of materials, including drawing, painting, ceramics, sculpture, photography, music, videography, and digital media.

title: Encoded Voices perform Sutartinės: Traditional Lithuanian Polyphonic Songs
description:
Experience the beauty of Sutartinės, ancient Lithuanian multipart songs performed by the vocal group Encoded Voices.

The word sutarti means “to be in accord,” and these unique polyphonic songs weave together voice, rhythm, and subtle movement in a powerful expression of harmony and connection. Traditionally sung by women in two- or three-part arrangements, Sutartinės are one of the oldest and most distinctive forms of Lithuanian folk music.

This special performance takes place as part of Culture Night, offering audiences a rare chance to experience this unique and ancient musical tradition live.

Sutartinės were recognised by UNESCO in 2010 as part of the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

title: ESB | A Bolt out of the Blue: Ardnacrusha Photographic Exhibition – 100 Years of Modernist Architecture at Ardnacrusha
description:
Visitors to “A Bolt out of the Blue” on Culture Night can enjoy traditional harp music, complimentary barista coffee and cupcakes served from the iconic ESB Volkswagen van, an ESB Archives display, worksheets and activities.

To commemorate the turning of the first sod at Ardnacrusha in August 1925, and in collaboration with the National Built Heritage Service, ESB will host a photographic exhibition in the foyer of its Headquarters on Fitzwilliam Street Lower, titled “A Bolt out of the Blue – 100 Years of Modernist Architecture at Ardnacrusha”.

August 1925 saw the signing of contracts between the Irish Free State and the German-based firm Siemens-Schuckert for the construction of a hydroelectric generating station on the River Shannon.

Known as the ‘Shannon Scheme’, it was to deliver the electrification of towns and villages throughout Ireland and accelerate the social, economic and industrial development of the country.

Now 100 years on, the enduring significance of the Shannon Scheme has been recognised in A Bolt out of The Blue, a specially curated exhibition with photographs by the Photographic Unit of the National Monuments Service.

Using light and shade, and emphasising perspective and scale, the exhibition is designed to challenge our perception of modern architecture & the artistic potential of industrial design.

title: EXHIBITION LAUNCH “WHERE THE FIELD FAILS TO HOLD” – BY CIAN LAWLER, PRESENTED BY MUINE BHEAG ARTS
description:
Muine Bheag Arts is delighted to present Where the Field Fails to Hold, an exhibition by Cian Lawler at the Bagenalstown Community Garden. The exhibition launches on 19th September as part of Culture Night and continues until 28th September.

Where the Field Fails to Hold is a series of photographic interventions which reflect on the rhythms of everyday life in a small town. The photographs document casual encounters with friends, familiar places and often overlooked details of Muine Bheag. Lawler began photographing his daily life in 2019 as a way to explore the emotional tether to his hometown.

Cian Lawler is a visual artist based in Muine Bheag, County Carlow. Rooted in exploration and introspection, his practice navigates the intersections of identity, community, and space. He investigates the spatial politics of queer existence, focusing on how environments are imbued with meaning through the presence and actions of bodies.

Working primarily with photography and video, his work seeks to uncover hidden narratives within spaces both public and private and examine the dynamics of belonging, intimacy, and cultural memory. His projects often reflect on personal experiences and broader sociopolitical contexts, with particular attention to queer histories and rural landscapes.

Muine Bheag Arts is an artist-run organisation that engages with the local context to present projects in the public realm. Guided by values of collaboration and experimentation, Muine Bheag Arts invites dialogue between artists, audiences, community and place. The programme includes exhibitions, workshops, events, residencies, publishing and radio broadcasts. These platforms provide opportunities for artists to research, test and make through close collaboration with the organisation and members of the local community. www.muinebheagarts.com.

title: Exhibition launch & Live Performance – The landscape swallows our histories by Amanda Rice & Jo Pester
description:
The landscape swallows our histories whole is a duo show by artists Amanda Rice and Jo Pester showcasing a new collaborative 8mm film work.

The film explores the geological, technological, human and more-than-human traces left behind at Knock Iveagh — a neolithic burial site in Northern Ireland. Comprising burial cairn and green energy solutions, multiple points of time collide within this ritual landscape: ancient pollen particles, cremated bone fragments, charcoal dating back to 3060BC, local residents, green capitalism, techno hubris. A shared terrain, haunted by both the past and pressing possibilities of imagined futures.

The film works with processes of archaeoacoustics and Stone Tape theory which use sound to extract communications from ancient materials. The artists’ bodies act as soundboards for the landscape, trespassing both material borders of landownership and temporal borders across time.

title: Exhibition Launch: Blossom: Contemporary Chinese Painting by Rong-Gen Yin
description:
To mark the opening of Blossom: Contemporary Chinese Painting by Belfast-based Chinese artist, Michael Rong-Gen Yin, we invite you to sample some traditional Chinese tea in the company of the artist. Michael will talk about Chinese artistic traditions, the techniques employed in the paintings and what has inspired them.

Michael Rong-Gen Yin, originally from Shanghai, began painting in the traditional Chinese manner in the 1970s. During the 1980s he was a member of an artist collective and tutored painting in Japan and Germany.

He came to Northern Ireland in 2003 and has continued to paint and teach traditional Chinese painting techniques. He practises the two main techniques of Chinese painting – Gongbi, where intricate brushstrokes form detailed coloured landscapes, which can include narrative themes – and Xieyi, which is much looser using bold brushstrokes and watercolour wash.

Michael currently tutors Chinese watercolour painting in the Chinese Resource Centre and the Crescent Arts Centre in Belfast.

title: Exhibition: FORMWORK Mandy O’Neill
description:
O’Neill uses photography practice in an instinctual and responsive manner, to understand, process and contain the material and social environments in which we live. She is especially interested in our built environment – from schools and community venues, to housing and institutional buildings. Her multi-layered methodology begins with walking and photographing to identify sites of interest. Geo-historical research, and social engagement with communities, reveals the lived experiences of these sites, often unearthing their socio-political and ideological underpinnings.   In this exhibition O’Neill presents a series of artworks responding to a particular site of development and dereliction in Dublin’s North inner city. The term formwork refers to a  support system of grids, panels, props and beams used in building. O’Neill has extensively photographed formwork and shoring structures across the city and suburbs, using these photographs as references for the creation of sculptural installations. Metaphorically the term formwork  describes the processes of making and construction, and the concepts of social and material support structures in Mandy’s practice. This site-specific installation presents various forms – architectural, sculptural, print-based, photographic, textual and aural, with a focus on spatial and material experience.

title: Exhibition: Politics and Democracy in Fingal, 1924-39
description:
Fingal Local Studies & Archives have commissioned Dr. Declan Brady to undertake a six-part book series on politics and local government in North County Dublin. This unique series will give a comprehensive political history of Fingal over more than 200 years.

The first book in this series, Politics and Democracy in Fingal, 1924-39, is accompanied by an exhibition which will be on display on Culture Night in County Hall, Swords. This exhibition recounts the story of the struggle after Irish independence to build and consolidate the new Irish Free State, and the attempts by local politicians in Fingal to maintain their political independence and influence. It is a story of not just political division and personal animosity born in the divisions of the Civil War, but also of political and administrative competition between centre and periphery, national and local government, and the unresolved issues of poverty, class inequality and the land question.

The book will be launched on Monday, 22nd September 2025 at the Carnegie Library in Swords and will be distributed free-of-charge through Fingal Library branches and as an eBook on BorrowBox.

Dr. Declan Brady is a research historian, educator and professional genealogist. He completed his PhD, ‘The Evolution of Local Politics in North County Dublin, 1870-1948’, at Maynooth University, where he now teaches.

After the walk, we’ll gather in the creative tent for an upcycling workshop. Children will turn the fabric scraps into beautiful feathers and creative collective bird, symbolizing all the voices of the forest.

To finish, children will take turns reading lines from Birds’ Radio, and their voices will be recorded to create a unique “live broadcast” of the poem—just like a real bird radio show!

title: Feathered Friends’ Art Exhibition, a Bird Conservation Project – Cobh Library
description:
An art exhibition titled Feathered Friends will be installed in Cobh Library for the month of September. The exhibition will launch on Culture Night, September 19th, with a special talk by renowned ornithologist and local author Jim Wilson, who will speak about the subject of the exhibition.

The collection features paintings depicting Irish bird species that are of conservation concern and appear on the red list. Through this work, the artist aims to foster a deeper connection with nature and raise awareness and appreciation for these vulnerable birds and their habitats.

Jim Wilson, who will deliver the talk at the launch, is a wildlife writer, international wildlife tour leader, photographer, and broadcaster. A former chairman of BirdWatch Ireland, he has published several books on Ireland’s birds and is a regular contributor to The Mooney Goes Wild Show on RTÉ Radio 1.

Cobh Library, located in the Arch Building on Casement Square, has a dedicated exhibition space and is an ideal venue for showcasing this nature-inspired artwork. The event will be promoted through targeted invitations, social media, and posters, reaching BirdWatch members, local schools, community and garden groups, businesses, and nature conservation organisations across Cobh and the greater Cork area.

title: Field Notes – Listening Party at Segotia
description:
We hear music everyday, but how often do we truly listen?

 

Field Notes is a full-body album listening experience. Set in Segotia’s yoga studio, Dublin’s new creative oasis, this four-part series invites you to slow down, tune in, and take note – what can we find, when we really pay attention?

 

The session is guided by artist and facilitator Maria Kelly, who gently leads participants through grounding and journaling exercises before the listening begins. Attendees are then invited to lie down, supported by bolsters, blankets, and eye masks. In this calm, screen-free space, we listen to one carefully chosen Irish album, in its entirety, through Segotia’s bespoke sound system; designed and built by Toby Hatchett (The Big Romance, Fidelity).

 

Field Notes launches on Culture Night with Sinéad O’Connor’s iconic The Lion and the Cobra.

 

Spaces are limited, early booking is advised.

 

Event Schedule:

7:45pm – Doors open. Attendees are invited into the yoga room to settle in and find a mat.

8:10pm – Welcome and introduction to the evening’s structure, album theme, followed by a short guided grounding exercise.

8:20pm – Journaling Exercise 1: a reflective prompt to tune into the album’s theme.

8:30pm – Full album listening experience begins.

9:10pm – Attendees are gently guided back into the room.

9:15pm – Journaling Exercise 2: reflect on the journey the album brought you through.

9:25pm – Gentle conversation and sharing are welcome.

10:00pm – Event ends.

title: Field Queens – a new play reading
description:
A reading of a new play “Field Queens” written by Áine Ryan at Jim of the Mills, Upperchurch, Co. Tipperary.

In rural Ireland, two fifteen-year-old girls clean vomit from a bus after a drunken mishap on their way to a teenage disco the previous night. When they encounter the bus driver’s alcoholic wife and spend the day drinking in a field together, laughter turns to danger and tears when the issue of alcoholism is confronted.

A representation of authentic rural Ireland and the youth that live there that is both funny and warm but also heartbreaking, capturing the spirit of hope and female friendship.

Áine Ryan is a multi award winning performer and writer. She has a BA in Theatre from Goldsmiths, University of London. Other writing credits include Paddy goes to Petra, Kitty in the Lane, From Out the Land (co-writer) and First Date (Disney Plus).

title: Flamenco Dance Demonstration with Sandra Palomar | 17:00
description:
Experience the vibrant rhythms and expressive power of flamenco at Instituto Cervantes this Culture Night. Recognised by UNESCO as Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2010, flamenco is a deeply emotive art form that tells stories of passion, resilience, and cultural identity.

Led by professional dancer and teacher Sandra Palomar, this interactive demonstration offers visitors a chance to witness the intensity and grace of flamenco up close. The event includes a brief introduction to the history and cultural roots of flamenco, followed by a lively and inclusive demonstration in a relaxed atmosphere.

Sandra Palomar, a skilled bailaora originally from Motril, Granada, brings decades of performance and teaching experience to the stage. Visitors of all ages are invited to take part, learn a few basic moves, or simply enjoy the rhythm and expression of this iconic Spanish tradition.

 

This event is part of the European Culture Trail – a EUNIC Ireland (European Union National Institutes for Culture) in cooperation with the European Commission Representation in Ireland.

title: From Grenfell to Belfast: Race, Poverty, and the Politics of Housing
description:
The Lab | Free/Booking Essential | 6.30pm – 8pm 

The Grenfell Tower fire exposed not only a devastating loss of life but also the deep structural inequalities of race, poverty, and class that shape who gets safe housing- and who doesn’t. This event connects that tragedy to the housing crisis in Belfast, unpacking how systemic neglect, economic injustice, and racial inequality intersect in both contexts. Through critical analysis and lived experiences, we will explore what these parallels reveal about power, accountability, and the urgent need for housing justice.

This event will include an introduction to The State of Belfast, an exhibition exploring housing inequality; a film screening of Seeking Home, about a homeless refugee family, and how precarious their life is; light food by the Kind Economy Chefs; and conversations with anti-racism and housing activists, refugees and filmmakers.

title: Gardens of Our Memory, Sherkin Island
description:
The Culture Night event will be a site specific set of video/visual and audio installations called ‘Gardens of our memory’, involving a walk around a semi-outdoor exhibition, set in a centrally located large set of gardens on Sherkin. The gardens are made up of tree covered areas, sheds, outhouses, conservatories and small pockets of garden and flowerbed areas.

The video element will comprise of a set of approximately 8 projections of video footage of local islanders gardens, projected onto walls with accompanying music, and seating areas for people to watch and listen. The videos will have been filmed in various garden locations around the island and will mainly focus on flowers, plants and trees, water features and streams, and be accompanied with music and nature/field recordings made in the gardens.

The event will kick off with serving botanical themed refreshments, and a talk about the installation, the ideas behind it and an invitation to share and record stories throughout the evening. As the evening progresses I will be onsite with a microphone and recorder, taking islanders stories in a special recording area (one of the sheds! )

The area will be lit with outdoor lights, light from the cabin and sheds, and the projectors. There will be indoor and outdoor seating, and a gazebo set up in the garden. As the dusk draws in, the projections will light up the different areas of the gardens and the trees, creating a beautiful visual effect.

It will provide attendees with a chance to see a small part of Sherkin, illuminated and with beautiful projections and music to create an audio/visual spectacle.

title: Gaza Biennale – Irish Pavillion
description:
Gaza Biennale is a collaborative international art project that features over 50 artists from Gaza, serving as a form of resistance against the ongoing war, destruction, and suffering of innocent civilians in Gaza.

International Pavilions for the project have so far been organised in Berlin, Edinburgh, London, Padua, South Africa, Valencia, Denmark, Istanbul, New York, Sarajevo, Toronto, Washington D.C., and now in Ireland.

Organised by the North Leitrim Palestinian Solidarity Group and supported by the Leitrim Sculpture Centre, the project in Ireland will feature a series of video portrayals of artists from Gaza, including several documentary and fictional films that provide historical context to the ongoing conflict.

The event in Ireland also hopes to feature ‘Gaza: A Picture of Destruction’ by Mohammad Suliman, who is displaced in Cairo. This installation project (currently en-route to Ireland) depicts the destruction of homes in the Gaza Strip caused by the war. Suliman utilises his training in creating architectural models to document this historical moment, the impact of war on civilian lives, and the profound psychological and social effects it leaves behind. The models depict destroyed cities, including demolished houses, and environmental elements that did not escape Israeli occupation.

The Gaza Biennale at Leitrim Sculpture Centre raises awareness and understanding of Palestinians’ current plight and affirms and supports their right to self-determination.

Middle Eastern music and food will accompany the exhibition.

title: Gile na Gile – Ceol agus Aistir Aodhagáin Ó Rathaille, Baile Bhuirne
description:
Composed and performed by Lorcán Mac Mathúna (voice), Martin Tourish (accordion), and Éamonn Galldubh (whistle and pipes).

The Gaelic world fell apart during the life of Aodhagán Ó Rathaille, and he was one of the main commentators on this decisive turning point in the history and literature of Ireland. He was born during the Bardic School era and died in poverty during the time of the Penal Laws and the poetic courts. He is the creator of the political Aisling; the music of hope during a dark period.

Rathaille wrote profound, bold, and fierce poetry. He was a keen critic of a tragic, feudal time, writing with understanding and always with an eye for beauty in language. He wrote lyrically, with rhythm and melodic harmony. He was the most skilled poet of the New Irish era. A poet whose words have yet to be surpassed. With the material he wrote, creating the meter and style of modern Irish, it can be said that Rathaille is the father of modern Irish literature.

“I sense the true pulse of Aodhagán the witty.”

title: Good Bog Bad Bog
description:
“Good Bog Bad Bog” is a collaborative project by Bray-based artist Sharon Wells, who creates imaginative landscapes from wool using felting techniques. Working with community groups, Sharon developed a series of wool “bog scapes” that contrast the richness of a living, functioning bog with the depletion of an eroded one. These tactile works highlight the ecological importance of Wicklow’s peatlands, sparking conversations about biodiversity loss, climate resilience, and water quality.

Through hands-on workshops, participants explored their own connections to the bog, while reflecting on the wider role of sheep and wool in shaping the Wicklow uplands. The act of crafting landscapes from local wool linked artistic expression with cultural memory, farming traditions, and environmental care.

The project will culminate in a Culture Night exhibition at the wonderful ‘Schoolhouse for Art’ in Enniskerry, showcasing the community’s creations. Visitors will encounter wool-based interpretations of the peatlands that invite reflection on how human activity influences these fragile ecosystems. By blending craft, ecology, and heritage, Good Bog Bad Bog highlights both the beauty and vulnerability of the landscapes that define Wicklow.

title: Guided Heritage Walking Tour of Mater Misericordiae University Hospital
description:
Step back in time this Culture Night with a guided walking tour of the Mater Misericordiae University Hospital, one of Dublin’s most important medical institutions.

From its opening in 1861 to its role today, the Mater has been at the forefront of Irish healthcare for over 160 years. On this engaging hour-long tour, visitors will discover the hospital’s iconic architecture and explore how it became a centre for medical education and groundbreaking research. Along the way, you’ll hear stories of patients and staff life in the early 1900s, and learn about the Mater’s involvement in pivotal national events, including the Easter Rising.

This enjoyable tour offers a rare chance to uncover the rich heritage and enduring impact of the Mater on Dublin and beyond.

The tour covers the main hospital campus, with some stairs along the way — but all routes are wheelchair and buggy accessible via lifts.

Meeting point: Eccles Street hospital entrance beside the original historic building.

Booking for this event will go live with the full Dublin City programme launch at 10am on 19 August.

title: Guided Tour of Broadstone
description:
This Culture Night, take a guided tour with Emma Gillece, architectural historian of Broadstone, a famous Dublin 7 landmark steeped in history. 

The historical Broadstone building operated as the headquarters of the Midland & Great Western Railway from 1847 and 1937. Built between 1841 and 1850, and known as the ‘Director’s House’, the building was designed by John Skipton Mulvaney and sat in front of a train shed offering rail access to points across the west of Ireland. Since the establishment of Ireland’s national bus company, Bus Éireann, in February 1987, the building has operated as offices for Bus Éireann as part of the Broadstone bus depot. 

The historical walking tour of Broadstone is open to all members of the public who are eighteen years and over.

title: Guided tour of Department of Finance and Government Buildings
description:
This Culture Night, visitors will be able to join a guided tour of the interior of South Block Upper Merrion Street, the magnificent building that is home to the Department of Finance and the Department of Public Expenditure, NDP and Reform. 

South Block was designed by Sir Aston Webb, the pre-eminent British architect of the early 20th century who designed the Victoria and Albert Museum, Admiralty Arch and the façade of Buckingham Palace, London. The building retains its original late Edwardian interior Government Buildings is Webb’s only known building in Ireland. The interior was renovated recently, which has included a restoration of original features.

Come along on Culture Night to enjoy a guided tour of the building, and take in a special talk on the history and architectural elements of the building.

title: Guided Tour of the Historical Garden at Athlone Castle
description:
The Historical Garden at Athlone Castle is like stepping back in time, featuring plants that would have grown in castle gardens during the Middle Ages. Medieval gardens were full of herbs, flowers, fruit trees, and bushes. Many of these plants were edible or used in cooking, while others had medicinal purposes or were used for making dyes and inks.

This variety shows how military castles, like Athlone Castle, were largely self-sufficient. Not only does the garden give us a tantalising glimpse into the past, but it also offers us benefits today. The Wildflower Meadow and planters provide a haven for bees and butterflies a colourful display for everyone to enjoy.

Come along to Athlone Castle this Culture Night for a guided tour of the Garden.

First Tour: 6-7pm

Second Tour: 7pm-8pm

Black Church Print Studio is a members organisation for professional artists working in fine art printmaking. Since its opening, 40+ years ago, it has established itself as a significant and dynamic organisation. The second floor is the etching workshop area. The top floor provides a workshop for screen print and an analogue photography and photo-etching darkroom. title: Guinness Storehouse Presents: These Walls
description:
Visit the iconic Guinness Storehouse after dark and experience These Walls – an immersive exhibition specially commissioned for Culture Night, celebrating the people and place of Dublin 8. Visual artists Deirdre Breen and Owen de Forge present an indoor iteration of their work from These Walls, a new street art initiative founded by the Guinness Storehouse in its 25th anniversary year.

Set within the Storehouse’s striking industrial setting, audiences are invited to step into this landmark exhibition and immerse themselves in an evocative portrait of Dublin 8 that explores memory and place through light, sound, and form. Breen’s abstract compositions respond to the area’s evolving architecture and layered histories, while de Forge’s figurative works capture the neighbourhood’s social life through playful characters and unconventional canvases. The exhibition is further enhanced by a specially commissioned soundscape by Saoirse Millar and Wastefellow, together with live contemporary dance.

After the exhibition, finish your night with a bite and a pint while taking in the spectacular city skyline from Gravity Bar.

The result was a new portrait, which since its completion in 2021 has been a treasured part of the private collection of friends of the artist. title: Hive Nature Poetry Showcase
description:
Hive is a journal of nature poetry from Ireland, set up in 2023 by Clare poet Niamh Twomey. This Culture Night, join Hive for a lively showcase hosted by poet and editor Grace Wells and featuring readings by four of Clare’s finest nature poets. This will be followed by an open mic, where you are warmly invited to share your own nature-inspired poems, or indeed the work of a favourite poet.

About the host: Grace Wells is an award-winning eco-poet and environmental writer. Nature, spirit-of-place, and humanity’s multiple ecological crises are the main themes of her work.  Her three poetry collections have all been published by Dedalus Press, most recently, ‘The Church of the Love of the World’, which was nominated for the 2023 Laurel Prize and the Farmgate National Poetry award. She is the winner of the Eilís Dillon award, and the Rupert and Eithne Strong Debut collection award. Her poetry has been translated into Italian, Spanish and Galego. In 2021, Grace Wells was selected as Poet Laureate of Ennistymon by Clare County Council and Poetry Ireland, during their inaugural Poetry Town project. Her book-length poem about the town, its past, present and future, ‘Everyone Has a Different Ennistymon’, was published by Doolin Arts, in January 2023.

The first two issues of the journal will be available on the night at a discounted price, and light refreshments will be provided. Venue limited to 20 audience members so arrive early to avoid disappointment!

title: Homesick: Domestic medicine in Ireland, c.1760-1900 Exhibition
description:
For most of our history the majority of medical and health care has been delivered in the home. The importance of the domestic setting, and the role of women, in the delivery of medical care has been overlooked in the history of medicine, which has focused on clinicians and their contributions.

This exhibition explores healthcare provision in middle and upper-class homes in Ireland between c.1760-1900. It highlights the active role of women in delivering medical care in this period, and how they were often the intended market for those selling treatments and remedies – from the conventional to the unusual. This often hidden history reminds us how important homes, and the people in them, have always been in looking after our health. Visit the Royal College of Physicians of Ireland at 6 Kildare Street on Culture Night to view this fascinating healthcare exhibition.

title: How might we reimagine death rituals?
description:
Death is the most inevitable rite of passage of all. It is a universal experience which we collectively face yet we do not often think beyond the ways in which we mark this final event.

Ritualisation is an ancient response to change, loss and death and offers powerful opportunities to creatively interpret and ascribe meaning to our unique human journeys. Join us for an experiential evening (6.45pm – 8.30pm) where we will meet, connect and explore the ways in which we might reimagine death rituals. 

As this is an experiential workshop, participant engagement is required throughout the duration of the event. Due to the nature of this delivery, participant numbers are limited to 20. It is respectfully asked that you do not register if you are unable to attend in full. The workshop will take place in Corley’s, Ballintubber (F12 EH24), an informal setting, accessible by wheelchair, where alcohol will be served. In I Dreamed of the Sea, Fiona takes audiences on a deeply evocative journey through music born of coastal life—from haunting ballads shaped by ancient maritime myths to powerful new songs that honour the grit and resilience of those who live and work by the ocean.

Accompanied by two superb musicians—Billy Kennedy on guitar and Paul Seymour on piano—Fiona weaves a rich tapestry of sound that captures both the wild beauty and the harsh realities of the sea. Expect an inspired blend of original compositions and time-honoured favourites, drawing from Celtic traditions, folk heritage, and contemporary songwriting.

This concert not only showcases Fiona’s distinctive voice and style but also pays tribute to the deep cultural connection between music and maritime communities—where every wave carries a tale, and every tide leaves a song behind.

Let the music carry you to distant shores, feel the salt in the air, and experience the timeless bond between the sea and the people who call it home.

title: IFCO & Screen Ireland: Classify an Irish Short Film
description:
As part of this year’s Culture Night, the Irish Film Classification Office (IFCO) and Fís Éireann / Screen Ireland invite visitors behind the scenes of the world of film classification for a one-of-a-kind experience. Step into IFCO’s intimate onsite cinema and take part in classifying a Screen Ireland short film alongside an official IFCO Film Classifier – a rare opportunity to see exactly how IFCO comes to a decision and why a particular age rating would be applied.

Each screening will be followed by an interactive discussion, where audiences can explore the guidelines and decision-making process that determine whether a film gets a G, PG, 12A, or 15A classification and debate where they would draw the line themselves!

With multiple screenings running between 16:00 – 20:00, there’s something for everyone, including options suitable for younger audiences. Booking is essential – make sure to reserve the screening that’s right for you and your family for this unmissable Culture Night event.

title: Inextinguishable – An Exhibition Celebrating Brigid by Greg Hallahan
description:
‘Inextinguishable’ by Greg Hallahan is an art exhibition that celebrates the spirit of Brigid using recycled cardboard as a canvas in the Lady Chapel inside St. Brigid’s Cathedral. Brigid, a revered figure in Irish culture, holds a special place in our hearts, making her influence truly ‘inextinguishable.’ The artworks, crafted from recycled double corrugated cardboard, breathe new life into this common material sourced from shops, stores, and even friends and family. By using this everyday material, the artist aims to recycle and reintegrate it into the very idea of transport and transcendence. This process also symbolically connects with the myths and stories of Brigid and Saint Bridget.

The artwork explores inner and outer surfaces, drawing the viewer in while also keeping them at a distance, creating a lively interaction. The link between the structures and the material is shown as deep – both are often overlooked, yet they hold a quiet strength and beauty that deserve attention. The artwork invites people to experience the meeting of myth, material, and art in honour of Brigid’s lasting importance.

Join us for an unforgettable evening as Inishowen Carnival presents An Púca, a magical sculpture and performance trail through Letterkenny Town Park for Culture Night.

A tribute to the mischief-making shapeshifters of Celtic folklore, An Púca celebrates the mysterious figures said to bring both good and bad fortune. Most often associated with rural and coastal communities, these elusive creatures take many forms, changing depending on where in Ireland their stories are told – sometimes animal, sometimes human, always unpredictable.

This year’s event will feature three striking large-scale Púca sculptures, a lantern and sculpture trail through the park, roaming characters, and live performances full of energy and wonder. title: Insane Mama Moments – A Storytelling & Soulful Connection Event for Mothers
description:
Insane Mama Moments – A Storytelling & Soulful Connection Event for Mothers
Hosted by The Sane Mama | Location: The Edge Café, Tallaght

“Insane Mama Moments” is a community storytelling and wellness event created for mothers — a deeply supportive space to share the often-unspoken realities of motherhood. Held in a warm, welcoming environment, the evening invites participants to reflect, release, and connect through shared experience.

The event features an open-mic-style session where mothers are invited to read aloud true stories, poems, or spoken word pieces that explore the raw, emotional terrain of their parenting journeys. These stories often carry themes of shame, overwhelm, trauma, and identity shifts — moments that are rarely shared due to stigma or silence, yet resonate deeply across maternal experiences.

This storytelling will be complemented by a group embodiment session, including gentle guided meditation and time for emotional processing and release. Participants will also be introduced to Matrescence, the psychological and emotional transformation into motherhood, often misunderstood or overlooked in mainstream discourse.

A light, workshop-style format allows space for group reflection, body connection, and story-collection activities, giving voice to personal experiences that deserve to be heard and held.

Set in the cozy and inclusive space of The Edge Café in Tallaght , the evening invites attendees to connect over tea, presence, and shared truth. Potential collaborators include local yoga teachers, Matrescence coaches, and maternal mental health professionals.

Insane Mama Moments aims to create visibility for the private, often hidden aspects of motherhood — increasing connection, reducing shame, and fostering emotional resilience through honest, collective storytelling.

title: Ireland: Land of a Thousand Welcomes?
description:
Did you know St Patrick was a migrant to Ireland? For thousands of years, Ireland’s history and culture has been shaped by much more movement and diversity than we might sometimes think. This event presents a series of talks and discussion on the sometimes hidden histories of the many different groups who have contributed to Irish culture. With presentations from academics, community leaders and other experts, this event celebrates the diversity of Irish history and the stories that we sometimes aren’t told. Individual speakers will cover the stories of Black and people of African descent in Ireland; Jewish Ireland; Traveller voices; and communities who have arrived more recently, including Brazilian- and Indian-Irish people. Ireland has long been known as the ‘land of a thousand welcomes’ – but who have we welcomed, when and how?

title: Irish Cooking – An traidisiún á thabhairt chun boird (Bringing tradition to the table)
description: Slow Food Galway in conjunction with Diarmuid Ó Mathúna, will host a bilingual traditional Irish food demonstration, at Pota Café, exploring the rich and enduring role of food in our culture. Through time-honoured recipes, using local ingredients, we will highlight how food connects us to the land, to our ancestors, and to one another. This event aims to deepen appreciation for the tastes, techniques, and traditions that have been passed down through generations, fostering a living connection to Irish heritage. The demonstration will promote cultural understanding, and the preservation of both language and food traditions. Diarmuid trained at Ballymaloe Cookery School and is passionate about the Irish language. He established Pota, a bilingual cafe in the heart of the Connemara Gaeltacht to provide a space where local ingredients and the language can flourish. Slow Food Galway is part of Slow Food International, a global grassroots movement founded in 1989 to counter the rise of fast food and fast life and promote local food cultures and traditions. It advocates for good, clean, and fair food for all, emphasising the pleasure of quality food and the responsibility to protect the heritage of biodiversity, culture, and knowledge that make it possible. There will also be some traditional Irish baskets on display that had a role in Irish kitchens and farms.

title: Irish Language and the 1925 Census of the Gaeltacht
description:
This Culture Night, the National Archives of Ireland invites visitors to delve into a fascinating chapter of Irish history with the exhibition Irish Language and the 1925 Census of the Gaeltacht.

The exhibition shines a light on the Irish Free State’s earliest efforts to protect and revive the Irish language, beginning with the landmark 1925 Census and the work of the Gaeltacht Commission. Visitors will uncover how Irish gradually found its way into government services, education, and public life, and how these efforts were supported by grassroots activism, place-name restoration projects, folklore preservation, and the promotion of traditional industries.

Through a display of original archival documents, the exhibition reveals the powerful and enduring influence of the Irish language on our cultural identity from the struggles of the early 20th century to its vibrant presence in modern media, the arts, and everyday life.

title: Jaskane at Ormston House
description:
Jaskane is an exciting chamber folk trio with a unique blend of oboe, violin and electric guitar. Their vibrant performances of well-known folk tunes from around the world as well as eclectic modern pieces, cinematic themes and original compositions will delight the listener.
Their first album, ‘Jaskane Café Trio Live’ was released in 2013, capturing the group’s energetic performance style. In 2016, the Jaskane recorded ‘Lumen’ with a new, expansive sound and distinctive original pieces.
In 2021, Jaskane released their first EP of entirely original compositions ‘Divoká Planeta’ recorded during, and in response to the COVID pandemic. Their latest release, ‘Wildlands’ (2022) is an EP of trad-inflected instrumental pieces inspired by the North Clare landscape.
Violinist Karen Kelly’s influences span from the simplicity of baroque string music to modern scores, tangoes and jazz. Etain McCooey has developed a uniquely ‘Irish’ oboe style by combining her classical oboe training with her knowledge of Irish whistle style and technique. Jason Noone is a guitarist and producer with a background in rock, blues, and improvisation.
Join Jaskane at Ormston at 7.30pm  for Culture Night 2025!

title: Jazz @ St Saviour’s Church, Rathdrum
description:
Bray International Jazz Festival returns for its fourth Culture Night to the lovely St. Saviour’s Church in Rathdrum to present ‘Ebb & Flow’; saxophonist Michael Buckley’s critically acclaimed quartet.
Ebb and Flow is a new and entirely original project from the Dublin bandleader and saxophonist, who is accompanied by three of the great players of contemporary Irish jazz: Greg Felton (piano), Barry Donohue (bass) and Shane O’Donovan (drums).

The group released their debut album to critical acclaim on the Livia Label in the Spring. The music is modern, tender, and exciting, featuring daring up-tempo post-bop tunes, beautiful ballads, and imaginative improvisation.

Michael Buckley is recognised as a leading Irish jazz musician, producer and band leader. A phenomenal tenor player, he is also a much in demand producer and arranger. He has collaborated and toured with The Mingus Big Band, and played with a host of international name jazz stars including Dave Liebman, Lee Konitz, John Abercrombie, Jason Moran, Jason Rebello and Joey Baron.

Recorded in 2024 at Michael Buckley’s House of Horns Studio, ‘Ebb and Flow’ the album has been described by Jazz Irealnd as “a compelling collection of nine original compositions” that “exemplifies the modern Irish jazz landscape at its finest.”

description:
As part of its Culture Night 2025 programme, Goethe-Institut Irland invites families to enjoy a live Kamishibai performance—a captivating form of Japanese paper theatre—at its library on 37 Merrion Square.

Kamishibai (literally “paper theatre”) combines striking illustrated cards with a scripted, spoken narration. Performed using a traditional butai (wooden stage), the storyteller slides through the illustrated scenes while bringing the story to life with dramatic flair.

Perfect for children and families, the event continues with a creative workshop where young participants are invited to create their own Kamishibai stories and decorate pre-prepared paper stages.

Suitable for the whole family.

title: Late Opening at IMMA: Art as Agency and Staying with the Trouble
description:
Celebrate Culture Night 2025 with a late-night visit to IMMA, where two major exhibitions—IMMA Collection: Art as Agency and Staying with the Trouble—will remain open for evening viewing.

The exhibition Staying with the Trouble, inspired by author and philosopher Donna Haraway’s seminal work, features over 40 Irish and Ireland-based artists whose diverse practices explore urgent themes of our time. Pushing against social norms, the works in the exhibition challenge us and attempt to make sense of the present, questioning interspecies relationships, ideas of transformation, and renewal. The exhibition challenges human-centric narratives, advocating for a multi-species/multi-kin perspective through sculpture, film, painting, installation and performance. 

Visitors can also explore Art as Agency, a major three-year display celebrating IMMA’s Permanent Collection as a source of agency and knowledge. The exhibition examines how artworks connect across time and contexts, fostering new interpretations and relevance. Works from the 1960s to the 1980s evoke the foundational story of the Irish art world. While acknowledging the context of the modernist, predominantly male dominance of that era, the exhibition also spotlights the material innovation and socially engaged practices of others who persisted despite the relatively conservative status quo.

This journey takes him—from the seabird colonies of Skellig Michael to tranquil woodlands in the Burren, from the corncrake stronghold of Tory Island to a solitary nest in the Donegal uplands—capturing the delicate soundscapes of Ireland’s wildest places. Seán’s hypersensitivity to sound—both a struggle and a strength—draws us into an immersive exploration of listening, memory, and connection with the natural world. Reger’s production skills have been widely recognized, earning him accolades from influential artists such as Special Request and Jaguar from BBC Radio 1. In 2020, he was a winner of Special Request’s Dubplate contest, which earned him a special-cut vinyl from the legendary producer and DJ. The two artists even played together at the JikaJika! Festival in Derry in 2021.

Inspired by some of the best selectors in the industry, including Gilles Peterson, Ben UFO, Call Super, Mr Scruff and Batu, Reger is known for his unique and intricate DJ sets that showcase a wide range of musical flavours and mind-bending selections. 

His contribution to the Irish music scene has been substantial, starting with his appearance on BBC Introducing’s ‘Beat Seekers’ series in 2020 and continuing with his fourth mixtape for the station, which showcased the diverse talent on the island of Ireland.

In September 2021, Reger made his AVA Festival debut, performing a 2-hour set on The Baltic stage that showcased his eclectic tastes and drew praise from the audience. He has also contributed original works and remixes to the cutting-edge Belfast imprint, Extended Play, and remixed local legend Carlton Doom on the renowned Hypercolour label.

At just 21 years old, Reger has a promising future ahead of him, with upcoming performances at AVA Festival, Ulster Sports Club, and curated nights at Thompson’s Garage. Keep an eye out for this rising star in 2023.

title: Lest We Forget – Castledermot’s Forgotten Poet, George Graham
description:
The poet George Graham was born in Castledermot in 1829 and his book of poetry ‘Lest We Forget’ which celebrates Castledermot was published in 1894. Given that he was a Methodist lay preacher, it is apt that he be celebrated in his own words and with music on Culture Night in Castledermot library, a former Methodist Church.

When, in 1866 George and his wife set sail for New Zealand, they left behind in the churchyard in Castledermot the remains of their three young children. In 1894 he returned for his first and only visit to Ireland. In a poem he titled ‘Once more I have seen thee’ he wrote of the joy and sadness of returning to his native village.

On Culture Night, Graham’s story will be told, his poems celebrated and music performed in Castledermot library at 8 pm by Angela Keogh and John MacKenna.

title: Liminal – Work In Progress Showing
description:
On Culture Night, The Playhouse is opening its doors for this special work-in-progress showing. You’re invited to step inside and experience a mix of music, lighting, and visuals that come together to create something new. The atmosphere shifts and changes, just like the world around us, and you’re encouraged to get involved and see how your presence shapes the experience. Liminal is an immersive live event that celebrates the Autumn Equinox with a multi-sensory spectacle, inviting audiences to step into the threshold where light meets shadow. As day and night balance, this experience explores our own precarious position in the climate crisis—halfway in the light, halfway in the dark. Through a dynamic fusion of music and light.

Liminal is an immersive live event that transforms the experience of transition into a powerful, multi-sensory spectacle, inviting audiences to step into the threshold where light meets shadow. At a time when balance feels both urgent and elusive, Liminal creates a space to reflect on our own precarious position in the climate crisis—halfway in the light, halfway in the dark, poised on the edge of change.

As participants enter the experience, they are drawn into an environment where boundaries blur and the ordinary becomes extraordinary. The event unfolds through a dynamic fusion of music, light, and evocative imagery. Pulsating rhythms and organic soundscapes intertwine with shifting beams of illumination, casting the space in a dance of brightness and darkness. Subtle atmospheric cues evoke both the beauty and fragility of the natural world.

Liminal is more than a performance; it is an invitation to pause and consider the choices that define our collective future. The perfect balance of light and shadow serves as a living metaphor for the urgent need to restore harmony to our planet. Audiences are encouraged not only to witness, but to reflect and engage with the questions at the heart of the climate crisis: What does it mean to stand at the threshold of transformation? How can we move from uncertainty to action?

In this shared moment, Liminal asks us to embrace the possibility of change. It is a call to awareness, a celebration of balance, and a reminder of our power to shape what comes next. Here, in the space between, transformation is not just possible—it is necessary.

This is a preview of what Liminal will become in the future. It’s an experiment, and your feedback and reactions will help shape where it goes next. Join us at The Playhouse on Culture Night, be part of the process, and help us find new ways to imagine change together.

Liminal Landscapes brings together new work by Gabhann Dunne and Theo Hynan-Ratcliffe, opening on Culture Night at The Courthouse Gallery & Studios, Ennistymon. The exhibition reflects transitional themes ranging from ecological shifts to the boundaries between sculpture and writing, drawing inspiration from the Burren’s unique environment and feminist new materialist perspectives. Through Dunne’s evocative environmental paintings, focused on the transformation of the Burren landscape and the resilience of native species, and Hynan-Ratcliffe’s sculptural and written explorations of grief, ritual, and materiality, the exhibition creates a compelling dialogue between art, ecology, and identity. Visitors are invited to experience this multisensory exhibition in an informal, social setting during the opening evening. The event offers an opportunity to meet the artists, engage with their ideas, and reflect on themes of environmental awareness, personal connection to place, and the passage of time.

title: Listen to the Land Speak – Clonakilty Library
description:
We are delighted that we will be launching our work on Friday 19th Sept at 2pm in the library where the tutor will do a talk & demo. 

 The inspiration for the project came from Manchán Magan’s book – Listen to the Land Speak.  

The exhibition is a collection of pots which were wheel-thrown, hand-built and decorated by individual Service Users with coloured glazes made from organic matter collected from each Service User’s local environment such as nearby fields, gardens and beaches. The materials included: Garden clay, Fern leaves, Ash leaves, Calathea, Hydrangea, Acacia berry twigs and Seaweed.  The materials were burnt to produce a variety of different ashes which were then sieved and added to our base glaze. The colours come from the metals remaining after burning, these probably include Iron, Copper, Cobalt, Manganese and Chromium.

This programme was kindly funded by Cork County Council Arts.

Pianist and PhD researcher Fidelma Nugent will introduce the music and its deep connection to colour, rhythm, and the natural world. As the piece is performed live, Bridget Lambert, a Tipperary-based artist and teacher, will guide participants in responding through visual art. Bridget’s work celebrates co-creation and has included large-scale community murals, such as her tribute to Dolores O’Riordan with children from rural Limerick. title: Little Cubists: A Journey into the World of Pablo Picasso
description:
Pablo Picasso was an artist from a very young age. In this fun workshop, children aged 6 to 12 will discover who Picasso was, how he lived, and why he changed art forever. They’ll learn about some of his curious artistic periods, ranging from his use of sad colors to his wildest portraits.

What if the eyes aren’t where they usually are? What if the nose is sideways? Participants, guided by early childhood teacher and art historian Sara Pascual, will explore the world of Cubism, where everything is seen through geometric shapes and lots of imagination. Through games, cut-outs, colors, and collage, they’ll create their own Cubist portraits, inspired by some of Picasso’s most famous works.

This is ideal for curious kids who want to play, create, and discover a world where art has no rules.

title: LoGaCulture: Voices of the Boyne
description:
On Culture Night, Trinity College Dublin’s Front Square will host a live demonstration of LoGaCulture: Voices of the Boyne, an immersive audio-augmented reality experience.

The project invites visitors to step into one of Ireland’s most decisive moments—the Battle of the Boyne (1690), when King William III and King James II clashed in the largest battle ever fought on Irish soil. Through music and sound, participants explore not only the world of 1690, but also connections to Neolithic Ireland and the present day. Players select a character, follow their path through song, and respond to symbolic calls: the Fox leading towards the future, the Raven guiding into the past. Along the way, choices—whether to face mercenaries or gather strength—shape the journey.

Though played on a smartphone, the experience comes alive through headphones provided on site, surrounding participants in an evocative soundscape.

The LoGaCulture Ireland project is led by Prof. Mads Haahr and Joris Vreeke at Trinity’s School of Computer Science and Statistics, with collaborators Dr Svetlana Rudenko (music and AR), Karun Manoharan (programming, spatial audio), and Breanne Pitt (evaluation and communication). Funded by the European Union’s Horizon Europe Framework Programme.

title: Longest Way Round, Shortest Way Home: The making of an exhibition
description:
For Culture Night 2025, join Michael Hill from Temple Bar Gallery + Studios as he reflects on the making of Longest Way Round, Shortest Way Home, an ambitious exhibition staged at Dublin Port’s Pumphouse heritage zone.

Taking its title from James Joyce’s Ulysses, the project explored ideas of travel, return, and transformation through two major site-specific commissions: Yuri Pattison’s dream sequence and Liliane Puthod’s Beep Beep. Set against the backdrop of Dublin Port’s historic graving docks and industrial heritage, the works responded to the unique character of the port as both a physical space and a cultural metaphor.

In this lecture, Michael will share insights into the curatorial process, the challenges of presenting contemporary art in industrial settings, and the dialogues that emerged between artists, place, and history.

After his performance, the garden transforms into a living fairytale in Madcap Chronicles of Wonderland, a vibrant outdoor show blending Slavic folklore with the whimsical world of Alice in Wonderland. description:
Produced by Artist Marie Phelan, Me and You and Us and Them is a short film which will be screened outdoors at Kilcumney Cross, South Carlow, along the Borris to Bagenalstown road.

Projected at the edge of a field, the work engages a landscape marked both by the nearby site of the 1798 Battle of Kilcumney, and by the ongoing encounters with traffic. Its non-linear structure allows audiences to engage at any point in the cycle, inviting passersby to slow down and consider what lingers after events have faded.

title: Medicine and Childhood – Museum of Childhood Ireland

Join the Museum of Childhood Ireland this Culture Night at the Old Anatomy Theatre in Trinity College Dublin. Hear an incredible panel of speakers sharing their unique insights on Medicine and Childhood, past, present, and future.

Speakers:
Dr Greg Martin, a medical doctor with specialist training in public health in Ireland and a Consultant with the HSE. Focused on evidence-based interventions to improve population health and address health inequalities.
Dr Ida Milne PhD, Author and Historian, and TCD Dept. of History visiting research Fellow and Carlow College history lecturer on the transfer of public health knowledge through the ages and infant mortality.
Dr Jean Walker, an Independent Historian and Lecturer, focuses on the social history of health and medicine, as well as the gendered history of the 19th & early twentieth centuries. She has made a particular study of the care and medical treatment of babies, children, and young women at the Westmoreland Lock hospital in Dublin in the nineteenth century, and more generally in the lives of the sick in Ireland, 1800-1950.
Dr Peter Boylan, FRCOG, FRCPI, is a former Master of The National Maternity Hospital and former Chair of the Institute of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists. Author of In the Shadow of the Eighth: My Forty Years Working for Women’s Healthcare in Ireland and, with Dr Jennifer Walsh, The Irish Pregnancy Book.

title: Miss Julie | Theatre at Tailors Hall
description:
This Culture Night, An Taisce welcomes visitors to Tailors Hall to enjoy a night of candlelit theatre by way of August Strindberg in his most famous of plays, ‘Miss Julie’.

Miss Julie is a naturalistic play written in 1888 by August Strindberg. This version is translated & adapted by Howard Brenton. It is set on Midsummer’s Eve and the following morning, which is Midsummer and the Feast Day of St. John the Baptist. The setting is an estate of a count in Sweden. Miss Julie is drawn to a senior servant named Jean, who is well-travelled and well-read. The action takes place in the kitchen of Miss Julie’s father’s manor, where Jean’s fiancée, a servant named Christine, cooks and sometimes sleeps while Jean and Miss Julie talk. They drink beer and eventually Miss Julie encourages Jean to seduce her.

The audience is invited to be part of a workshop dress rehearsal of this great play. They will get to see the inner-workings of rehearsal and see the actors explore the piece rather than a final polished piece of theatre.

Maureen O’Connell will play ‘Miss Julie’ opposite Michael Mullen as ‘Jean’ with Leanne Bickerdike as ‘Kristin’. Paul Nugent from AboutFace Theatre Company will direct. Jennifer Keane is the Production & Costume Designer with assistance from Tara Norris in Costume. Conor Tobin is the videographer. Produced by Tom Lynch for 3 Hot Whiskeys Prods. With big thanks to Sinéad Owens, Narella Forte at An Taisce and to Stephen O’Donoghue.

Performed by candlelight in one of Dublin’s most historic buildings, this promises to be an unforgettable Culture Night experience.

 

An extra 15:00 performance of Miss Julie at Tailors Hall has been added due to demand.
