Mo has been a former special guest at the Dungarvan Singers Club on a few occasions on all of which he has played up a storm and gone down hugely with our appreciative audience. And why wouldn’t he be popular? He appeals to every taste. He plays guitar, piano, keyboard, fiddle, accordion, banjo, mandolin, harmonica, dobro (the dobro is a splendid instrument and very rarely played.) He is a multi-instrumentalist par excellence. He plays blues, jazz, classical, bluegrass, country, folk, traditional, Cajun, …. We were at a trad. session one time and a guy came up and said “By any chance, would you know any Al Jolson? I suppose that’s unlikely!” And Mo immediately without any warning or preparation sings a medley of ten, not just one, f Al Jolsons hits!!

The guy can play and sing anything. Just try him with your favourite request. He does George Jones better than anyone else, also Paul Brady, Elvis, Mississippi John Hurt, Merle Haggard, Maggie Barry, Django Reinhardt, Robert Johnson, Segovia, Jerry Lee Lewis.

title: Moments in Light – A Photographic Journey Along the Wild Atlantic Way
description: Solas Photography Club is a vibrant and inclusive collective of photography enthusiasts based in Oranmore, Co. Galway. Founded by a group of passionate local photographers, Solas is dedicated to celebrating the art and craft of photography through shared learning, creativity, and community spirit. Our annual programme includes workshops, talks, and field trips that bring members out into the heart of Ireland’s most breathtaking natural settings – from the rugged shores of Connemara to the limestone landscapes of the Burren and beyond. For Culture Night 2025, Solas are proud to host “Moments in Light– A Photographic Journey Along the Wild Atlantic Way”, a curated exhibition of images that reflect the diverse talents and perspectives of our members at The Foyer of the Marine Institute in Rinville. The exhibition will showcase work ranging from sweeping sea-scapes and quiet rural scenes to intimate portraits, wildlife encounters, and documentary-style moments captured across the Wild Atlantic Way. An informal artist talk and Q&A session will accompany the exhibition, offering a chance to meet the photographers, hear the stories behind the images, and share in the passion that drives the work. Whether you’re a fellow photographer, a fan of the Wild Atlantic Way, or simply curious, you are invited to join in this celebration of light, sea-scape, and creativity.

title: Moon Tell Me the Truth
description:
As part of this year’s Culture Night, The Museum of Free Derry is proud to host the Moon Tell Me Truth exhibition. 

The exhibition, curated by the Hands Up Project, is a collection of 60 illustrated poems created by children from Gaza. 

Tragically, most of the students featured in the exhibition are now displaced, with their homes and schools destroyed, and at least two are known to have been killed in Israeli airstrikes. 

Museum of Free Derry curator Adrian Kerr said: 

“We are very proud to host this deeply moving exhibition and to give local people the chance to read these words from children in Palestine, written just before their world was brutally torn apart by the Israeli onslaught on their homes, but in a year – 2023 – that was already by then the most dangerous on record for Palestinian children until the current genocide.

description:
Rooted in the beauty of the west of Ireland, The Push and Pull explores the dualities

captures the emotional rhythms of raising children: moments of connection stretched

title: Nano Nagle Place – Global Hub: Embracing Rights, Enriching Culture
description:
Visit the exhibition ‘Embracing Rights, Enriching Culture: Our Story is One – The Legacy of the Ten Shiraz Women’ on Culture Night.
Honouring ten Baha’i women executed in Shiraz, Iran, in 1983 for their faith, the exhibition is part of a global campaign that spotlights courage and the ongoing struggle for equality and justice. Visitors begin at the #OurStoryIsOne area, where they explore articles, artwork, and videos about human rights. Each person randomly selects an envelope containing a photo and the name of one of the ten women, embarking on a personal, multimedia journey through her story.
Photographs and narratives celebrate both the individuality and unity of the Shiraz women. QR codes lead to narrated videos and campaign artwork. A symbolic prison enclosure recreates the women’s sense of isolation; inside, a looped video of a prison poem brings to life their experiences of imprisonment and execution. The exhibition concludes with a poignant video in which the mothers of two women describe the aftermath of the executions. A moving musical tribute highlights the inspiration and hope drawn from the women’s ultimate sacrifice for justice and equality.

description:
‘Listen to the Fields’ is an evening of film, spoken word, art, science and music – a reflection on biodiversity along the rivers of Cork City.

In early summer, a group of people met at the Old Cork Waterworks and walked from there across the Thomas Davis Bridge, through the park at Mardyke and across the footbridge to the Lee Fields, where they stopped to watch an immobile heron gazing at the foamy water of the weir. The group included 20 Young Travellers, ecologist Irene Ní Shúilleabháin, spoken word artist Raphael Olympio, botanist Helena Brady, artists Anne Cleary and Denis Connolly and Cork TVG youth workers Rachel Coffey and Patrick McDonagh.

This was the first of several such meetings to observe, think, talk and make art about fresh water biodiversity on the Cork Waterways

description:

The exhibition explores symbolic connections between people, place, and memory through the ancient technique of encaustic painting – combining beeswax, pigments, natural materials, and layered textures.
The work will draw inspiration from the Longford landscape, its mythology, and personal narratives connected to the land. Pieces will be small to medium in scale and displayed in an intimate, reflective setting that invites visitors to engage with themes of time, loss, regeneration, and rootedness.
A key participatory feature of the evening will be the Wishing Wall – where members of the public are invited to write a memory, wish, or reflection on small waxed paper slips and pin them to a communal board, which becomes part of the evolving artwork. The artist will be present throughout the evening to talk informally about the encaustic process and answer questions.
This event aims to create a warm, sensory-rich experience that connects people with traditional techniques in a contemporary and accessible way. It will be family-friendly, drop-in, and suitable for all ages.

title: Neil Ó Lochlainn’s Emain Ablach
description:
Clare musician and composer Neil Ó Lochlainn’s ‘Emain Abhlach’ is an imagined Irish mythological tale

expressed through a suite of music in three movements with an interwoven text by acclaimed Irish poet Aifric Mac Aodha. Having researched and analysed a wide range of early Irish writing both ancient myth and medieval legend, Neil has re-taken the essence of these stories and re-presented it for modern sensibilities in a musical suite of 75 minutes duration.

In mythological writing, Emain Ablach is one of many names for the otherworld, the lands inhabited by the fairy people. In keeping with many early Irish stories, this music is structured around a hero’s journey to the otherworld, their adventures there, and their eventual return. To do justice to the fullness of the drama demanded by and the multiple parts involved in such a narrative, Neil has put together a thrilling ensemble consisting of many of Ireland’s leading performers from a wide variety of musical backgrounds. He commissioned poet Aifric Mac Aodha to compose a poetic sequence based on his imagined story and this is blended into the suite.

The music is rooted in the language of traditional Irish dance music and song (sean-nós) while taking in other musical influences (jazz, minimalism, west african music, contemporary classical music) as well to create something original and innovative. The band assembled to perform the piece features a mixture of many of the most accomplished and exciting traditional musicians from Ireland today and also some of the most highly regarded musicians from jazz and creative music scenes across Europe.

The suite was premiered in Galway and Dublin in November 2023 and this Culture Night performance will see the Clare premiere.

title: New Skin
description: This work in progress represents the new topographics in process and the idea of the interminable continuum of time. Holding you in the moment of incompleteness and the possibilities of new interconnectivity. Using the construction sector as a source as it represents the most physical attributes of a time. Sequent occupance the idea that slowly dissipates the past further out of view, and the new that shares a familiarity but is not entirely the same. This is a layered art installation with a primary focus on photography, with real time recent and current observations in the sector. This installation consists of mixed materials (paper, card, wood, rock, print) representing the idiocracy of time and place. The best identifier of time is marked by its aesthetics, which are only temporal. Also a psychogeography of the new landscape, in states that go mostly underrepresented, highlighting time continuum and the temporal nature of life, where nothing is eternal in the physicality of the man made. This is a continual subject in Michael’s works, the in between, in various aspects of the everyday, poetics of the real. A dynamic and interesting piece work, attentive to contemporary Ireland, in where we are today, where dreams and realities are mixed.

title: New Work Showcase
description:

Barry McKinley – Literary Reading
Writer Barry McKinley will share a reading from his upcoming novel, MANHATTAN LOVERS, offering audiences a preview of a chapter ahead of its publication. This session will provide an opportunity to hear directly from the author and gain insight into his writing process and narrative approach.

Deirdre Fleming – Solo Performance
Performer Deirdre Fleming will present her new solo piece, THE BOY. This original work explores a range of emotional and thematic material through Fleming’s distinctive theatrical style, offering audiences a personal and reflective performance.

Izzy Santina – Musical Performance
Singer-songwriter Izzy Santina, originally from New York and now living in Carlow, will perform a selection of her own songs. Drawing on both her American and Irish influences, Santina’s music offers a blend of perspectives shaped by her diverse background.

title: Nezlamni, live in concert
description:
The Ensemble Незламні project is a joint collaboration between Westport Welcomes Ukraine and one of their volunteers, Ian Leslie: musician/Music therapist/ Guided Imagery and Music therapist.

In 2023 singers and musicians from Ukraine, living in the Westport area, were invited to form a music ensemble with the intention of meeting to play music together and performing live at various local events and venues. The response to the invitation was such that a professional level ensemble, Ensemble Незламні (Unbreakable), was formed and we have been rehearsing and performing since. In 2024 the ensemble developed to collaborate with Irish musicians for further projects.

This ensemble of talented singers and musicians from Ukraine and Ireland presents an exciting cross-cultural experience for Culture Night patrons. The concert offers an eclectic mix of folk and contemporary music selections from both countries, featuring innovative original arrangements.

In the past 2 years the ensemble has performed at a wide range of events, including concerts at music festivals such as Westival, The Clare Island Folk Festival and The National Fleadh Ceol.

In addition to this, the ensemble has featured in a number of newspaper and magazine articles in The Mayo news and The Mayo Yearbook. The ensemble in a special 2-hour program on MidWest Radio during Christmas week 2023. They performed live on TG4 at The national Fleadh Ceol in Wexford, 2024, which included a film of the story of the ensemble.

title: Niamh Regan
description:
Niamh Regan’s Pavilion Theatre debut promises an intimate evening with an artist at the height of her powers, offering Culture Night audiences a rare opportunity to experience one of Ireland’s finest voices in a uniquely up-close setting.

With her 2024 album Come As You Are, Niamh Regan confirmed her place as one of Ireland’s most compelling songwriters. Nominated for the RTÉ Choice Prize for Irish Album of the Year, the record showcases Regan’s gift for raw honesty and intricate storytelling, pairing delicate folk instrumentation with lush, cinematic soundscapes. Produced by Tommy McLaughlin (Attica Studios), it’s a deeply personal collection that invites listeners to reflect on life’s uncertainties, relationships, and self-acceptance.

Since the release of her acclaimed debut Hemet (2020), which earned nominations for both the RTÉ Folk Awards and the Choice Music Prize, Regan has toured widely across Ireland, the UK, Australia and beyond, sharing stages with CMAT, Villagers, John Grant, SOAK, Patrick Watson, James Vincent McMorrow and Sam Amidon.

This tour will cover early policing in Ireland from the days of the Night-Watchman, the establishment of An Garda Síochána in 1922, right up to the high-tech aspects of modern day policing in Ireland.

title: NIGHT MOVES CULTURE NIGHT LATE NIGHT
description:

Aligned with the Late-Night Events strategy, this dynamic programme is designed to build on the success of the recent NIGHT Moves programme over 2024 and 2025, & will further provide new & engaging intergenerational night time cultural experiences in Drogheda across accessible public & shared spaces, Ambitious, innovative and experimental supporting artists & creatives, and in partnership with a variety of businesses and buildings. Encapsulating our joint vision of extending cultural offerings, fostering partnerships, & creating diverse opportunities for artists & audiences alike, with a variety of programmes across the town for audiences. From 9.30pm – til late.

 

NIGHT POOLS: a light installation trail by artist Vivienne Byrne. Using video projection, sound and light sculpture, the richness of the natural habitats will be celebrated. Five outdoor urban projections will be presented in varying sizes and shapes, ranging from small, watery pools of light to large, single projections. The projections will link aesthetically as one travels across town from the Georgian architecture of Barlow House in Narrow West Street to the Georgian-inspired Clarke House with projections on the pavement, to Patrickswell Lane, Droichead Arts Centre & the Ulster Bank, culminating with a nature-inspired large light sculpture outside the former Methodist Church at Laurence Street and bringing light to dark spaces, urban living with rural landscape offering a fresh narrative for Drogheda. The installation of over 20 lanterns in shop fronts will accompany the trail.

title: North Main St. SC Car Park: Kaught At The Karpark
description:
Cork City was a cultural hotbed of Irish absurdist music back in the late 70’s and early 80’s. Bands like Nun Attax (5 Go Down to the Sea), Microdisney and Stump honed their – wonderfully bizarre – craft in the Arcadia on the Lower Road, when Elvera Butler hosted gigs in the Downtown Kampus.

Celebrating these hugely influential artists of Cork’s punk/post-punk period, Kaught at the Karpark is more than simply a lookback to the glory days. It will also showcase current music by band members who are working musicians today, and of course celebrate those like Mick Lynch, Finbarr Donnelly and Cathal Coughlan, gone but not forgotten, who left an indelible mark on their home town.

Presented by Seanie Buttons with Leagues O’Toole of Foggy Notions, these (free) tickets will be snapped up by both those who remember this heyday and by new audiences curious about this significant phase of Cork’s musical heritage.

Performances include Big Boy Foolish, Sean O’Hagan …and NUN came back.

description:
Ó GHLÚIN GO GLÚIN’  – Ceiliúradh ar an nGaeilge agus an Cultúr Gaelach – An intergenerational celebration of Irish language and Gaelic Culture.’

Cuirfear tús leis an oíche le togha an cheoil  ó dhaltaí  scoile ó Nás na Ríogh. Ina dhiaidh sin, beidh deis ag an bpobal steipeanna damhsa ar an sean-nós a fhoghlaim ón sárdhamhsóir, Nada Ní Chuirrín agus ansin, déanfaidh an t-amhránaí clúiteach, Féilim MacDonncha ceardlann amhránaíochta ar an sean-nós. Cuirfear focail agus treoir foghraíochta ar fáil. Seinnfidh grúpa ceoil traidisiúnta John McNamaras’s rogha poirt chun clabhsúr a chur leis an oíche álainn seo. Hup! Tapaigh an deis!

Arna eagrú ag Seirbhís Leabharlainne Chill Dara i gcomhar le hOireachtas na Gaeilge.

 

The evening will begin with the best of music from schoolchildren from Nás na Ríogh. Afterwards, the audience  will have the opportunity to learn sean-nós dance steps from the brilliant Nada Ní Chuirrín and then, the renowned singer, Féilim MacDonncha, will facilitate a sean-nós singing workshop. Words and pronunciation guides will be provided. John McNamaras’s traditional music group will play a selection of tunes to polish off this beautiful evening. Hup! Not to be missed!

Brought to you by Kildare Library Service in partnership with Oireachtas na Gaeilge.

description:
The newly launched International Centre for the Image celebrates Culture Night with a vibrant evening of exhibitions and events at Coopers Cross. Visitors are invited to explore Foreword, a major group exhibition featuring works by 17 Irish and international artists. 

The exhibition will be accompanied by the following programme of events:

Location: Kinsale Museum

Time: 5:00 – 8:00 PM

Step inside one of Kinsale’s oldest buildings for a captivating journey through time at Kinsale Museum. Located in the heart of the town and housed in a 400-year-old former market house and courthouse, the museum offers a unique glimpse into the stories, people, and events that have shaped the region.

Wander through an eclectic collection of historical artefacts and curiosities, each one offering a window into Kinsale’s colourful past — from maritime adventures to everyday life in centuries gone by.

Whether you’re a history buff, a curious visitor, or a local wanting to reconnect with the town’s heritage, this after-hours opening is a perfect opportunity to explore the museum in a relaxed, atmospheric setting.

Free entry | All welcome

title: Open Studio Night at Touch Design Ceramics
description:
At Touch Design Ceramics beautiful, functional pottery is made entirely by hand by Radek Zemlicka, a
second-generation Czech potter who has continued his family’s craft in Ireland since 2005.
Meet Radek in his historic pottery studio, on Balbriggan’s main street, for a live demonstration of wheel
throwing, the traditional technique he uses to transform a ball of clay into a bowl, cup or lighthouse!
Tour his pottery production from pugmill, to wheel, to kiln, to firing to finished piece. Radek has created
many bespoke orders over the years from a dinner service to a mini Taj Mahal to funeral urns to tea sets
to fairy houses! He has become best known for his handmade catering supplies and of course his iconic
lighthouses inspired by our built heritage.
Your visit ends with a tour of his finished pieces in his studio shop – and a chance to find out about his
pottery workshops.

title: Órchloch – Alchemy
description:
The Painted Pot: Órcloch – From Earth to Art

Órcloch (literally meaning “gold stone”) speaks to the alchemy at the heart of ceramics. Through fire and craft, humble clay is transformed into something precious. Pottery is not only a functional art form, requiring technical skill and precision, but also a deeply expressive medium where design, form, and personality converge.

Every pot begins as earth. In the hands of a skilled maker, it becomes more than a vessel—it becomes a story. Handles are tested for strength, forms refined for purpose, and every surface bears the intentional touch of the artist. From nature-inspired works to playful character pieces and sleek modern designs, each creation is a reflection of the maker’s vision and individuality.

The Painted Pot exhibition, presented by Newcastle West Arts at the Red Door Gallery, showcases a vibrant collection of ceramic works by local artists. Incorporating both traditional hand-building and wheel-thrown techniques, this diverse exhibition celebrates the transformation of clay into crafted beauty, stone into gold.

title: Our Crucial Callows
description:
The art exhibition “Our Crucial Callows” is inspired by the natural beauty and biodiversity of the the wetlands known as the callows (from the Irish word caladh). The regular and substantial flooding of these lliminal spaces between the river and dry land, makes them exceptional in many regards.  The callows are home to a wide variety of plant, animal and bird life.  Many of these are scarce species which risk being lost forever if their habitat is not respected and protected. The exhibition will contain work in various art forms created using a variety of media including paint, print, recycled fabric, home-made charcoal, photography and 3D sculptures.

The artist is excited to present this evolving body of work on Culture Night 2025 and hopes it will evoke a sense of wonder, admiration and desire to look anew at these local wetlands.  Visitors are encouraged both to celebrate our callows and also to consider how we may all play a part in the preservation of these critical and remarkable features.

title: Outdoor Screening: Rear Window
description:
What does a neighbourhood sound like when you really listen? The life of the community is revealed through the noises that drift into open windows and across shared courtyards. Join us for a special outdoor screening of Alfred Hitchcock’s Rear Window (1954) – presented in collaboration with Excite WNP and Waterside Together.

The screening will be introduced by a short audiovisual piece created by young people in the community, using field recordings to build a sound map of the city—inviting us to listen more deeply to the places we live.

In Rear Window, a photographer who is forced to stay at home with a broken leg, begins spying on his neighbours from his apartment window. As he pieces together stories from glimpses and sounds, suspicion grows that something sinister has happened. The film uses snippets of conversations; footsteps, drifting music, clinking dishes, laughter, arguments—and sudden silence—to guide our attention to the life of a tightly packed urban community, turning the neighbourhood itself into a living, breathing character.

This screening is part of an Outdoor Cinema Programme that is being run as part of Waterside Together, a shared green spaces events and festival project which aims to reanimate spaces that are perceived as belonging to the ‘other community’, transforming them into areas that are open, welcoming, and safe for all members of the Waterside community. Programmes will be delivered in parks, greenways and community spaces, targeting a range of participants including families, children and young people, older people, and members of the BAME community.

This project is supported by PEACEPLUS, a programme managed by the Special EU Programmes Body (SEUPB) and funded under the theme of Community Regeneration and Transformation, and it is also funded through Derry City and Strabane District Council’s PEACEPLUS Local Co-Designed Action Plan.

The Excite Project programmes classes, courses, and activities to give young people the opportunity to experiment and develop creatively and shape their future through multimedia, art, and creative technologies. It is run as part of Waterside Neighbourhood Partnership, who deliver programmes and training for people living in Waterside Neighbourhood renewal areas.

Step inside one of Ireland’s most significant historic buildings this Culture Night with guided tours of Leinster House, the home of the Oireachtas, comprising Dáil Éireann and Seanad Éireann.

Located in the heart of Dublin, Leinster House was originally built in the mid-18th century as the townhouse of James Fitzgerald, the Earl of Kildare and first Duke of Leinster. Designed by renowned architect Richard Castle, the building features classical Palladian architecture, including a grand double-height hall and picture gallery.

On the night, visitors will have the unique opportunity to explore the Dáil and Seanad chambers, as well as the beautifully restored Georgian interiors following a major conservation project completed in 2019.

With something for everyone, this special evening of culture and heritage is open to all: families, history lovers, and curious visitors alike are warmly welcomed.

title: Plants Fantastic – tales of innovation and evolution at Trinity College Botanic Garden
description:
Trinity College Dublin Discipline of Botany are delighted to invite you to celebrate Culture Night 2025 at Trinity College Botanic Garden with a guided exploration of the amazing world of plants. This is a great opportunity to learn the history of this unique teaching, research and conservation facility and see the diverse collection of plants from around the world. Trinity’s botanists will regale you with stories about the fascinating lives of plants, how they have innovated, evolved and adapted in sometimes extreme environments, and what they can teach us about the atmosphere we all inhabit.

Meet the ‘Witness Trees’ and hear how they absorb vital climate change information through their leaves; learn how insect-eating plants can have their pollinators, and eat them too! Plus, see other amazing plants older than the dinosaurs and hear how they survived extinction.

Tour numbers will be limited due to space constraints, so please register early, and remember: if you change your mind, please release your space for someone else.

If you prefer, you may wander the Garden at your own pace using our printed guides. There is an arboretum with many mature trees, a sheltered walled garden, and several glasshouses with plants from tropical cloud forests and arid deserts; there are quiet places to sit and a sensory trail which can be followed by accessing the Garden’s website.

Whichever way you choose to enjoy it, Trinity College Botanic Garden welcomes you on Culture Night.

title: Poets & Makers | The Makers House
description:
Our first Culture Night in our new location on The Boardwalk, Crescent Quay will be special.
This year we have invited local poets, Conor Daniel Lyons, Margaret Galvin and Mary Wallace to join our Makers John Sinnott, Annette Byrne, Mairead Stafford and Emma Phillips.

Also on the night you can view ‘Along the edge’, an exhibition inspired by the Raven Point by local artist John Cullen.

The Makers House is a true reflection of the cultural richness of Wexford. Our Makers hail from all corners of the county and our aim is to bring awareness of the arts, crafts
and design that make up the heritage of our county. Our hope is to encourage others to get involved and take part.

Programme of Events

Meet The Makers
5:30pm – 7pm

John Sinnott
John will introduce you to the mysteries of discovering a beautiful wooden bowl hidden within
a block of wood. Curious about the various types of wood he uses? How he ‘knows’ what to
find inside? All will be revealed in a talk and video presentation.
Annette Byrne, Julsuluv
Annette will talk about finding inspiration for her jewellery making. A demonstration on how
to begin and end off a necklace – clasp crimp and cover – to give a nice finish.

7pm – 8:30pm

Mairead Stafford
An interesting look at how patterns and textures can be made using found materials. Some
of Mairead’s techniques will surprise you.
Emma Phillips
Curious to know how Emma achieves the super-real finish to her animal portraits? Watch
her fascinating pastel drawing techniques as she creates life-like textures of animal fur.

Meet The Poets
6:30pm

Conor Daniel Lyons

Conor explores nostalgia – as it pertains to our own personal experiences and memories and also in broader societal sense. How nostalgia can be a way to connect with the past and history, as well as being a remedy to the chaos of the modern world. He tries to come to terms with how nostalgia can sustain us through hardship but can sometimes be an illusion that serves to halt real progress.

7pm

Margaret Galvin

Margaret’s writing is very accessible, rooted in the ordinary and the everyday. Her reading

from ‘The Creative Impulse’ will include a poem about a Polish immigrant in a fish factory
who longs to make it known that she’s a ballroom dancer at competition level in her native
country; and then there’s the checkout girl in Supervalu who can’t wait to clock off to get
back to her painting of hummingbirds.

7:30pm

Mary Wallace

Mary will make her debut to read from her collection of Morning Köans. Since 10th
November 2020 she has written a three line response to the morning sky. Written from the
bottom up, just as she looks to the sky – horizon first then up and up! This has become a
delightful morning routine with not a day missed.

John Cullen’s exhibition ALONG THE EDGE

title: Put Your Soul on Your Hand and Walk
description: Put Your Soul on Your Hand and Walk offers an intimate, first-hand perspective of life in Gaza, told through a series of video calls between filmmaker Sepideh Farsi and young Palestinian photojournalist Fatma Hassona. Their digital dialogue became a vital record, bearing witness to everyday life, loss, and acts of resistance amid escalating violence. Just a day after the film’s selection at Cannes, Fatma was tragically killed in an Israeli airstrike on her home. This heartbreaking loss deepens the film’s impact, which combines raw immediacy with profound humanity to portray the stark realities of daily life during conflict, seen through the eyes of those trapped in an endless cycle of war and living under siege.

title: Pygmalion’s Statue is a Lolita
description:
A haunting, dialogue-free short film that reimagines grooming as the act of sculpting. Pygmalion’s Statue Is a Lolita follows an adult woman shaped into a fetish by a controlling older man. Through faceless compositions, static frames, and symbolic imagery, the film critiques the male gaze, objectification, and the violence beneath aesthetic obsession. As the sculptor’s fantasy unravels, the statue begins to break, flee, and reclaim herself. A dark feminist reckoning with silence, power, and the myth of transformation where creation is control, and escape is the only act of selfhood.

Trigger Warning: Contains depictions of grooming, coercion, and implied sexual violence. Viewer discretion is strongly advised.
fullAddress: The Garage Theatre, Campus Old, Armagh Road, Knockaconny, Monaghan, Ireland

Let yourself be transported by the delicate interplay of voice and viol in an intimate setting that highlights the charm and grace of this historic repertoire.

title: QueerVerse – a Celebration of LGBTQIA+ Poets
description:
8*pm Glor Studio Theatre

Join Quare Clare – Clare’s LGBTQIA + support and social group as they kick off Clare Pride Weekend 2025 and celebrate Culture Night in Glor Studio Theatre with an evening of poetry and craic.

This hugely popular event returns for its third year as part of Culture Night in Ennis and will continue to bring some of the very best LGBTQIA+ poets to Clare audiences. There will be three guest poets who will all read or perform a selection of their work followed by a limited ‘open-mic’ session where local writers can put their names down to read a poem of their own.  This event will be MC’d by Clare- based poet and community worker Sarah Clancy.

Our invited guests are

Sonia Mulligan who runs the Pride Poets Monthly Reading Series in Dublin and who is a poet, a painter, a director, producer and a crafter. She has had her poetry published in various publications including the recent Pride Poets Anthology and Washing Windows III from Arlen House.

Gráinnemir Abualrob is a queer Palestinian Performer and theatre-maker based in Ireland. In 2013 they joined the Freedom Theatre in Jenin Refugee Camp, Palestine, where they completed four years of Theatre and Cultural Resistance study. Gráinnemir’s performances reflect their experiences as a queer Palestinian, navigating both their heritage and identity in Ireland, creating thought provoking theatre and spoken word that connect diverse cultural contexts and highlight struggles of resistance. We are extremely lucky that Gráinnemir will be joined by Sorcha Fox, the renowned and much loved actor, writer, director and facilitator who was a co-director of Benbo Productions with Donal O’Kelly. She also attended a course in the Freedom Theatre in Jenin and regularly collaborates with Gráinnemir and has twice been awarded an Arts Council Bursary for her performance poetry.

Rafael Mendes is a Brazilian-Irish migrant whose work has recently appeared or is upcoming in Poetry Ireland Review, Propel Magazine, and Poetry Salzburg Review. He is a PhD candidate in Latin American Studies at Trinity College Dublin and a creative writing workshop facilitator. They are  the author of ‘The Migrant Dictionary’ one of two poetry collections published this year by The Ireland Chair of Poetry Trust.

title: Race and Place in the City – Culture Night Special
description:
Using stories of local buildings and places, Richard Carson invites participants to reimagine our relationship with the place and with one another on this tour for Culture Night 2025. Using history, theology and more, the group will encounter how the colonial imagination was established in the place of the north east inner city and is still yet to be exorcised. 

A local wedding that united two settings of 19th-century colonialism from opposite sides of the world and how what happened at the site of Store St. Garda Station over 250 years ago reminds us that so-called “new communities” are not so new after all – just two of many unexpected stories to be encountered on the night.

This 90-minute walking tour of Lower Gardiner Street and its laneways has featured on RTÉ Lyric FM, Culture Night 2023-2024 and with numerous schools, colleges and community groups.

Heralded by previous attendees as: “Mind blowing”, “Brilliant”, “I will never look at these streets the same again.”

title: Recital on Carillon of St. Colman’s Cathedral, Cobh
description: Adrian Gebruers, Cobh Cathedral Carillonneur, will present a recital of some of his favorite music on the instrument he loves. Over a hundred years ago, Most Rev. Dr Robert Browne, Bishop of Cloyne, commissioned a grand carillon from the bell-founders John Taylor & Son of Loughborough (England) to be the crowning glory of his magnificent new St Colman’s Cathedral. This unique instrument is played from a console within the belfry consisting of a keyboard and a pedalboard. Carillon bells do not move in performance – the clappers, which are connected by direct mechanical linkage to the keys and pedals of the console, move to strike the bell. Hence, this is a percussion instrument which is completely touch responsive to give the carillonneur full capability for every musical expression from a gentle whisper to a thundering fortissimo. This Carillon boasts 49 accurately tuned bronze cast bells, i.e. four chromatic octaves, with a total weight of 26 tons including the heaviest belt in Ireland at 3.6 tons. It is the largest such instrument in these islands in terms of numbers of bells. In 2019 “Cobh Carillon Playing” was added to Ireland’s National Inventory of Intangible Cultural Heritage. Particularly good listening places are the Memorial Garden across the road from the main Cathedral entrance and the car park to the north of the Cathedral.
fullAddress: Saint Colman's Cathedral, Cathedral Place, Kilgarvan, Cobh, County Cork, Ireland

title: Remote Association – Exhibition at TØN
description:
TØN Dublin is proud to present Remote Association, an exhibition by Norwegian contemporary painter Kyrre Mogster, whose work explores themes of transcendence and duality. Mogster’s practice draws on historical approaches to painting, with an emphasis on colour, composition, light, and texture.

Born in Stord, Norway, in 1985, Mogster spent his early years in a fishing community before moving with his family to Seattle, USA. This dual heritage—rooted in Nordic landscapes yet shaped by international perspectives—infuses his work with depth and resonance.

From an early age Mogster has been interested in the details and patterns in nature and everyday life. His point of departure might be a remote fjord in Norway, but his work glides throughout art history, onboarding the nuance of landscape and society and lands with a vitality and confidence that can only be achieved by coming home after a long and arduous journey.

title: Rooms of the Unspoken
description:
Rooms of the Unspoken

This series is part of an innovative multidisciplinary project exploring the intersection of painting, music composition, and somatic experience. Developed from PhD research in music composition, the project bridges a gap between visual, physical, and sonic practices.

Each painting inspires a corresponding composition, created through sessions that integrate movement, colour, and sound. Recordings of the artist   painting, recalling gestures, textures, and bodily sensations are examined, then translated these into musical language through acoustic and electronic means. The result is a unified sensory installation: ten large scale paintings exhibited alongside ten new compositions.

Each painting opens a door into a world that feels both familiar and dreamlike. Domestic spaces (bedrooms, dining tables, hospital wards) are tilted toward something extraordinary. A figure floats upward through a burning doorway; a man in a hospital bed merges with moss and butterflies; a woman slices a tomato under the watch of a priest and a police officer. These works belong to Magic Realism for their insistence that hidden lives exist within the ordinary. A kitchen can carry the weight of a secret; a shared dinner can reveal the deathly silence between two people. The glowing rose dress of a woman beside a grieving man becomes both a shroud and a field of memory.

Threaded through all these images is a meditation on intimacy and estrangement. The paintings ask: what is hidden in our most private rooms? How do lovers, family, strangers coexist when grief, desire, and memory haunt the air? Technology intrudes, rituals repeat, people vanish or transform before our eyes, and yet we go on sitting at tables, scrolling through our phones, feeding children, watching ships sink through glass walls.

title: RTÉ Concert Orchestra with special guest Patrick Dexter – Cellist
description:
Dublin City Council and NEIC (North East Inner City) invites you to a unique one off event for Culture Night Dublin 2025. Dublin’s North Inner City will resonate with the sound of world-class music as the RTÉ Concert Orchestra joins forces with acclaimed Irish cellist Patrick Dexter for a special free performance at Our Lady of Lourdes Church, Sean McDermott Street.

This early-evening concert will feature 45 musicians performing a specially curated programme that blends classical and Irish traditional influences. Patrick Dexter, who won global acclaim during lockdown with his soulful outdoor performances from his West of Ireland cottage, will bring his signature style to the stage. His debut album Solace reached No. 15 in the US and Canadian charts, captivating millions of listeners worldwide.

Our Lady of Lourdes Church, a neo-Romanesque landmark with deep historical and spiritual roots, provides a unique backdrop for this cultural celebration. From its beginnings as a tin chapel in 1915 to its dedication in 1961 and its strong legacy of community solidarity and addiction recovery support, the church is both a spiritual and social cornerstone of Dublin’s North Inner City.

Event Highlights:

RTÉ Concert Orchestra – 45 musicians live in Dublin’s North Inner City

Patrick Dexter – celebrated Irish cellist performing alongside the orchestra

Cultural landmark setting – the historic Our Lady of Lourdes Church

About the Venue:

Since the early 1990s, Our Lady of Lourdes has been cared for by the Salesians of Don Bosco, who anchor its mission in addiction recovery, youth outreach, and community solidarity. With its connections to Venerable Matt Talbot, papal visits, and its enduring service to the community, the church remains both spiritually significant and socially inspiring.

Doors 18:00

title: Rustle of Reeds
description:
The Rustle of Reeds workshop celebrates traditional folk strawcraft, and how many societies have strawcraft as part of their cultural activities. While seeking for ways to connect with nature, and to be more mindful in designing and sourcing materials to be creative, we can draw inspiration from the rural folk calendars and the crafts and celebrations involved.

The Irish folk tradition through the use of harvest knots, St Bridgid’s crosses and Wren boys has been a huge inspiration to the workshop. Combining the Irish strawplait with hanging elements of delicate European straw ornaments, the workshop visitors will create their own pieces of folkcraft, straw and reed braided accessories following the tradition of the last sheaf worn on the shoulders to celebrate the harvest. (This can also be created as a headpiece or ornament if needed.)

Straw braid is embellished with ornamental and traditional straw stars and threaded trimmings, using linen thread, needles and Co.Limerick reeds and straw. This workshop is suitable for beginners, but has great potential with more experienced braiding crafters. The Rustle of Reeds workshop will also offer a great opportunity to collect folklore on the straw craft during the event.

SECONDS is a play written by Ciara O’Grady and debuting at the Edinburgh Fringe Festival. Sandra is a first-time mother living rurally, her vision for motherhood not going as planned, marred by colic and harbouring a secret. Jenny is heartbroken and cynical, reeling from a failed romance she thought would last forever. What binds them?

Doors at 7:00pm

Run time 55minutes
fullAddress: Moanmore, County Kerry, V92 YW10, Ireland

title: Secrets of Dublin: Hidden History Walking Tour
description:
Step off the tourist trail and into the heart of Dublin’s lesser-known past with the Hidden History Walking Tour. Led by a passionate local guide, this immersive journey reveals the city’s forgotten corners and untold stories—from ghostly encounters and dramatic train crashes to Nobel laureates and curious quirks of civic life.

Uncover the astonishing tale of the 1900 Valentine’s Day train crash on Harcourt Street, explore the enduring appeal of St Stephen’s Green, and learn how Dublin once had its own time zone—and the man who tried to change it.

This tour offers a fresh and surprising perspective on the city, ideal for both history buffs and the simply curious. Join us this Culture Night and see Dublin’s streets come alive with stories rarely told.

This tour begins at the main, Grafton Street entrance to St. Stephens Green.

Booking for this event will go live with the full Dublin City programme launch at 10am on 19 August.
fullAddress: 23 St Stephen's Green, Dublin, Ireland

title: Seeds of Harmony: A Cultural Night of Song, Community, and New Beginnings – Mercy Centre, Mallow
description:
Join us as we sow the first seeds of a vibrant future at the launch of our Community Garden Project — a blank canvas poised to blossom with life, creativity, and community spirit. While the garden is just in its infancy, this special evening invites everyone to imagine what can grow when hands and hearts come together. As part of Cork County Council’s Culture Night, this event celebrates not just the promise of green spaces, but the rich cultural fabric that binds our community.

At the heart of the evening’s program is a live performance by OTOV, the multicultural choir whose harmonies span continents and traditions. Their singing reflects the diversity and unity that the future garden hopes to cultivate. Together, we’ll celebrate the beginning of something beautiful — a space that will soon nourish both body and soul. Come and be part of this inspiring launch — a celebration of community, culture, and the fertile ground of possibility.

title: Self Guided Tour of Church
description:
This architecturally unusual church in the centre of Monkstown Village dates from 1789 and was radically extended by John Semple & Son in 1830. Semple also designed churches at Whitechurch, Kilternan, Tallaght, St Mary’s Chapel of Ease (Black Church), Abbeyleix and Killeshin. When opened on Christmas Day 1831, the Dublin Penny Journal claimed that ‘there was not a spot in the church where the eye can rest without pain’! One hundred years later Sir John Betjeman described it as ‘a cheerful Irish castle with a seaside rather than a fortress flavour’.

 

We invite you to come and visit the church and decide for yourself whether the above descriptions adequately describe this extraordinary building. The church is partially wheelchair accessible, and free guide leaflets, quizzes for adults and treasure hunts and quizzes for children will be available.
fullAddress: Monkstown Church of Ireland, Monkstown Road, Dún Laoghaire, Monkstown, County Dublin, Ireland

title: Self-Guided Tour of Christ Church Cathedral | 16:00
description:
This Culture Night, explore the awe-inspiring Christ Church Cathedral, Dublin’s oldest working structure, at your own pace with a captivating self-guided audio tour. Using vivid storytelling and rich soundscapes, the guide brings nearly 1,000 years of history to life — from Viking origins to medieval grandeur and beyond — offering a fresh and engaging way to experience this iconic landmark. Visitors are able to choose from three different themes as they explore: ‘Power and Politics’, ‘Christ Church & the City’ and ‘Music & Spirituality’.

This audio tour is offered in 7 languages; English, French, German, Spanish, Polish, Portuguese and Italian. Irish Sign Language and Audio Descriptive tours are also available with transcriptions (in English only). Please download the audio guide onto your own device and bring your earphones/headphones. There is a limit of 200 spaces available for each self-guided tour and they must be pre-booked in advance. The audio guide must be downloaded onto your own device as physical devices will not be available on the night. The tour lasts approx. 45 minutes. Latecomers will not be admitted. There are no bathroom facilities on site.

title: Set Dancing Ceilidh with Theresa and her Kilchreest Straw Boys
description: The Kilchreest Straw Boys will host a night of fun and revelry with a set dancing evening open to the public. The dancing will be led by music and dance teacher Theresa Reilly. Beginning with the introduction of basic jig and reel steps, Theresa will then teach the Connemara Set, interspersed with more well-known dances, such as Shoe the Donkey and Siege of Ennis. The 16-member straw boys team will assist in bringing all participants out onto the dance floor. Live set dancing music will be provided by local traditional musicians. In the spirit of Straw Boys our group will dress up in old fashioned, weird and wonderful clothes, with some more wacky items being purchased from local charity shops. Dance brings out fun and spontaneity in everybody and links with Ireland’s rich heritage of dance, connecting with tradition and passing on cultural assets to our local community.

title: Sharon Slater talk & Ormston House late opening
description:
For Culture Night 2025, Ormston House is delighted to extend our opening hours to 9pm. The exhibition, Bíodh Orm Anocht, developed in partnership with the 41st edition of EVA International, be in situ. This exhibition brings together four artists, Laura Ní Fhlaibhín, Sean Hannan, Kiera O’Toole, and Cirarán Ó Dochartaigh, unified by shared approaches and sensibilities. A poetic, organic minimalism distinguishes their work, and there is a propensity towards using natural materials. This exhibition demonstrates how places and things are capable of holding and transmitting other-worldly forces.
To compliment the exhibition, historian Sharon Slater will lead a walk and talk, starting at Ormston House moving to the old St. Micheal’s Cemetary at Charlotte’s Quay. This historic cemetery is largely unknown to Limerick citizens and Sharon will share knowledge of the history of the site and of the people who now rest there. The talk will take place from 5-6pm and will start at Ormston House and then making the way to St. Micheal’s Cemetery on foot.
fullAddress: Ormston House, Cultural Resource Centre, Patrick Street, Prior's-Land, Limerick, Ireland

title: SHE.S
description:
‘SHE.S’ Photography Exhibition
Titled “SHE.S,” this photography exhibition weaves a visual narrative, exploring the inherent power of women within the landscapes of Ireland and France. Each shot reveals a connection to nature, embodying a quiet yet powerful strength. It’s an invitation to an immersive journey through magnificent locations.
Accessible to all, this project is a unique artistic contribution, celebrating the profound interaction between identity, environment, and the place of women in society.
SHE.S is a double entendre: it literally means “she is” and “she has.” Additionally, it’s a direct reference to the French word “elles,” the feminine plural for “they,” highlighting the collective female presence.

title: Shorts for Families
description:
Colourful, imaginative, intriguing, amusing, moving… this collection of short films for those aged eight and above is all of that and much more.

The films in this year’s programme are from France, Portugal, Brazil, Mexico and the UK and present an eclectic mix of styles ranging from watercolour, cut outs, stop-motion, hand-drawn and 2D computer animation. Equally diverse are the array of stories here which promise to entertain and enchant children and adults alike.

There are stories of little girls whose imaginations take them to fantastic places; one absorbed by a book that becomes a forest of printed knowledge while the other’s drawings magically come to life, helping her to process difficult emotions. There are also stories of children whose connection to animals (a rat and a crab) help them understand something significant about themselves. And in a summer campsite, a little boy laughs at couples kissing; however, he secretly wants to give it a try…

Nearly all the films are dialogue free, with one in French language and another one with a brief line of poetry in Spanish.

title: Sing and Sign Athy present ‘Remarkable Women of Ireland’
description:
Join Sing and Sign Athy this Culture Night as they celebrate the remarkable women who have shaped modern Ireland. Inspired by Jennifer O’Connell’s article in The Irish Times, the event pays tribute to 25 fearless women who challenged stereotypes, broke barriers, and transformed Irish society — yet many remain overlooked by history. Through creative expression, they created a striking figurine made of chicken wire and paper mache, symbolising these inspiring women. Participants will also have the opportunity to write down the names of women who inspire them on banners and displays, fostering a sense of community and shared history. This event aims to raise awareness of the vital contributions women have made to Ireland’s cultural, social, and political landscape. Come and celebrate these trailblazers, learn their stories, and reflect on the ongoing journey towards equality and recognition. All ages are welcome to participate in this empowering and inspiring evening.

With an ISL Interpreter.

title: Singing for the Soul
description:
Taking place in the intimate setting of the former Mount Carmel Monastery, Galway County Integration Team are delighted to bring prominent Community Choir Director, Róisín Mulliez to Culture Night 2025. As an established jazz vocalist, choir director and music educator operating out of Galway City, Róisín brings a rich mix of passion, experience and accessibility to her work. Helping participants to find their voice in a communal group setting, this workshop will allow attendees to embrace the joy of singing in an open and organic setting.

The Singing for the Soul project is a 2-hour workshop where Róisín will guide participants through a welcoming and nourishing evening of singing. The session begins with a grounding exercise to calm the mind and bring everyone’s attention into their breath and body. From there, Róisín leads playful vocal warm-ups and group activities that help participants let go of tension.

The main part of the workshop focuses on learning a handful of songs drawn from folk, bluegrass, and gospel traditions. These songs are carefully chosen to be easy to learn, with simple harmonies that allow everyone – regardless of experience – to join in. By the end of the session, participants will have learned three to five new, uplifting songs. No previous singing experience is needed – just a willingness to join in and share the simple pleasure of raising our voices together!

title: SOD SCRAPER | Exhibition & Talks at NCAD Gallery
description:
SOD SCRAPER is an exhibition and talk series by artists Jack Galligan, Jennifer O’Brien, and Nicholas Sidarchuk, presented as part of the NCAD Gallery Student Open Call 2025 for Culture Night Dublin 2025.

Collectively, SOD SCRAPER examines the shifting relationship between Ireland’s landscape, its histories, and the hidden architectures of the global data economy. The exhibition explores the intersections of personal narrative, contested land, industrial expansion, and the cultural re-framing of digital infrastructure.

Jack Galligan’s performance work situates the body as both an operator and a spectacle within the flows of data. From a sculptural bench, echoing the stark repetition of data centre architecture, Galligan uses a mobile phone to stream live to a facing screen, transforming the act of sitting into a public stage.

Jennifer O’Brien’s Grazing Licence grounds the global in the local. Her research traces the story of Mannix Coyne’s appeal against the development of a 24.5-acre data centre in Clonee, Co. Meath, on land he had rented to graze horses.

In his works’, Nicholas Sidarchuk repositions the data centre as a tourist attraction, revealing its strange kinship with ancient monuments.

Together, the exhibition articulates a layered portrait of a country where global capital reshapes ancient ground, where personal histories collide with corporate expansion, and where the monumental can be both stone circle and server farm. SOD SCRAPER asks, who owns the infrastructure, the field, the view, and what is the cost of our connection?

title: Sound the Bells in Taney
description:
The Taney Bell Ringers are a group in Dundrum, Dublin that practice the traditional art of full-circle change ringing. This is a method of ringing where bells are rung by hand in a series of varying sequences under the direction of a conductor. In this form of ringing, bells in the Church steeple are mounted on a headstock attached to a large wheel attached to a rope. When the ringer pulls the rope at the bottom of the tower, this turns the wheel, causing the bell to swing and then rotate in a full circle. The bell rotates from top to bottom and back again – sounding a chime at each end of the rotation. Full circle change ringing can be traced to the early 17th century. Since then, mechanical systems have replaced most teams of ringers – Taney is one of just five steeples in Dublin that are still rung by hand.

 

The bell tower at Taney houses a set of bells from St George’s Church on Hardwicke Street. These bells were first commissioned by architect Francis Johnston for his own use in a full-size steeple he built at the end of his garden. His neighbours persuaded him to donate the bells to a church, so they were moved to St. George’s in 1828. After St George’s was deconsecrated in 1990, these bells were rescued and stored until their installation at Taney in 2000. For Culture Night, we will host three open ringing sessions – at 6pm, 7pm and 8pm – where visitors can listen to a team ring, then try sounding a bell themselves.

title: St. Peter’s Church: Beneath Our Feet
description:
In the winter of 2021-22 a team of archaeologists, under the direction of Avril Purcell, Lane Purcell  Archaeology  excavated a large site, 92-96 North Main Street, in the heart of Cork city, in advance of a development for student accommodation. The site extended downwards to a depth of approximately three metres below street level and a total of twelve identifiable buildings from the medieval period, including stake-built, post and wattle and sill-beam timber houses were recorded.

The site is a valuable window on the lives of medieval Cork people, offering evidence of everyday life and activities from the 12th to the 14th centuries and beyond.

In 2024, Cork City Council Archaeologist Ciara Brett and the artist and archaeologist John Sunderland received Creative Ireland Funding to undertake a project which would interpret the archaeology at the site at North Main Street through visual arts. 

The aim of the exhibition is to bring the information gained from the excavation to the wider Cork public in an engaging and imaginative that investigate and interpret the findings of the excavation through the dual lenses of archaeology and art. 

The exhibition will run from the 20th September until the 4th October. It will include an expansive installation of painted boards by Sarah Baume, artist and writer, in the rough form of an altarpiece creating an ‘iconography’ medieval Cork; sculptural pieces by the UK-based glass artist, Matt Durran, photographs of artefacts from North Main Street, pressed flora, a sensitively assembled installation of bracken and bone, recordings of oral histories by some of the specialists involved with the excavation, and a programme of talks. 

The exhibition will preview on Culture Night in St. Peter’s. The present St. Peters’, was built on the site of a medieval church and is located just a few doors down from the excavation site , and so it was likely the place where the inhabitants of the  wooden houses uncovered went to worship.

title: Stellar Choir Choral Performance
description:
Stellar! is a vibrant mixed-voice choir (soprano, alto, tenor and bass) based in Rathmines, Dublin 6. Founded in January 2018 by Aoife O’Gorman, the choir began as a way of bringing together parents from Kildare Place School. Since then, it has grown into a lively community ensemble of 52 singers, welcoming members from across the wider area. Under the expert direction of musical director Thomas Kehoe, Stellar! has developed a distinctive voice and an eclectic repertoire that spans contemporary music, jazz standards, and beloved works from the classical tradition.

The choir has enjoyed many memorable performances, from concerts at City Hall to Culture Night appearances at The Amphitheatre. They were awarded second place in the Chamber Choir category at the AIMS Choral Festival in 2019, and more recently received high commendation at the Cork Choral Festival (2024). A career highlight came in June 2025, when Stellar! travelled to New York to perform Mozart’s Vesperae de Confessore K. 339 at the world-famous Carnegie Hall, sharing the stage with choirs from across the United States.

For Culture Night 2025, Stellar! will perform a selection of favourites, including Geantrai, Space Oddity, O Love, I Got Rhythm and Va Pensiero, promising an evening of uplifting choral music.

title: Step back in time in The Liberties – Iveagh Trust Tour
description:
Stepping onto Bull Alley Street for a tour of the Iveagh Trust building is like time-traveling to an era when social housing was, surprisingly, a grand philanthropic gesture! Imagine red-brick facades rising proudly, hinting at the forward-thinking vision of Edward Cecil Guinness, who dreamt of better homes for Dublin’s working class. As you wander through the carefully preserved rooms, you can almost hear the echoes of families bustling about, the clatter of pots on the old range, and perhaps even the lively tunes from a piano in a cosy living room. It’s a delightful peek into a crucial chapter of Dublin’s history, showcasing not just architecture, but the very heart and soul of a community built with purpose and a surprising touch of elegance.

18:00 – 18:30

18:30 – 19:00

19:00 – 19:30

19:30 – 20:00

title: SWAMP – A Dance Performance by Annekatrin Kiesel
description:
SWAMP, a solo dance performance by Annekatrin Kiesel, explores swamp landscapes as a metaphor for and place of memories. With its immersive, at times meditative atmosphere, SWAMP invites the audience into an inner landscape where repression, flashbacks and disorientation mark a difficult yet healing journey of “working through” memories – much like crossing a swamp. In a time marked by personal and collective trauma, the performance opens a space for relating to memory and nature without claiming control over either.

Annekatrin Kiesel is an accomplished contemporary dance artist who relocated from Berlin to Ireland in late 2024. Anne studied in Cologne and Antwerp and holds a master’s degree in Dance Studies. For over 15 years, she has worked as a dancer and choreographer across a broad spectrum of projects in contemporary dance, dance theatre, music theatre and performance. Since moving to Ireland, she has focused on developing her choreographic voice and shares her passion for dance through teaching and community engagement.

Supported by / This project was made possible with the support of
Moving Earth Festival – Eco Dance Day at Interface Inagh, Creative Space Residency at Shawbrook Residential and Percolate Residency at Dance Limerick.

description:
This tour will explore the streets and stories of 18th-century Dublin through the life and legacy of the founder of St Patrick’s University Hospital, celebrated satirist and author of Gulliver’s Travels, Jonathan Swift.

Led by the Archivist at St Patrick’s Mental Health Services, you’ll learn about Swift’s deep connections to the city—from his time as Dean of St Patrick’s Cathedral to his advocacy for the poor, and his lasting impact on Irish literature and society. The tour will conclude with light refreshments at St Patrick’s University Hospital, founded by Swift in 1746. Now known as St Patrick’s Mental Health Services, the organisation is driven by the same vision, energy, and determination first demonstrated by Dean Swift, who, on his death in 1745, bequeathed £12,000 to establish not only the first psychiatric hospital in Ireland, but one of the very first in the world.

Come along on Culture Night to walk in Swift’s footsteps and discover the city through his eyes.

This one-hour walking tour will meet near Dublin Castle and will conclude with light refreshments at St Patrick’s University Hospital.  The exact meeting location will be communicated following registration for tickets.

Booking for this event will go live with the full Dublin City programme launch at 10am on 19 August.

title: Talk and Exhibition – ‘The Knockcroghery Pioneer Pipe Band’
description:
Mary Dwyer (Knockcroghery Village Tapestry) will host a fascinating talk on the history of the Knockcroghery Pioneer Pipe Band 1930s – 1950s along with an exhibition of old instruments.

In the mid 1930’s two young teenagers  George Scally and Joe Gordon decided to start a pipe band. The Knockcroghery Pioneer Pipe Band’ was formed and its first official outing was a parade after St. Patrick’s Day mass on March 17th 1938.

Over two decades the band played at carnivals, sports days, religious and military events,  and famously led the victorious Roscommon All- Ireland winning football teams of 1943 and ‘44 through the county town. On Culture night we will remember the pipe band and their important cultural legacy. It is hoped that anyone with memories of seeing the band or of hearing stories from their parents, will share them on the night and the walls of Culleen Hall will once again hear of the Knockcroghery Pioneer Pipe Band.

Nuala O’Connor lives in Co. Galway, Ireland. Her poetry and fiction have been widely published, anthologised, and won many literary awards. Her sixth novel Seaborne, about Irish-born pirate Anne Bonny, is nominated for the Dublin Literary Award and was shortlisted for Eason Novel of the Year at the 2024 An Post Irish Book Awards. Her novel NORA (New Island), about Nora Barnacle and James Joyce, was a Top 10 historical novel in the New York Times. She won Irish Short Story of the Year at the 2022 An Post Irish Book Awards. Her fifth poetry collection, Menagerie, is published by Arlen House in March 2025. www.nualaoconnor.com

Breda Burns lives in Westport. Seeing, understanding, speaking, engaging, challenging, playing, destroying, reconstructing, standing back, letting go and starting over are all part of the artistic endeavour. Both as a solitary and collaborative process, the artist stands in these rapidly changing times, inside and outside the tribe, both states mirroring each other.
www.bredaburns.com

The mission of Tertulia is to make a positive contribution to the way the world thinks.
Tertulia, a magical place for book lovers, Harry Potter fans is a place to relax, enjoy a coffee, a place to meet, a place to chat. We value community and all our stories matter.

title: The Bard Of Cloghbrack
description: Martin O Halloran will read from his latest book The Bard of Cloghbrack; Micheal Luke Pháidín. Michael Coyne, the poet, was born, in Cloghbrack Upper in 1882, son of Luke Coyne and Sarah ‘Sally’ Diskin. He went to school to third class in an English only school as Ireland was still under British rule. He took the emigrant ship to Scranton, Pennsylvania to work in the depths of the coal mines there. He returned hoping for some support to progress his learning and scholarship but when it wasn’t forthcoming he left again this time for Pittsburgh, mining coal in the bowels of the earth. Michael never returned to Ireland. Before he emigrated, while still a young man he composed more than 20 poems on the themes of love, loss, emigration, the social life of Cloghbrack and the Irish language. It is believed he composed more poems in Pittsburgh but none are known to survive. He died in September 1916 and was buried in Calvary cemetery in an indigent plot. It is illustrated with images of manuscript pages from the handwritten notes of Professor Tomás Ó Máille and copies of transcriptions from the Dúchas, National Folklore Collection.

title: The Blind Fiddle Master’s Concert
description:
The Blind Fiddle Master’s Concert is the highlight of the culture night celebrations in Longford this year. Headlined by Kíla, the event will involve musicians and artists from diverse musical and visual art backgrounds including the Yershova Sisters – a classically trained quintet from Kerry and Longford’s premiere Ceili band – Banna Céilí Béal Átha na Muc. Headlining the concert are the internationally renowned Irish folk group – kila. Along with playing their own music, the performing musicians will honour the Blind Fiddler Kernan’s legacy by performing his tunes – many of which have not been performed in many decades.

This concert represents a significant milestone in honouring the Fiddler Kernan legacy. Thomas Kernan from Drumlish was a celebrated Fiddler player and teacher in the 19th century. He recorded several hundred tunes to paper that he had composed or picked up from a life in music. He influenced a style of playing in the Longford-South Leitrim region that still exists today.

In tandem with the live music concert, three visual artists Mary Fleming, Sergii Khazdava and Anna Wiercioch have also been commissioned to create a digital projection mapping and art piece for the concert site. The Blind Fiddler Concert will provide the finale for a series of broader Culture Night events that will occur in Longford Town and the surrounding county including several art exhibitions, childrens art workshops, and performances.

This event was funded as part of the Arts Council’s Culture Night Late series and supported by Longford County Council’s Arts, Tourism and Night Time Economy Departments.

title: The Dirty Painter Exhibition
description:
The Dirty Painter was born out of a personal need to be both creative and sustainable; I wanted to make my life as low impact as possible but still make art I love. I paint only with mud that I collect myself and water, and I use natural materials including paper, card and linen to paint on.

I began using mud as my paint to reduce all the chemicals, toxins, heavy metals and VOCs found in traditional paints, and soon fell in love with the possibilities. The linen I source locally, and I love the connection to Belfast but it is also a lower impact alternative to cotton canvas, which is much more energy and water intensive in its production.

My work is a huge passion project for me, and the aim of my exhibition would be to educate and inspire people to look differently at how we do things, and what is expected as “the norm” within art but also in our daily lives. It is so vital for me to demonstrate that there are alternatives out there if we look a bit outside the box, or in my case, paint tins. Nature, animals and wildlife are a huge inspiration for my work, and I hope to engage viewers in conversations around environmental protection, as well as admiration for our surroundings.

title: The LAB: Mother Storm by Shifting Stages
description:
Shifting Stages presents Mother Storm, an evocative evening of theatre exploring the complex, powerful experience of motherhood. The show features a series of original pieces performed at Dublin City Council’s Arts Office, Studio 3, The Lab on Foley Street.

Shifting Stages is a newly founded collective of mothers and theatre makers dedicated to supporting each other’s practices while managing the demands of mothering through all the stages. The collective evolved from ‘Waking the Feminists’ where mother activists questioned the role of mothers in Theatre in Ireland in November 2015.  Following this movement, Mother Artist Makers (MAM) was formed as an Artist Collective of mothers in Irish theatre who advocate for career support for creative practitioners with caring responsibilities and to promote family friendly arts practice.

 Mother Storm offers an intimate, honest, and often raw look at the perfect storm of emotions, challenges, and triumphs that define motherhood, making it a must-see for anyone interested in contemporary theatre and real-life stories.

title: The Last Witch Bridget Cleary, Kinsale
description: In 1895, Bridget Cleary was murdered by her husband, who claimed she had been taken by the fairies and replaced by a changeling. The story of her death captured international attention and became one of the most disturbing and enigmatic cases in Irish history. “The Last Witch Bridget Cleary” is a dramatic retelling of this true event—deeply rooted in Irish folklore, superstition, and rural tradition. At its heart is a clash between the old world and the new, between emerging modern female agency and a community still bound by fear of the fairies. Bridget’s story is a lens through which we examine the enduring power of myth in Irish life—the belief in the sí, the changeling legend, and the blurred lines between folklore and fact. Presented as part of Culture Night 2025, this work honours Ireland’s rich oral heritage and shines a light on the role folklore has played in shaping identity, behaviour, and society. It invites us to remember not only Bridget Cleary’s tragic fate, but the cultural forces that surrounded her—a world where ancient beliefs coexisted with modern Ireland’s dawning progress. Through story, performance, and reflection, The Last Witch brings Bridget’s voice back from the shadows—and reminds us of the potent, sometimes dangerous, power of the stories we choose to believe. There will be two performances in total. First performance from 1-2pm and the second from 8-9pm.

The Linenhall is thrilled to invite the people of Castlebar to (re)discover the magic of opera and the extraordinary global success of this local performer with the support of Culture Night Late.

Castlebar will come alive on Friday 19th September 2025 with The Margaret Burke Sheridan Trail – a vibrant evening of music, storytelling, exhibitions, and live performances celebrating Castlebar’s very own international opera star, Margaret Burke Sheridan.

Margaret Burke Sheridan (1889–1958), affectionately known as “La Sheridan”, was one of Ireland’s first great international opera stars and a world renowned interpreter of Puccini. Born in Castlebar, she studied at the Royal Academy of Music in London before making her operatic debut in Italy, where she became celebrated for her powerful interpretations of Puccini’s heroines. Her performances at La Scala and other renowned opera houses won her worldwide acclaim, making her one of the most remarkable Irish sopranos of the 20th century.

Events will take place across multiple town centre venues and in unexpected spaces, animating Castlebar in a unique celebration of music, creativity, and identity. From intimate opera recitals to traditional sessions, from talks and readings to multimedia projections, the Trail promises to surprise and delight audiences of all ages.

“We are delighted that with the support of Culture Night Late, we can bring these events to the very heart of our town,” said Fiona Neary, Co-Director of The Linenhall. “People can dip in and out, spend time at one event and move on, or decide to stay a while longer at a recital or performance. It’s an open invitation for the community to come together in celebration.”

All events are free of charge and no booking is required. Seating is on a first-come, first-served basis.

title: The Market Yard presents: Community Trad, Film Screening and Rakish in Concert
description:
6pm to 7pm – Community Trad Session

Carrick Trad and Drumsna Comhaltas come together to provide a fantastic mix of young and not so young traditional Irish musicians revelling in the joy of music as a shared language. Over the years to this group has expanded its influence, spreading the beauty of traditional music and song far and wide.

7.15pm to 7.45pm – Film Screening – The Call of the Shannon

The Call of the Shannon is a collection of four short stories from ordinary people about their lived experience of the river. From a fisherman, Colin Wike, who travelled from England to fish in its waters, to Colin Becker, a waterways expert and current owner of the Chang Sha, a boat built in 1846.

His story is followed by Mary and Jeanette Dunne, who share their childhood memories of the Shannon, the Chang Sha, and their beloved parents. The film finishes with an account of two young boys, Damien Masterson and Fred Óg Holt, captured in a Dollard Tru-Colour postcard in the 1960s, and how the Shannon influenced the life of one of the boys in particular.

This work highlights the importance of photography and film in documenting domestic culture and the everyday in a social, political, and historical context. From the 1950s to the 1970s, Atty Dunne documented life in Carrick-on-Shannon, both on and off the river, long before it was common practice. Her archival material is a treasure trove, capturing a different way of life, transporting us like time machines to the past.

8pm to 9.30pm – Rakish in Concert

The Fantastic Rakish. Following huge demand, this local band is back after bringing their toe-tapping music to delighted audiences in Ireland and across the world. Rakish thrill their audiences, performing haunting Irish melodies, classic country to foot stomping folk Rock. An event not to be missed in this new and exciting venue.

title: The Moon Goes Round and Round
description:
A curated night of events to celebrate WB Yeats’ love of the moon – in a diverse and fun way – for all ages.

This is an inclusive programme, celebrating contemporary culture, including a wide variety of artistes and rooted in the wider works of WB Yeats and his time in history, allowing us to animate this cultural institution in an engaging and entertaining way.

From 4–6pm, children can join the Black Minnaloushe Drawing Workshops with artist Rebecca Massey, exploring the moon’s phases and creating personalised ink drawings of Yeats’ famous cat beneath the full moon (with a copy of The Cat & the Moon to take home).

At 5–6pm and 8–9pm, enjoy a rehearsed reading of Lady Gregory’s powerful 1907 one-act play The Rising of the Moon, first staged at the Abbey Theatre, delving into Irish nationalism and identity.

6–7pm, local drama students bring moon-themed poetry to the streets of Sligo, sharing short recitals and handing out printed verses.

From 6–8pm, watch Georges Méliès’ groundbreaking 1902 short film Le Voyage de la Lune (with commentary from his granddaughter), a classic of early cinema.

The night ends with Night Moon Music (9–10pm) – a live, moon-inspired set by local producers Magnata in the Oak Moon Café, where moon-themed treats and drinks are served throughout the evening.

This programme is curated by Susan O’Keeffe, Director, Yeats Society Sligo.
