title: The OtherSide
description:
The OtherSide, a late-night TV talk show style event in front of a live audience, comes to Siamsa Tíre for the first time for Culture Night 2025.

Running since 2017 at various venues around Tralee & Listowel, The OtherSide features conversations with a wide range of guests from musicians, actors and stand-up comedians to political figures, sports people and local legends. The OtherSide offers a rare opportunity to hear these guests in conversation in an intimate setting and without an agenda. It’s conversation done differently. Kicking off at 8pm sharp, this show is free to attend as part of Culture Night celebrations in Kerry. Due to demand, tickets must be booked in advance through Siamsa Tíre.

The OtherSide Guests:

David Keenan –  A captivating Irish musician offering up inspired songs like medicinal anthems for those looking to be uplifted. David will be in conversation on the night, as well as previewing some tunes from his eagerly awaited new album.

Louise Ní Mhuircheartaigh –  One of Kerry’s most celebrated Gaelic footballers. A native of Corca Dhuibhne in west Kerry, she made her senior debut for Kerry in 2008 at just 16 years old. Over an incredible 17 career inter-county career, she earned five All-Star awards, Players Player of the Year award (2023), multiple league and Munster titles, as well as a famous All Ireland win in her final year as a Kerry player in 2024. Louise is regarded as a role model for young players and a huge ambassador for women’s sport in Ireland.

Jonno Brien  – is a Kerry based DJ/ producer and promoter. He started out DJing in the mid 90’s playing house and techno, before going on to appear at some of the biggest UK super clubs. He held a long running residency at the legendary Horan’s club in Tralee, alongside bringing some huge international DJs to the town during the 00’s. Jonno’s production work continues to be in demand, and he runs regular club nights and events around Tralee, under the Salti Beats banner.

Ellie Horgan – is a Tralee comedian rising up through the Irish comedy ranks with her tongue in cheek naughty humour. Her physical comedy is bold and is for the girlos!! Be ready for some belly aching comedy.

Make sure to join us for conversation done differently, at Siamsa Tíre this Culture Night!

title: The Rising of the Moon
description:
South Roscommon Singers Circle will bring to life some of the 300-plus compositions by Fenian poet, orator and activist, John Keegan Casey (1846 – 1870). Casey, or ‘Leo’ as he was known in the pages of the Nation Newspaper, is best remembered in this region for his numerous poems, ballads & stories about his beloved Lough Ree, the Black Islands and its people.

For a few short years in the mid 19th century his voice was ‘the voice of Ireland’– a rallying force for his country. Around his songs, stories, poems and ballads a people living on the edge of despair found new cause for hope and new impetus to struggle on.

In the 20th /21st century his songs and ballads have been recorded by scores of artists, including: John McCormack, Joseph Loche, The McNulty Family, The Clancy Bros., The Dubliners, Shane MacGowan & The Pogues, Josie McDermott, Ron Kavanagh and Thomas McCarthy. The best known of his compositions include: The Rising of the Moon, Donal Kenny, Costello’s Lament (Úna Bhán), Kathleen Machree and Boating on Lough Ree, – the list goes on.

Learn more about the life and times, the songs and the stories of John Keegan Casey on Culture Night ’25 in Knockcroghery.

title: The Sound of Appalachia in the Liberties
description:
The Dublin Sacred Harp Singers bring the sound of traditional American country-gospel singing to The Liberties this Culture Night. 

Familiar from the soundtrack of films such as ‘Cold Mountain’ or ‘Lawless’, this is a truly original American music form. This four-part a cappella music dates from the 16th through the 20th centuries, and is characterised by haunting harmonies, traditional modes, raucous songs, serene hymns, fast fugues, and high-energy anthems. The notation is written in shapes that correspond to degrees of the scale, making it easy to sight-sing. This tradition is democratic and egalitarian. 

Come along and join Sacred Harp Singers of Dublin as they glory in the powerful and joyful experience of singing their hearts out together. All voices are welcome, newcomers and beginners are always welcome.

title: The Spanish Harp: Beyond Classical with Pilar Paradela
description:
The Instituto Cervantes Dublin invites audiences to a bold and unexpected musical journey with Spanish harpist, singer and composer Pilar Paradela. 

Classically trained but creatively untamed, Paradela breaks the mould of the harp as a purely classical instrument. Her performance blends original compositions with surprising reworkings of iconic Spanish songs, moving effortlessly through flamenco, rumba, jazz and beyond. With each string and each note, Paradela reveals the harp’s full expressive potential—raw, rhythmic, emotional and free. This is not just a concert; it’s a reimagining of what the harp can be, and an invitation to feel music without borders.

 

This event is part of the European Culture Trail – a EUNIC Ireland (European Union National Institutes for Culture) in cooperation with the European Commission Representation in Ireland.

title: The Story of William Clifford Smith
description:
Celebrating the Legacy of Architect William Clifford Smith at Number 44 O’Connell Street
This Culture Night, explore the legacy of architect William Clifford Smith, fondly known as “Cliffy”, at Number 44 O’Connell Street, one of Limerick’s treasured Georgian buildings.
Previously shown at Shannon Rowing Club during Open House Limerick, this exhibition now finds a fitting home in Number 44, once the site of Stewart’s Chemist. Founded in 1884 by Joseph Stewart, the family-run pharmacy operated for over 80 years. In 1911, Stewart hired the Smith to redesign the shopfront in an Arts & Crafts style.
Born in Poole, Dorset in 1882, Smith rose to prominence after winning an international competition in 1902 to design the new Shannon Rowing Club. One requirement: move to Limerick to oversee construction, a move that spurred a celebrated Arts & Crafts architectural career in Ireland.
His signature can still be seen across the city, from in Number 45 O’Connell Street, the Belltable Arts Centre, and other iconic buildings.
Join us on Culture Night 2025 to walk through the history of Number 44 and celebrate the man who helped shape Limerick’s architectural identity. Discover the stories etched into the walls of this remarkable building and the legacy of William Clifford Smith.
fullAddress: 44 O'Connell Street, Prior's-Land, Limerick, Ireland

title: THE UNDERTAKING – PREMIERE SCREENING
description:
He Asked, They Came.
The Undertaking is a poignant short documentary produced by Creative Productions and directed by Georgina Brennan Stynes. It tells the story of Rory Healy, a third-generation undertaker in Carlow, and his quiet role in a moment that deeply moved an entire community. When Mary Regan passed away with no known next of kin, Rory made a gentle appeal on social media for people to attend her funeral—and the people of Carlow responded with warmth and solidarity. Filmed on location in Carlow, the documentary explores themes of dignity, remembrance, and the power of collective kindness. It is a tribute to the unseen work of funeral directors and the compassion that lies at the heart of Carlow town. After the screening, attendees will have the opportunity to honour a past loved one on our Remembrance Wall, followed by a short Q&A session—chaired by Marc Grogan—offering a unique behind-the-scenes look at the making of the film. Join us for the premiere at IMC Cinema, Carlow, and experience this heartfelt story on the big screen.

title: The Workers’ Skyscraper – Liberty Hall at 60
description:
This Culture Night, step inside one of Dublin’s most recognisable landmarks as Liberty Hall marks its 60th anniversary with a special evening of reflection and celebration.

Originally built as the headquarters of the Irish Transport and General Workers’ Union (now SIPTU) the striking modernist tower was constructed between 1961 and 1965. At 59.4 metres (195 feet), it held the title of Ireland’s tallest building for a time and has since become an enduring symbol of Dublin’s labour movement, architectural innovation, and cultural identity.

To honour this milestone, SIPTU will host an exclusive Culture Night event in Liberty Hall Theatre, celebrating the building’s architectural, historical, and cultural legacy. Visitors will be invited to explore the story of how Liberty Hall rose to prominence on the city’s skyline and why, six decades on, it remains a powerful emblem of progress and solidarity in Ireland’s capital.

title: Things We Carry: Expressions of Black-Irish Identity at Riverbank Arts Centre
description:
An evening of spoken word performances and conversations featuring artists chaired by presenter, writer, creative producer and Gaeilgeoir Ola Majekodunmi with Fiyin Oloukun (mixed-media visual artist & spoken word artist), Samuel Yakura (poet, playwright & performer) and Tanzanian artist and filmmaker Sekera Mohamed Besta (Ngôma Hoe).

 

Samuel Yakura is a Nigerian-Irish Multi-disciplinary Artist. A Poet, Playwright and Performer who explores themes of home, identity, and cross-cultural inquiry through storytelling. His work centers voices often pushed to the margins, creating multidimensional characters that challenge stereotypes. He is the co-founder of Talkatives, a Dublin-based poetry slam, and is currently developing his new project SOAK. Whether on stage or the page, he is passionate about exploring narratives that lie beneath complex truths.

 

BIOGRAPHIES

Ola Majekodunmi was born in Lagos, Nigeria and raised in Dublin, Ireland. She is a broadcaster, writer, Gaeilgeoir, creative producer and workshop facilitator. She’s produced and spoken/performed at literary events with the likes of San Patrizio Livorno Festival, IASIL Conference, Dublin International Literature Festival, Cúirt International Festival of Literature, West Cork Literary Festival and Irish Writers Centre. Majekodunmi has performed her poems at home in Ireland and internationally in Italy and Egypt. Her poetry and prose work have been published in Cnámh & Smior, including poetry journals, magazines and zines such as COMHAR, Storms, Airmid and Blue Bodies. Majekodunmi writes primarily in Irish, English and Yoruba. She has also released poetry films with NÓS Magazine and Axis Ballymun, Dublin.

Sekera Mohamed Besta (Ngôma Hoe) is a Tanzanian artist and filmmaker whose work explores narratives of Black African identity. Her work is research based, and re-tells from personal experiences, portraying black Africanism realistically. She gives subjects that are overlooked, a chance to be seen.

Fiyin Oluokun is a mixed media visual artist whose work explores identities and how environments shape and morph these identities. The subject of their work is pulled out of small encounters, gestures and interactions – a nose bleed, stepping on a shoe, a head nod at a stranger. Fiyin’s background in architecture allows them to translate these simultaneously personal and wholly universal moments into visual works that are both spatial and experiential.

title: Think About It: Sharing Ideas for a Better World
description:

The IIEA is Ireland’s foremost international affairs think tank, functioning as a laboratory of ideas where policymakers, researchers and the public can meet and exchange opinions. On Culture Night, guests will be welcomed to the IIEA’s Georgian townhouse for a wine reception. A curated exhibition will showcase ideas and art that have been historically suppressed, illustrating the journey from censorship to freedom of expression. From 6.00p.m. until 7.00p.m., guests will be invited to a fireside chat amongst authors, journalists and policymakers, hosted by Alex White, Director-General of the IIEA, to discuss how the open exchange of ideas has helped shape Ireland’s place in the world, and why freedom of thought cannot be taken for granted.

Traditional Music
Blessington native Rachel Conlon is widely recognised as one of Ireland’s finest traditional fiddle players. Now based in Co. Clare, Rachel is a dedicated teacher and performer, sharing her music across Ireland.

Special Guest
Joining us from Orsa, Sweden, Margaretha Mattsson is a master fiddle player steeped in the Swedish folk tradition. A lifelong teacher and performer, she has toured internationally and has become highly accomplished in Irish traditional music. title: Tramore Valley Park EcoLab: Eco-Poetry Reading
description:
On Culture Night, Tramore Valley Park’s EcoLab will come alive with words that celebrate, challenge, and reimagine our relationship with the natural world. This special eco-poetry reading features four acclaimed voices—Jenny Mitchell, Leah Sohotra, Sheila Mannix, and Brendan Duffin—whose work bridges the personal and the planetary.

From lyrical meditations to experimental explorations, these poets engage with themes of biodiversity, climate change, memory, and renewal. Their readings invite audiences to consider how language can help us reconnect with the earth—and with each other—in a time of ecological urgency.

The event is presented as part of The KinShip Project, a socially engaged art initiative that fosters a deeper sense of connection between people and the ecology of Tramore Valley Park. Once a landfill and now a thriving public green space, the park embodies transformation and resilience, making the EcoLab the perfect venue for this exchange between poetry and place.

title: Trinity Orchestra presents Culture Night
description:
It is with great excitement and pleasure that Trinity Orchestra welcome visitors back for a special programme of classical and traditional music for Culture Night.

In collaboration with the DU Music society, earlier this year Trinity Orchestra threw an event raising money for the Palestinian Red Crescent charity to create awareness of the genocide in Palestine. Taking inspiration from the awareness Irish trad group Lankum, members of the orchestra arranged and  performed renditions of many of Lankum’s most popular pieces such as ‘Go Dig My Grave’ and ‘Bear Creek’. For Culture Night, they look forward to presenting some of these pieces again, and to pay respect to traditional music, which is at the heart of meaning and understanding of culture on the island of Ireland.

Trinity Orchestra will also perform pieces, sonatas, studies and familiar favourites from the integral genre of classical music, a genre in which the orchestra thrives and revolves around, with two classical concerts taking place across the academic year annually.

Visitors will first be introduced to the rich history of this iconic university, walking in the footsteps of Ireland’s greatest literary minds—from Oscar Wilde and Samuel Beckett to Sally Rooney—and learning about the college’s profound impact on Irish culture and literature.

Tales of Traveller Faith and Beliefs – Storytelling Event

11pm at CTWN Offices, 2nd Floor, Triskel

Irish Travellers are an indigenous ethnic group with a unique culture and heritage. Come to this storytelling morning with Paddy Doyle, celebrating the importance of faith, religion, holy wells, and traditional cures in Traveller life. Organised by Cork Traveller Women’s Network and Storyteller Paddy Doyle. Supported by Cork City Council Arts Office.

No booking required. Limited capacity of 10 people. This venue is not wheelchair accessible.

6.00pm to 8.00pm at CTWN Offices, 2nd Floor, Triskel

‘Creating Connections, Traveller Lives’ is a 12-minute immersive Virtual Reality experience exploring Traveller traditions. Produced by Linda Curtin with Cork Traveller Women’s Network. Commissioned by the Traveller Accommodation Unit, Cork City Council, and funded by Dormant Accounts.

Limited capacity. Viewing is in half-hour slots on a first-come, first-served basis. Suitable for ages 12+. Viewed through a VR headset in a swivel chair. Not recommended for people with photosensitive conditions or vertigo.

title: Under the ambient
description:
Under the Ambient is a film about the changing underwater world off the west of Ireland across a full year. It shows how the water changes from autumn through summer with autumn’s restless but milder waves shifting into winter’s stronger, stormier seas that stir up sediment and seaweed, making the water murkier. Spring and early summer bring plankton blooms and clearer water, and summer’s warmer, calmer seas reveal underwater life growing and moving more slowly.
The live music by Simon O’Reilly, harpist Aishling Lyons and Myles O’Reilly, creates an ambient soundscape that reacts to the images in real time. The visuals themselves shift subtly during the performance, introducing gentle variations that reflect the unpredictable nature of the sea environment.
Presented as a live audiovisual installation, the work shows the natural flow of the underwater world. From busy and churning seas to calm clear waters using live music and shifting visuals that respond to each other in real time.
João Tudella – Film/visual artist: 
Filmmaker and visual artist from Lisbon, now based in West Clare, Ireland. With a background in environmental and resource management, João started by filming surf culture before shifting to quiet, observational work focused on rural and coastal life. His practice emphasizes collaboration with artists and communities, capturing stories and environments as they naturally unfold, often blending film with live audiovisual performance.
Simon O’Reillyis a composer, producer, multi-instrumentalist, songwriter, visual artist and cofounder of Hedge School festival His is based near the cliffs of Moher where he has his recording studio. He has worked with many musicians including Rufus Nightjar, Manchán Magan, The Monks Of Glenstal, Mick Flannery & Susan O’Neill, Myles O’Reilly, The ConTempo Quartet, Steve Wall, and many more.
Myles O’Reilly is a Dublin-born Irish musician, composer, and filmmaker renowned for his
significant contributions to Ireland’s music and arts scene.

Visitors will also hear music and talks from Trinity staff and local residents who have taken part in Unit18’s Dublin Diaries, a storytelling initiative capturing memories of life in Dublin over the decades.

The evening begins at 16:00 with a chance to browse the Creative Pathways and Dublin Diaries exhibitions over tea and biscuits. At 17:00, Creative Pathways poets and contributors take the stage, followed at 18:00 by a celebration of legendary Irish tenor John McCormack with musician Michael McLaughlin. More performances from the poets will follow at 19:00, with the event concluding at 20:00.

Presented in collaboration with We Act — a campaign honouring the charity and community sector — this event invites audiences to connect with powerful stories, rich history, and vibrant creativity from the heart of Dublin.

Booking is encourages but walk-ins are also welcome. This event aims to be family friendly but may explore difficult themes of poverty and exclusion. For more information contact unit18@tcd.ie or tara@atdireland.ie.

title: Where Silence Settles – Cobh, Spike Island
description:
Where Silence Settles is the result of Barbara Diener’s residency at Spike Island, presented in the atmospheric Punishment Block as part of Culture Night this September. This exhibition continues a five-year partnership between Spike Island and Sample-Studios, supporting site-responsive work that engages with the island’s layered history. Diener brings a contemplative lens to Spike Island’s complex legacy.

Her practice explores memory, time and obsolescence—qualities echoed in the island’s crumbling walls and overlooked narratives. Working with archival materials, installations and still and moving images, she constructs a visual narrative that traces what remains after silence has settled. The exhibition draws from pivotal moments in the island’s past, including the story of The Aud and its connection to the Easter Rising. Diener’s haunting underwater video work and photographs of abandoned, overgrown architecture—often in areas not usually accessible to the public—reflect how nature slowly reclaims places marked by human ambition and conflict, offering a quiet meditation on loss, transformation and renewal.

A short guided tour of the fort will take place at the beginning of the event. Visitors are then invited to join an exhibition tour and an artist talk to learn more about the work on display and the creative process behind it. The residency and exhibition were facilitated by Spike Island curator Dorota Gubbins.

title: Whites Whiskey Session
description:
An Evening of Drams, Tales & Trad in Belfast’s Oldest Tavern

Step into the storied walls of White’s Tavern, Belfast’s oldest licensed pub, for a spirited Culture Night celebration blending rich history, fine whiskey, and traditional Irish culture.

White’s Whiskey Session kicks off with a guided whiskey tasting, featuring a carefully curated selection of local and historic Irish whiskeys. Sip and savour as experts share tasting notes and heritage stories behind each pour, connecting the flavours in your glass to Belfast’s long and proud distilling tradition.

As the tasting unfolds, you’ll be introduced to the newly released White’s Whiskey Book – a beautifully crafted homage to Irish whiskey and the legacy of White’s itself. Delve into tales of smuggling tunnels, merchant cellars, and the tavern’s evolution since 1630, all rooted in the very cobbled alley you stand on.

Next, gather close for a captivating storytelling session – unearthing some of White’s most colourful characters, from rebels and revolutionaries to poets and publicans. Learn how this tavern earned its nickname, “The Last Chance Saloon”, and what secrets echo through the vaulted ceilings of its historic cellar.

Then the mood lifts as a live traditional Irish music session takes over the room. Enjoy the timeless sound of fiddles, flutes, and bodhráns as the night comes alive in true céilí spirit.
fullAddress: Whites Tavern, Winecellar Entry, Belfast, UK

title: Wicked at Mallow Castle

This Culture Night, step into the magical setting of Mallow Castle for a spectacular outdoor screening of Wicked, the breathtaking 2024 film adaptation of the beloved Broadway musical.
About the Film
Directed by Jon M. Chu, Wicked tells the untold story of the witches of Oz before Dorothy’s arrival. The film stars Cynthia Erivo as Elphaba, the misunderstood young woman destined to become the Wicked Witch of the West, and Ariana Grande as Glinda, the effervescent Good Witch. With powerful performances, dazzling visuals, and unforgettable songs, Wicked brings to life a tale of friendship, identity, and the choices that change everything.
Already hailed as one of the most spectacular films of the year, Wicked combines stunning musical numbers with an emotionally rich story, making it a perfect experience for audiences of all ages.
What to Expect
Free Admission – arrive early to secure your spot
Bring blankets or cushions for a cosy evening under the stars
A magical atmosphere in the historic grounds of Mallow Castle
Don’t miss this chance to experience Wicked in one of Cork’s most enchanting venues – a Culture Night highlight for the whole family.
There will be a very special  dance performance before the screening  from The FrienDS Club youth club 
The frienDS club is a youth club for young persons with Down Syndrome, established in 2019. It provides a safe space for young people to develop as individuals and reach their full potential. It aims to nurture & develop friendships while enjoying a wide variety of events and challenges, both in The Big Blue Cube and also out and about and indeed further afield.
Indulging in an array of creative, active, social and fun experiences ensures the club members enjoy a wide and varied calendar of events.
Most of the club members also attend Centre Stage School in Mallow to further  positively enhance their life experiences.

title: Wild Songs at Coole: Songs From the Burren
description:
The National Parks and Wildlife Service invite you to celebrate Culture Night 2025 with an immersive, intimate concert in the magical setting of Coole Park Nature Reserve, featuring songs by Brian Patrick Nally, plucked from hollows, meadows, and cracked beauty of the Burren. No curtain. No stage. Just the bare song under the trees of Coole, when the shadows stretch long and the sun dips low. Bring a blanket. Bring a flask. Or bring nothing at all. The rest is already waiting.

Brian’s performance will weave together nature, music and place, offering a unique evening of song that celebrates the spirit of the region. Much of the work carries a quiet nod to his experience with Burrenbeo Trust, an organisation who, like the National Parks and Wildlife Service, is also engaged in the stewardship of the Burren’s remarkable natural and cultural heritage. A short guided walk through the trees to tune your ears to nature’s sounds will precede the concert and will lead you to the outdoor performance venue.

Please note that the outdoor venue will be on grass but will be accessible for wheelchairs. Should the weather decide to be uncooperative, the concert will be diverted indoors. Please also note that no dogs, except assistance dogs, are permitted at this event.

At 17:00, Wolfe Tone Square comes alive with the dynamic rhythms of Dublin Doo-Doong Samulnori. This captivating Korean percussion ensemble features four musicians performing on traditional instruments: the kkwaenggwari (small gong), jing (large gong), janggu (hourglass drum), and buk (barrel drum).

Samulnori, which originated from the vibrant rhythms of Korean rural folk music, has grown into a celebrated art form performed on stages worldwide. With its driving beats and layered textures, this performance offers Dublin audiences a rare chance to experience one of Korea’s most dynamic and iconic musical traditions.

title: Wolfe Tone Square: Sandie Purcell & Seán McElwain
description:
At 18:40, Wolfe Tone Square hosts Sandie Purcell & Seán McElwain for an evening of traditional Irish music that spans lively jigs and reels, to soulful slow airs. Sandie Purcell, a fiddle player and composer from Co. Kildare, brings the rich heritage of the instrument to life with masterful technique and a deep connection to the stories behind the music.

Featured in the Irish Traditional Music Archive’s Saothar series (2022) and as St. Brigid’s Day composer (2025), Sandie has published collections including 101 Original Compositions of Irish Traditional Music and New Songs from Old Stories (2023), alongside her album The Crooked Picture. Her online tune collection, supported by The Arts Council, features 180 original works performed by leading musicians.

Seán McElwain, from Co. Monaghan, complements this with his dynamic playing on banjo, bouzouki, and guitar. A former member of Téada and a researcher of Sliabh Beagh musical traditions, Seán’s work has contributed to the TG4 Gradam Ceoil-winning album Our Dear Dark Mountain with the Sky Over It and publications on collector James Whiteside. Together, they create a performance that is both energetic and deeply musical, inviting audiences to tap their feet, feel the rhythms, and immerse themselves in the vibrant storytelling power of Irish traditional music.

He doesn’t just recite poetry; he invites you into a world of shared experience, where every word is carefully chosen to create a lasting impact.

description:
Formed in 1994 by a group of passionate singers from South Dublin, the Ballinteer Male Voice Choir (BMVC) has been delighting audiences for over three decades. Known for their rich harmonies and warm stage presence, the choir is arranged in two tenor sections with a baritone and bass line and has a repertoire spans classical works, timeless ballads, popular hits, musical theatre favourites, hymns, and, when the season calls for it, festive carols.

Expect stirring choral arrangements, familiar melodies you can hum along to, and a few surprises from their ever-evolving setlist—performed with the passion and camaraderie that make them a cherished addition to any stage.

title: Wood Quay Amphitheatre: Farah Elle
description:
Libyan-born, Dublin-based artist Farah El Neihum—known to audiences as Farah Elle—has been composing music since the age of 10, crafting a sound that seamlessly blends her North African and Irish heritage. Her 2022 debut album FATIMA, named in tribute to her mother, was the culmination of nearly a decade of work, weaving traditional Arabic melodies into lush, contemporary arrangements that are entirely her own.

For Culture Night at Meeting House Square, Farah will deliver a special performance that celebrates multilingualism, culture clash, and the integration of identities through music. Expect hypnotic rhythms, soaring vocals, channelling generational healing with the simplicity of one voice and a piano. Imagine a blend of eastern prayer calls, nature sounds and pop ballads, together presenting an intimate and powerful set that reflects Farah Elle’s unique journey, uniting audiences across borders.

title: Wood Quay Amphitheatre: Jessica Hayes & Zach O’Brien
description:
Fresh from completing their BA (Hons) in Musical Theatre at MTU Cork School of Music, Jessica Hayes and Zach O’Brien bring their powerhouse vocals and stage presence to Culture Night 2025.

Zach’s recent credits include lead roles in Our House and 9 to 5 The Musical at Cork’s Everyman Palace Theatre, as well as featured performances in Steppin’ Out at Cork Opera House. He has appeared with Northern Ireland Opera, The Sondheim Festival (An Audience with Rachel Tucker), and in industry workshops for new musicals at The Gate Theatre and Smock Alley, Dublin.

Jessica has shone as Judy in 9 to 5 The Musical (directed by West End star Killian Donnelly), featured in The Wizard and I with Broadway legend Liz Callaway, and performed in Steppin’ Out at Cork Opera House. Her training also took her to Amsterdam’s Lucia Marthas Institute for Performing Arts through two European exchanges and she has toured the USA with the original production Find Your Way Home.

Together, Jessica and Zach promise a dynamic performance, blending musical theatre favourites with fresh interpretations, replete with smiles, tears, adversity, desperation, heroics, joy, high notes, low notes, reflections on the ups and downs of our time on the planet, and safely home again! Don’t miss this chance to see them live as they step onto the stage for Culture Night, ready to captivate audiences at Wood Quay Amphitheatre.

title: Would you like to live it, Love? –  A Day in the Life of a Traveller Woman
description: ‘Would you like to live it, Love?’  is a rehearsed reading presented by women engaged with Kildare Traveller Action and women from New Irish communities. The reading takes the audience on a journey through a day in the life of a Traveller woman in Co. Kildare. She takes us with her as she cares for her family, her home, and her community. In the course of her day, she meets a member of the New Irish community. The two women talk about the racism they face. This highlights that racism towards Travellers is more acceptable than racism towards brown and Black people. Regardless of a person’s appearance, however, racism hurts the victim the same. After all, as Bridgie (our heroine) tells us “Love is love, but hate is hate too, you know”.

title: Youghal Clock Gate Tower
description:
Step inside one of Ireland’s most fascinating heritage landmarks this Culture Night! Youghal Clock Gate Tower will open its doors for free guided tours on Friday, 19th September 2025, offering a rare opportunity to explore this iconic building after hours. Join us for a captivating 45-minute journey through time, as our passionate guides bring to life the stories, secrets, and dramatic history of this unique 18th-century tower. Once a prison, a family home, and a timekeeper for the town, the Clock Gate Tower holds centuries of memories within its walls.

Tour times: 6:00 PM   7:00 PM   8:00 PM

Spaces are limited and advance booking is essential. Each tour is suitable for ages 7+, and involves climbing several flights of stairs, so comfortable footwear is recommended. Children must be accompanied by an adult at all times.

Arrival Time: Please arrive 10 minutes before your scheduled tour. Late arrivals may not be admitted to avoid disrupting the tour experience.

Tours last approximately 55 minutes.

Book by calling 024-20769 or calling into Living Youghal Ticket Office, 85 North Main Street, Youghal.

Whether you’re a local rediscovering your town’s hidden heritage or a visitor curious about Youghal’s colourful past, this Culture Night experience promises insight, atmosphere, and a real sense of place. Celebrate Culture Night 2025 with us and see Youghal Clock Gate Tower like never before — by night, for free, and full of stories.

ZASKA’s high-energy live shows leave audiences buzzing with media describing performances as “masterful,” “incomparable,” and “joyous.”
